        },
        "input":{
          "content":"# SoraMech — Roadmap\n\n## Phase 1 — Foundation\n\nGoal: a map you can edit in the browser and execute from the terminal.\n\nAt the end of phase 1, the user can:\n- Open index.html, connect it to a running server, and see a canvas\n- Create boxes, set their ref/fn/inputs/outputs, wire them together\n- Edit branch boxes with named ports and predicates\n- Save all edits as box files on disk\n- Run `luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>` and have it execute the map\n- Write a custom language driver and have the runner use it\n\nIssues:\n  101 — project scaffold and map directory format\n  102 — language driver interface\n  103 — runner: graph loader and validator\n  104 — runner: synchronous executor (task boundary)\n  105 — HTTP server: file CRUD API\n  106 — web editor: canvas and box rendering\n  107 — web editor: wiring and connection UI\n  108 — branch box and predicate routing\n  109 — data files: persistent and ephemeral storage\n  110 — phase 1 demo\n\nDemo: a small lua FSM (3-4 boxes) runs via the CLI, exercises a branch\nbox, reads a data file, writes an output. The browser shows the same map\nvisually with correct wiring drawn.\n\n## Phase 2 — Concurrent execution\n\nGoal: boxes whose inputs are all satisfied fire concurrently.\n\n- Integrate effil-jit as the threading backend (replacing synchronous\n  depth-first walk)\n- Runner becomes an M:N task scheduler: each box invocation is a task,\n  boxes park when waiting on upstream results\n- Multiple maps running concurrently share nothing (separate processes)\n- Begin integration path toward the 3d-rts custom thread pool\n\n## Phase 3 — SoraMind integration\n\nGoal: boxes that call SoraMind inference endpoints on the Alpine cluster.\n\n- LLM call box type: sends a prompt, receives a completion string\n- Prompt assembly: text values wired from upstream boxes, data file\n  sections explicitly loaded into prompt context\n- Branch box connected to an LLM classifier: \"rogue, wizard, or else\"\n- Else port retry with pseudo-randomized temperature parameter\n- Streaming output from SoraMind inference back to the runner\n\n## Phase 4 — Map-to-map calls\n\nGoal: a box that invokes another map as a subroutine.\n\n- Map call box type: specifies another map directory, passes inputs,\n  receives outputs\n- Maps can run concurrently with each other\n- Entry/exit contracts defined in meta.json\n\n## Phase 5 — Remote runner\n\nGoal: run a map on the Alpine cluster, edit it from a laptop.\n\n- Runner process on a remote machine (Alpine node)\n- Server on the same machine exposes map files over HTTP\n- Browser editor on the laptop connects to the remote server\n- Results written to remote data files, accessible via server\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/docs/002-roadmap.md"
        }
      }],

  "toolUseResult":{
    "content":"# SoraMech — Roadmap\n\n## Phase 1 — Foundation\n\nGoal: a map you can edit in the browser and execute from the terminal.\n\nAt the end of phase 1, the user can:\n- Open index.html, connect it to a running server, and see a canvas\n- Create boxes, set their ref/fn/inputs/outputs, wire them together\n- Edit branch boxes with named ports and predicates\n- Save all edits as box files on disk\n- Run `luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>` and have it execute the map\n- Write a custom language driver and have the runner use it\n\nIssues:\n  101 — project scaffold and map directory format\n  102 — language driver interface\n  103 — runner: graph loader and validator\n  104 — runner: synchronous executor (task boundary)\n  105 — HTTP server: file CRUD API\n  106 — web editor: canvas and box rendering\n  107 — web editor: wiring and connection UI\n  108 — branch box and predicate routing\n  109 — data files: persistent and ephemeral storage\n  110 — phase 1 demo\n\nDemo: a small lua FSM (3-4 boxes) runs via the CLI, exercises a branch\nbox, reads a data file, writes an output. The browser shows the same map\nvisually with correct wiring drawn.\n\n## Phase 2 — Concurrent execution\n\nGoal: boxes whose inputs are all satisfied fire concurrently.\n\n- Integrate effil-jit as the threading backend (replacing synchronous\n  depth-first walk)\n- Runner becomes an M:N task scheduler: each box invocation is a task,\n  boxes park when waiting on upstream results\n- Multiple maps running concurrently share nothing (separate processes)\n- Begin integration path toward the 3d-rts custom thread pool\n\n## Phase 3 — SoraMind integration\n\nGoal: boxes that call SoraMind inference endpoints on the Alpine cluster.\n\n- LLM call box type: sends a prompt, receives a completion string\n- Prompt assembly: text values wired from upstream boxes, data file\n  sections explicitly loaded into prompt context\n- Branch box connected to an LLM classifier: \"rogue, wizard, or else\"\n- Else port retry with pseudo-randomized temperature parameter\n- Streaming output from SoraMind inference back to the runner\n\n## Phase 4 — Map-to-map calls\n\nGoal: a box that invokes another map as a subroutine.\n\n- Map call box type: specifies another map directory, passes inputs,\n  receives outputs\n- Maps can run concurrently with each other\n- Entry/exit contracts defined in meta.json\n\n## Phase 5 — Remote runner\n\nGoal: run a map on the Alpine cluster, edit it from a laptop.\n\n- Runner process on a remote machine (Alpine node)\n- Server on the same machine exposes map files over HTTP\n- Browser editor on the laptop connects to the remote server\n- Results written to remote data files, accessible via server\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/docs/002-roadmap.md",
    "structuredPatch":[]
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-07T22:26:24.011Z",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",

  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "name":"Write",
        "id":"toolu_011ntLFu9sfgTYhnVAGXJfLH",
        "type":"tool_use",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "content":"# SoraMech — Language Driver System\n\n## What a driver is\n\nA driver is a shell script. It knows how to invoke a function in one\nlanguage. The runner knows nothing about any language — it looks up the\nfile extension in drivers.json, finds the driver script, and calls it.\n\nLua and C ship with pre-written driver scripts. They are not special\ncases in the runner. They use exactly the same interface a user-written\ndriver uses. If you want to call a Haskell function or a Rust function,\nwrite a driver script and add the extension to drivers.json.\n\n## Driver contract\n\nThe runner invokes a driver as:\n\n  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n\nArguments are always strings. Structured values (tables, arrays) are\npassed as JSON strings and must be decoded by the driver before use.\n\nThe driver must:\n  - Exit 0 on success, non-zero on failure\n  - Print a single JSON value to stdout on success: either a JSON array\n    (for multi-output / tuple returns) or a single JSON value (for\n    single-output functions)\n  - Print an error message to stderr on failure (runner captures and logs\n    it)\n\nNothing else. No side channels. The runner reads stdout, parses JSON,\nand maps the array positions to the box's declared output port names in\ndeclaration order.\n\n## Shell script vs. binary caller\n\nTwo kinds of refs exist in a box file:\n\n  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\",  \"fn\": \"trim\"\n      → source caller. runner looks up \".lua\" in drivers.json and\n        invokes the driver with file + fn + args.\n\n  \"ref\": \"src/trim.sh\"       (no \"fn\")\n      → binary caller. runner invokes the script directly with just\n        the args. The script is its own driver. Stdout is parsed as\n        JSON as with a normal driver.\n\nBinary callers include compiled binaries too: if the ref ends in a\nbinary extension or has no extension, the runner execs it directly.\n\n## Built-in driver scripts\n\nShipped in a global drivers/ directory alongside soramech-runner.lua.\nMaps can override any driver by defining the same extension in their\nlocal drivers.json pointing at a map-local script.\n\n### drivers/lua.sh\n\nInvokes a single function from a Lua file using luajit. The function\nmust be a module-level export (returned from the file or set in a\npackage). Args are decoded from JSON; return values are encoded to JSON.\n\n### drivers/c.sh\n\nCompiles the .c file if its mtime is newer than the cached binary in\ntmp/cache/. The cache key is the source file's absolute path hashed.\nInvokes the compiled binary with the args. The binary must follow the\ndriver output contract (JSON to stdout).\n\nThe binary is expected to expose a `main`-style entry that reads args\nfrom argv and writes JSON to stdout. A small C header (shipped with\nsoramech) provides helpers for this.\n\n### drivers/bash.sh\n\nInvokes a bash function defined in the .sh file by sourcing the file\nand calling the function with the args as positional parameters.\nThe function must echo a JSON value (or array) to stdout.\n\n## User-defined drivers\n\nAdd the file extension and path to the map's drivers.json:\n\n  { \".rs\": \"drivers/rust.sh\" }\n\nWrite drivers/rust.sh. It receives the same arguments as any built-in\ndriver. Compile, interpret, or delegate however the language requires.\nThe runner doesn't care.\n\n## Driver lookup order\n\n  1. Map-local drivers.json (maps/<name>/drivers.json)\n  2. Global drivers.json (alongside soramech-runner.lua)\n  3. Hard error if extension not found — no fallback, no silent skip\n\n## Passing structured values between boxes\n\nAll inter-box values are JSON at the transport layer. Inside a Lua box,\ndkjson decodes input strings to Lua tables. The driver re-encodes return\nvalues to JSON. Inside a C box, the shipped helper header decodes argv\nJSON strings to C structs and encodes results back.\n\nThis means structured values cross language boundaries cleanly: a Lua\ntable produced by one box can be consumed by a C function in the next\nbox, because both sides see JSON at the wire level.\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/docs/003-driver-system.md"
        }
      }],

There is no defined on-disk format for map\ndirectories, box files, data files, or driver configuration.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe repository contains:\n  - Symlinks in libs/ pointing at dkjson and luasocket from the shared\n    library location\n  - A well-defined map directory format, documented and validated by a\n    small lua schema checker\n  - An example map in maps/hello/ that exercises one lua box and one data\n    file\n  - A create-map.lua utility that scaffolds a new map directory with all\n    required files and a tmp/ symlink\n  - A validate-map.lua utility that checks a map directory for format\n    errors and missing references\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Symlink dkjson.lua and luasocket into libs/\n2. Write src/001-schema.lua — defines the expected structure of box files,\n   meta.json, and drivers.json as lua tables. Used by both the runner and\n   the server to validate inputs before writing.\n3. Write src/002-validate-map.lua — loads all box files in a map directory,\n   checks schema, validates that every connection's to_box exists, validates\n   that branch boxes have \"else\" handled or declared. Prints errors and exits\n   non-zero if invalid.\n4. Write scripts/create-map.sh — takes a map name and maps-root path,\n   creates the directory structure, writes empty meta.json and drivers.json,\n   creates the tmp/ symlink to /tmp/<map-name>/.\n5. Create maps/hello/ as an example:\n   - One box calling src/hello.lua / hello()\n   - meta.json marking it as the entry box\n   - A data file data/state.json with one mutable field\n6. Write src/hello.lua with a public hello() function that reads a name\n   from its input and returns a greeting string.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/001-architecture.md — full map directory layout spec\n- docs/003-driver-system.md — driver contract referenced by validate-map\n\n## Notes\n\nThe tmp/ symlink must be created with an absolute path target. The\ncreate-map utility must handle the case where /tmp/<map-name>/ does not\nyet exist and create it.\n\nvalidate-map.lua is the source of truth for format correctness — any\ntime the architecture doc and the validator disagree, fix the validator\nand update the doc.\n",

{

          "content":"# 102 — Language driver interface\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo driver scripts exist. The runner has no mechanism to invoke functions\nin any language. There is no defined contract for how a driver receives\narguments or returns values.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA drivers/ directory exists alongside soramech-runner.lua containing\nthree built-in driver scripts: lua.sh, c.sh, and bash.sh. Each follows\nthe same interface. The runner invokes any driver identically regardless\nof language. A user can write a fourth driver for any language by copying\nthe pattern.\n\nDriver invocation contract:\n  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n\nAll args are strings. Structured values are JSON strings. Driver writes\none JSON value (or JSON array for tuples) to stdout on success. Exits\nnon-zero on failure, error message to stderr.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Write drivers/lua.sh — sources the target .lua file via luajit,\n   calls the named function with decoded JSON args, encodes return value\n   to JSON on stdout. Single-value and multi-value (tuple) returns both\n   produce a JSON array.\n2. Write drivers/c.sh — checks mtime of .c file against cached binary\n   in tmp/cache/. Compiles if stale (using gcc or cc, flags configurable\n   via env). Invokes the binary with args as argv. Binary must write JSON\n   to stdout per the contract.\n3. Write drivers/bash.sh — sources the .sh file, calls the named\n   function with args as positional params. Function must echo JSON to\n   stdout.\n4. Write a small test map maps/driver-test/ with one box per driver type\n   to verify each driver works end-to-end before the runner is built.\n5. Document the driver contract in drivers/README (plain text, short).\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/003-driver-system.md — full driver system spec\n- issues/101 — map scaffold (tmp/cache/ directory created there)\n- issues/103 — runner uses these drivers once they exist\n\n## Notes\n\nFor lua.sh: luajit must be on PATH. The script should fail with a clear\nerror if luajit is not found, not silently produce wrong output.\n\nFor c.sh: the cache key for compiled binaries is the absolute path of the\nsource file. A sha1 or md5 of the path is sufficient; the binary is\nstored as tmp/cache/<hash>. Stale check: stat both files, compare mtimes.\n\nFor bash.sh: functions in a sourced file may have side effects and access\nthe filesystem. This is expected and correct — bash boxes are intentionally\nless constrained than lua or C boxes.\n\nThe \"no special cases in the runner\" constraint means the runner must not\nhave any if-elseif chain on file extension. All dispatch goes through\nthe driver table loaded from drivers.json.\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/102-language-driver-interface.md"
        }
      }],

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-07T22:27:36.836Z",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",

    "content":[{
        "name":"Write",
        "id":"toolu_015UUw3RQcJSEXZer9TYdARF",
        "type":"tool_use",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "content":"# 103 — Runner: graph loader and validator\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 101 (map format must be defined before loading can be implemented)\n- 102 (driver list loaded here; drivers must exist to validate references)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo runner exists. There is no mechanism to load a map directory into\nmemory as a graph structure or to validate its integrity before execution.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nsoramech-runner.lua, when given a map directory, performs a load and\nvalidate phase before any execution begins:\n\n  1. Reads meta.json — confirms entry_box_id is present\n  2. Reads all files in boxes/ — parses each as a box table\n  3. Reads drivers.json (map-local, then global fallback)\n  4. Validates:\n     a. Every connection's to_box references an existing box id\n     b. Every connection is reciprocally written in the target box's file\n        (both ends agree) — disagreement is a hard error with a message\n        naming both files and the conflicting field\n     c. Every ref's file extension has a driver defined\n     d. Branch boxes: every non-\"else\" port has a predicate defined;\n        \"else\" port exists; if the map has any LLM-type boxes connected\n        to the branch, \"else\" is permitted to be unwired (retry semantics);\n        otherwise \"else\" must be wired or the runner refuses to start\n     e. No cycles that don't pass through a branch box (direct loops are\n        an error; loops through branches are allowed — they are the retry\n        pattern)\n  5. Builds an in-memory graph: table of box tables, adjacency lists\n     keyed by box id, driver table keyed by extension\n\nThe runner prints a structured error report and exits non-zero if any\nvalidation fails. No fallbacks.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Write src/003-loader.lua — public functions:\n   - load_map(map_dir) -> graph, err\n   - validate_graph(graph) -> ok, errors[]\n   Each error in errors[] is a table: {box_id, field, message}.\n2. The graph structure: { boxes={[id]=box}, entry=id, drivers={[ext]=path} }\n   Adjacency is derived from boxes' connections lists; no separate edge table.\n3. Cycle detection: DFS from entry box, mark visited. A cycle that reaches\n   a branch box is allowed (log a warning, not an error). A cycle that\n   doesn't pass through a branch box is an error.\n4. Write tests/001-loader-test.lua — loads maps/hello/ and maps/driver-test/,\n   asserts no errors. ```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-07T22:28:25.761Z",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",

  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "name":"Write",
        "id":"toolu_01V4seQPmw75JwXufjYFrzVZ",
        "type":"tool_use",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "content":"# 105 — HTTP server: file CRUD API\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 101 (map format must be defined; server validates against schema)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo server exists. Map files can only be edited by hand on the machine\nwhere they live.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nsoramech-server.lua is a minimal HTTP server backed by luasocket. It\nexposes a REST API that the browser uses to read and write map files.\nIt does nothing else. No runner management, no process spawning, no\nstreaming.\n\nStarted with: `luajit soramech-server.lua <maps-root> [port]`\nDefault port: 7700\n\nEndpoints:\n  GET  /maps                          — list map names (array of strings)\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes             — list box IDs in this map\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>        — read one box file (JSON)\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>        — write one box file (validates schema)\n  DELETE /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      — delete box (hard error if referenced)\n  GET  /maps/<name>/data/<filename>   — read a data file\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/data/<filename>   — write a data file\n  GET  /maps/<name>/drivers           — read drivers.json\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/drivers           — write drivers.json\n  GET  /maps/<name>/meta              — read meta.json\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/meta              — write meta.json\n\nAll request and response bodies are JSON. Content-Type: application/json.\nCORS headers must be set (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) so index.html\nserved from a file:// URL or a different origin can reach the server.\n\nError responses: { \"error\": \"message\" } with appropriate HTTP status.\n400 for schema violations, 404 for missing resources, 409 for constraint\nviolations (delete of a referenced box), 500 for filesystem errors.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Write src/005-http-server.lua — top-level server loop using luasocket's\n   tcp server primitives. Accept connections, parse HTTP request line and\n   headers, dispatch to handler table by method + path pattern.\n2. Route table: a dispatch table mapping {method, pattern} -> handler_fn.\n   Pattern matching is simple prefix matching on the path segments —\n   no regex needed.\n3. Each handler receives {method, path_parts, body_string} and returns\n   {status, body_string}. The server wraps these in HTTP framing.\n4. Validate box writes against src/001-schema.lua before writing to disk.\n   Reject with 400 and a descriptive error if validation fails.\n5. For DELETE /boxes/<id>: scan all other box files for references to the\n   deleted id in their connections list. Hard error with 409 if found;\n   list all referencing boxes in the error body.\n6. Write a simple smoke test: scripts/test-server.sh — starts the server,\n   uses curl to create a box, read it back, update it, delete it. Asserts\n   expected responses.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/001-architecture.md — endpoint list and error format\n- issues/101 — schema validator used in step 4\n- issues/106 — browser client that calls these endpoints\n\n## Notes\n\nluasocket's HTTP server support is low-level.     "content":"# 105 — HTTP server: file CRUD API\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 101 (map format must be defined; server validates against schema)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo server exists. Map files can only be edited by hand on the machine\nwhere they live.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nsoramech-server.lua is a minimal HTTP server backed by luasocket. It\nexposes a REST API that the browser uses to read and write map files.\nIt does nothing else. No runner management, no process spawning, no\nstreaming.\n\nStarted with: `luajit soramech-server.lua <maps-root> [port]`\nDefault port: 7700\n\nEndpoints:\n  GET  /maps                          — list map names (array of strings)\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes             — list box IDs in this map\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>        — read one box file (JSON)\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>        — write one box file (validates schema)\n  DELETE /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      — delete box (hard error if referenced)\n  GET  /maps/<name>/data/<filename>   — read a data file\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/data/<filename>   — write a data file\n  GET  /maps/<name>/drivers           — read drivers.json\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/drivers           — write drivers.json\n  GET  /maps/<name>/meta              — read meta.json\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/meta              — write meta.json\n\nAll request and response bodies are JSON. Content-Type: application/json.\nCORS headers must be set (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) so index.html\nserved from a file:// URL or a different origin can reach the server.\n\nError responses: { \"error\": \"message\" } with appropriate HTTP status.\n400 for schema violations, 404 for missing resources, 409 for constraint\nviolations (delete of a referenced box), 500 for filesystem errors.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Write src/005-http-server.lua — top-level server loop using luasocket's\n   tcp server primitives. Accept connections, parse HTTP request line and\n   headers, dispatch to handler table by method + path pattern.\n2. Route table: a dispatch table mapping {method, pattern} -> handler_fn.\n   Pattern matching is simple prefix matching on the path segments —\n   no regex needed.\n3. Each handler receives {method, path_parts, body_string} and returns\n   {status, body_string}. The server wraps these in HTTP framing.\n4. Validate box writes against src/001-schema.lua before writing to disk.\n   Reject with 400 and a descriptive error if validation fails.\n5. For DELETE /boxes/<id>: scan all other box files for references to the\n   deleted id in their connections list. Hard error with 409 if found;\n   list all referencing boxes in the error body.\n6. Write a simple smoke test: scripts/test-server.sh — starts the server,\n   uses curl to create a box, read it back, update it, delete it. Asserts\n   expected responses.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/001-architecture.md — endpoint list and error format\n- issues/101 — schema validator used in step 4\n- issues/106 — browser client that calls these endpoints\n\n## Notes\n\nluasocket's HTTP server support is low-level. The server loop must handle\nkeep-alive connections correctly, or close after each response. Closing\nafter each response (HTTP/1.0 style) is simpler and sufficient for the\nbrowser editor's access pattern.\n\nThe server should log each request to stdout in a single line:\n  [timestamp] METHOD /path -> status (ms)\nThis makes debugging easy without needing a log file.\n\nThe server must not follow symlinks outside the maps-root. Validate that\nevery resolved file path begins with maps-root before reading or writing.\nThis is the only security boundary needed since the server is local-only.\n",

          "content":"# 106 — Web editor: canvas and box rendering\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 105 (server must be running for the editor to load map files)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo web editor exists. Map files can only be viewed and edited as raw JSON.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nindex.html is a single-file web application (no build step, no framework,\nno dependencies beyond the fetch API and the Canvas 2D API). When opened\nin a browser and pointed at a running soramech-server, it:\n\n  - Renders an infinite-scroll canvas with pan (drag) and zoom (scroll)\n  - Loads all boxes for the current map and draws each as a rectangle\n  - Each box displays: label, kind badge, input port list on the left,\n    output port list on the right\n  - Clicking a box opens an inspector panel on the right side showing all\n    editable fields (label, ref, fn, inputs, outputs)\n  - Editing any field in the inspector sends a PUT to the server immediately\n    (autosave — no explicit save button)\n  - Double-clicking the canvas background creates a new box at that position\n  - Boxes are draggable; dragging updates the ui.x/ui.y fields in the box\n    file via PUT\n\nThe canvas coordinate system uses a camera transform (pan offset + zoom\nscale) applied before drawing. All box positions are in \"world\" coordinates\nstored in the box file; the camera transform maps world to screen.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Write assets/index.html with a <canvas> element full-viewport and a\n   sidebar div for the inspector panel.\n2. Write assets/js/001-canvas.js — camera state (pan x/y, zoom), input\n   handlers for drag-to-pan and scroll-to-zoom, a render loop using\n   requestAnimationFrame, coordinate conversion functions world_to_screen\n   and screen_to_world.\n3. Write assets/js/002-boxes.js — box rendering (rectangle, label,\n   kind badge, port dots on left/right edges), hit testing for click and\n   drag.\n4. Write assets/js/003-api.js — thin wrapper around fetch for each server\n   endpoint. Returns parsed JSON or throws with the server error message.\n5. Write assets/js/004-inspector.js — sidebar panel that populates a form\n   from the selected box's fields and fires PUT on each input change.\n6. Write assets/js/005-app.js — top-level: on load, ask the user for the\n   server URL and map name, load all boxes, enter the render loop.\n7. All JS files are loaded with <script> tags in index.html in numbered\n   order. No module bundler.\n\n## UI design notes\n\nPort dots: input ports are drawn on the left edge of the box, one dot per\ninput, evenly spaced. Output ports on the right edge. Port dot size should\nbe large enough to click (at minimum 8px radius in screen space). Port\nlabels appear on hover.\n\nKind badge: a small colored label in the top-right corner of the box.\n  \"call\" → blue, \"branch\" → orange, \"data\" → green.\n\nBox size: calculated from the number of ports. Minimum height ensures the\nlabel and badge fit. Width is fixed (e.g., 180px world units).\n\nInspector panel: slides in from the right when a box is selected. Fields\nrendered as labeled inputs. Input/output port lists are rendered as\nadd/remove lists (click + to add a port, click x to remove). Predicate\nfields on branch box ports are shown as a comparator dropdown + value input.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/001-architecture.md — box file format (ui.x, ui.y fields)\n- issues/105 — server endpoints used by api.js\n- issues/107 — wire drawing added on top of this canvas\n\n## Notes\n\nThe canvas render loop should only redraw when state changes (box moved,\nbox selected, camera moved) — not every frame unconditionally. A dirty\nflag is sufficient for v1; no need for a scene graph.\n\nThe server URL and map name should be stored in localStorage so the user\ndoesn't have to re-enter them on reload.\n",

          "content":"# 107 — Web editor: wiring and connection UI\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 106 (canvas and box rendering must exist before wires can be drawn)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nBoxes can be drawn on the canvas but there is no way to connect them.\nConnection data exists in box files but is not visualized.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe canvas renders wires between connected boxes. The user can draw new\nwires by dragging from an output port dot to an input port dot. Wires\ncan be deleted by clicking them and pressing delete.\n\nWhen a wire is created:\n  1. Both endpoint box files are updated via PUT (connection added to both)\n  2. If the connection creates a cycle that does not pass through a branch\n     box, the editor warns but does not prevent the connection (the runner\n     will reject it at load time; the editor is not the enforcement point)\n\nWhen a wire is deleted:\n  1. Both endpoint box files are updated via PUT (connection removed from both)\n\nWire rendering:\n  - Bezier curve from output port dot to input port dot\n  - Control points offset horizontally by ~80 world units to give a smooth S curve\n  - Color: neutral (grey) by default; selected wire highlighted\n  - Branch box ports: each port has its own wire color (cycling palette)\n    so multi-port wires are visually distinct\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1.           "content":"# 108 — Branch box and predicate routing\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 104 (executor must exist; predicate evaluation is added to it here)\n- 107 (wire UI must exist; branch port wires need visual distinction)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo branch box type exists. All routing is linear (one output, one wire).\nThere is no mechanism to conditionally fire one box vs. another based on\na value.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA box with \"kind\": \"branch\" has named output ports instead of positional\noutputs. Each port (except \"else\") carries a predicate. The executor\nevaluates each predicate against the input value and fires the first port\nwhose predicate is true. If no predicate matches, the \"else\" port fires.\n\nPort predicates:\n  { \"op\": \"eq\"|\"lt\"|\"gt\"|\"lte\"|\"gte\"|\"contains\"|\"matches\", \"value\": <literal> }\n\n\"matches\" uses lua pattern matching against a string input.\n\"contains\" checks whether a string input contains the literal as a substring.\n\nBranch box behavior in two scenarios:\n\n  Numeric/string predicate branch:\n    - \"else\" port must be wired to something, or the runner refuses to start\n    - If no predicate matches and \"else\" fires, the program continues from\n      the \"else\" port's connection\n    - The runner logs which port fired for each branch box in last-run.json\n\n  LLM output classification:\n    - \"else\" port may be left unwired in the box file (omit the connection)\n    - If \"else\" fires on an unwired port, the runner re-queues the box\n      whose output fed this branch box (the immediately upstream box in the\n      path that led here)\n    - The upstream box is re-invoked with any fields marked \"retry_vary\"\n      in its box file pseudo-randomized (e.g., temperature, top_p)\n    - Retry limit: configurable per branch box, default 3. Exceeded retry\n      limit is a hard error, not a silent loop.\n\nThe \"retry_vary\" field on a box:\n  \"retry_vary\": { \"temperature\": { \"min\": 0.5, \"max\": 1.2 } }\n  On retry, any field listed here is replaced with a random value in range.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Add branch box handling to src/004-executor.lua:\n   - When a branch box fires, evaluate each port's predicate in order.\n   - Fire the first matching port's connection.\n   - If no match, fire \"else\". If \"else\" has no connection, trigger retry.\n2. Add retry state to the executor: a per-box retry counter in run state.\n   On retry trigger, decrement counter; if zero, halt with error.\n3. Implement retry_vary: before re-invoking the upstream box, for each\n   field in its retry_vary table, generate a random value in the given\n   range and override the corresponding input before invocation.\n4. Update src/003-loader.lua validation: branch boxes without an \"else\"\n   connection are valid only if at least one upstream box has a retry_vary\n   field. If neither condition is met, the validator rejects the map.\n5. Update assets/js/006-wires.js: branch box ports each get a distinct\n   color from a cycling palette. Port labels (\"rogue\", \"wizard\", \"else\")\n   are drawn alongside the port dot on the canvas.\n6. Update assets/js/004-inspector.js: branch box inspector shows port list\n   with add/remove, predicate editor per port (op dropdown + value input),\n   and retry limit input.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/001-architecture.md — branch box file format\n- issues/104 — executor (predicate evaluation added here)\n- issues/107 — wire UI (port color and label rendering)\n\n## Notes\n\nPort predicate evaluation order matters: ports are evaluated in the order\nthey appear in the \"ports\" array. The first matching predicate fires. This\nis intentional — the user controls priority by ordering ports. Document\nthis in the inspector UI (e.g., \"ports are evaluated top to bottom\").\n\nThe retry mechanism is deliberately minimal: it re-runs one upstream box\nwith varied parameters. It is not a general loop construct. If the user\nneeds complex retry logic (backoff, multiple retries with different\nstrategies), they should model it with explicit boxes wired in a cycle\nthrough a branch box. The built-in retry is for the common case of\n\"ask the LLM again with a different temperature.\"\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/108-branch-box-and-predicate-routing.md"
        }

          "content":"# 109 — Data files: persistent and ephemeral storage\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 101 (map directory and tmp/ symlink created there)\n- 104 (executor must exist; data file access added to driver interface here)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo data file access exists. There is no distinction between persistent and\nephemeral storage in the map directory.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA map's data/ directory contains JSON files. Each file is a lua table\nserialized with dkjson. A section-level \"constant\" flag marks individual\nfields as read-only. A file-level \"constant\" flag makes the entire file\nread-only.\n\nBoxes access data files through a lua library (libs/soramech-data.lua)\nthat the driver for lua boxes includes in the lua environment. The library\nis not built into the runner — it is imported by the lua driver like any\nother library.\n\n  data.get(map_dir, filename, field_path) -> value\n  data.set(map_dir, filename, field_path, value) -> ok, err\n  data.load(map_dir, filename) -> table, err\n\ndata.set refuses writes to constant fields and returns an error string.\nThe caller decides whether to propagate the error or halt.\n\nEphemeral data (state during a run, logs, last-run snapshot) goes to\ntmp/, which is a symlink to /tmp/<map-name>/. The same library works\nwith tmp/ as a directory argument — no special case. Tmp files are not\nbacked up and are expected to disappear on reboot.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Write libs/soramech-data.lua — implements data.get, data.set, data.load.\n   Uses dkjson for all encode/decode. data.set reads the current file,\n   modifies the specified field path (dot-separated key), validates the\n   constant flag, and writes the file back atomically (write to .tmp then\n   rename).\n2. Define field_path as a dot-separated key string: \"config.model\" accesses\n   table[\"config\"][\"model\"]. Supports only string keys (no array indexing\n   in v1).\n3. Write tests/003-data-test.lua — creates a temp data file, calls\n   data.set, reads back with data.get, asserts value matches. Tries to\n   write a constant field, asserts error returned.\n4. Document in libs/soramech-data.info.md: each public function with\n   inputs, outputs, and error conditions.\n5. Update drivers/lua.sh to add libs/ to the luajit package path so\n   soramech-data.lua is available to any lua box function without\n   explicit path manipulation.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/001-architecture.md — data file format and tmp/ symlink\n- issues/101 — tmp/ symlink creation\n- issues/102 — lua driver (package path updated in step 5)\n- issues/104 — executor (data library available to boxes during execution)\n\n## Notes\n\nAtomic writes (write-to-tmp-then-rename) are important for data files\nthat a running map and the browser editor might both touch. Rename is\natomic on POSIX filesystems; the reader always sees either the old or\nthe new file, never a partial write.\n\nConstant field validation: when data.set is called on a constant field,\nreturn an error string rather than panicking. The driver should propagate\nthis to the runner as a non-zero exit (write the error to stderr). The\nrunner then halts the map with a descriptive message. Prefer hard errors\nover silent skips here.\n\nThe library design (separate from the runner, imported by the driver) is\nintentional. It means the library works identically in a standalone lua\nscript, in a test, and inside a running map. No runner context is needed\nto use it.\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/109-data-files-persistent-and-ephemeral.md"
        }
      }],

        "input":{
          "content":"---\nname: SoraMech project context\ndescription: Core architecture decisions, file layout, and north star use case for SoraMech\ntype: project\n---\n\nSoraMech is a visual FSM/dataflow editor and execution engine at /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/.\n\n**Why:** Primary use case is LLM orchestration on the SoraMind Alpine cluster. Strings flow between boxes like variables. History is explicit, loaded from disk only when a box needs it.\n\n**Three independent programs sharing a map directory:**\n- `soramech-server.lua` — thin HTTP file CRUD proxy only. No runner management. Started for remote editing.\n- `soramech-runner.lua` — FSM execution engine, invoked from CLI independently. Reads map dir, walks graph, invokes drivers.\n- `index.html` — vanilla JS canvas editor. Editor only, no \"run\" button. Talks to server for file ops.\n\n**Key architecture decisions:**\n- Each box is its own JSON file in `boxes/<id>.json`. Connections written to BOTH endpoint files; runner validates both ends agree — hard error if not.\n- Language drivers are shell scripts. No special cases for any language in the runner. Lua/C/bash ship as pre-written driver scripts, same interface as user-defined ones.\n- Driver invocation: `<driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [args...]`. Outputs JSON to stdout.\n- Branch box: dedicated node kind with named output ports + always an \"else\" port. LLM-based \"else\" can be unwired (triggers retry of upstream box with pseudo-randomized retry_vary fields). Numeric/string \"else\" must be wired or map won't start.\n- Data files: per-map JSON in `data/`. Section-level `constant` flag. Accessed via `libs/soramech-data.lua` library (not a built-in runner API).\n- State/ephemeral: `tmp/` is a symlink to `/tmp/<map-name>/`. Logs, last-run snapshot, C binary cache go here.\n- v1 executor: synchronous, each box call wrapped in `task_fn(inputs)->outputs` boundary matching 3d-rts thread pool action chain signature for future swap.\n\n**How to apply:** When working on any component, respect the three-way separation. Server never knows about runner. Runner never knows about server. Map directory format is the only shared contract.\n",
          "file_path":"/home/ritz/.claude/projects/-mnt-mtwo-programs-sora-soramech/memory/project_soramech.md"
        }
      }],

There is no defined on-disk format for map\ndirectories, box files, data files, or driver configuration.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe repository contains:\n  - Symlinks in libs/ pointing at dkjson and luasocket from the shared\n    library location\n  - A well-defined map directory format, documented and validated by a\n    small lua schema checker\n  - An example map in maps/hello/ that exercises one lua box and one data\n    file\n  - A create-map.lua utility that scaffolds a new map directory with all\n    required files and a tmp/ symlink\n  - A validate-map.lua utility that checks a map directory for format\n    errors and missing references\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Symlink dkjson.lua and luasocket into libs/\n2. Write src/001-schema.lua — defines the expected structure of box files,\n   meta.json, and drivers.json as lua tables. Write src/002-validate-map.lua — loads all box files in a map directory,\n   checks schema, validates that every connection's to_box exists, validates\n   that branch boxes have \"else\" handled or declared. Prints errors and exits\n   non-zero if invalid.\n4. Write scripts/create-map.sh — takes a map name and maps-root path,\n   creates the directory structure, writes empty meta.json and drivers.json,\n   creates the tmp/ symlink to /tmp/<map-name>/.\n5. Create maps/hello/ as an example:\n   - One box calling src/hello.lua / hello()\n   - meta.json marking it as the entry box\n   - A data file data/state.json with one mutable field\n6. Write src/hello.lua with a public hello() function that reads a name\n   from its input and returns a greeting string.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/001-architecture.md — full map directory layout spec\n- docs/003-driver-system.md — driver contract referenced by validate-map\n\n## Notes\n\nThe tmp/ symlink must be created with an absolute path target. The\ncreate-map utility must handle the case where /tmp/<map-name>/ does not\nyet exist and create it.\n\nvalidate-map.lua is the source of truth for format correctness — any\ntime the architecture doc and the validator disagree, fix the validator\nand update the doc.\n",

Loads a map directory, validates the graph, then\n49\texecutes boxes in dependency order. None of the three knows about the others at runtime.\n\n```\n  Browser (index.html)\n       |  HTTP (file CRUD)\n       v\n  soramech-server.lua          [map directory]\n                               maps/<name>/\n                                 boxes/\n                                 data/\n                                 drivers.json\n                                 meta.json\n                                 tmp/ -> /tmp/<name>/\n       ^\n       | reads & writes\n  soramech-runner.lua\n```\n\n### soramech-server.lua\n\nThin HTTP proxy. Receives JSON requests from the browser and translates\nthem into file reads and writes on the map directory. No logic beyond\npath validation and basic consistency checks (e.g., reject a delete if\nthe box is still referenced by another box's connection list).\n\nStarted with: `luajit soramech-server.lua <maps-root> [port]`\nDefault port: 7700\n\nEndpoints (all operate on map files):\n  GET  /maps                        list maps\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes           list box IDs\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      read box file\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      write box file\n  DELETE /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>    remove box (validates no dangling refs)\n  GET  /maps/<name>/data/<name>     read data file\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/data/<name>     write data file\n  GET  /maps/<name>/drivers         read drivers.json\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/drivers         write drivers.json\n  GET  /maps/<name>/meta            read meta.json\n\n### soramech-runner.lua\n\nFSM execution engine. Loads a map directory, validates the graph, then\nexecutes boxes in dependency order. Each box invocation is wrapped in a\n`task_fn(inputs) -> outputs` call — matching the 3d-rts thread pool's\naction chain signature for future threading compatibility.\n\nStarted with: `luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>`\n\nExecution steps:\n  1. Read all box files from boxes/\n  2. Validate: all connection endpoints exist, branch \"else\" handled\n  3. Determine entry box from meta.json\n  4. Execute: resolve inputs, invoke driver, collect outputs, fire wires\n  5. On completion, write last-run snapshot to tmp/last-run.json\n\n### index.html\n\nStatic HTML + vanilla JS. Infinite-scroll canvas. Box diagram editor.\nTalks to soramech-server.lua for all file operations. No run button —\nthe user starts the runner separately from the terminal.\n\n## Map directory format\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/\n  meta.json          — { name, description, entry_box_id }\n  drivers.json       — { \".lua\": \"drivers/lua.sh\", \".c\": \"drivers/c.sh\", ... }\n  boxes/\n    <id>.json        — one file per box (see Box file format below)\n  data/\n    <name>.json      — lua table as JSON; sections have \"constant\": bool\n  drivers/\n    lua.sh           — built-in lua driver (shipped with soramech)\n    c.sh             — built-in C driver",

The runner validates\n130\tat load time that both ends agree. Disagreement is a hard error.\n131\t\n132\t## Language driver interface\n133\t\n134\tDrivers are shell scripts. The engine invokes them as:\n135\t\n136\t  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg1> <arg2> ...]\n137\t\n138\tOutputs are returned as JSON on stdout. Exit code non-zero = box failure.\n139\tSee docs/003-driver-system.md for the full driver contract.\n140\t\n141\t## Execution model (v1 — synchronous)\n142\t\n143\tThe runner walks the graph depth-first from the entry box. Each box call:\n144\t\n145\t  1. Collect inputs: read wired output values from predecessor boxes\n146\t  2. Invoke driver: shell out to the appropriate driver script\n147\t  3. Collect outputs: parse JSON from driver stdout\n148\t  4. Store outputs: held in runner memory, keyed by box id + output name\n149\t  5. Fire connections: enqueue boxes whose input dependencies are now met\n150\t\n151\tEach step is wrapped in a `task_fn` boundary so the runner can be\n152\tthreaded later by substituting the synchronous executor with one backed\n153\tby effil-jit or the custom thread pool from the 3d-rts project.\n154\t\n155\t## Data files\n156\t\n157\tPersistent data lives in data/<name>.json. Individual\n170\tfields can be flagged constant within an otherwise mutable file.\n171\t\n172\tEphemeral state (scratch tables, logs, last-run snapshot) goes to tmp/,\n173\twhich is a symlink to /tmp/<map-name>/. {

          "content":"-- Schema definitions and validators for SoraMech map files.\n-- Validates box files, meta.json, and drivers.json against the spec\n-- in docs/001-architecture.md. Used by both the runner and the server\n-- before any file is written to disk.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ valid_kinds\nlocal valid_kinds = { call = true, branch = true, data = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ valid_ops\nlocal valid_ops = {\n    eq = true, lt = true, gt = true,\n    lte = true, gte = true, contains = true, matches = true\n}\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ err\nlocal function err(errors, msg)\n    errors[#errors + 1] = msg\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_port\nlocal function validate_port(port, i, errors)\n    -- \"else\" port has no predicate; all others require one\n    if port.name == nil then\n        err(errors, \"port[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'name'\")\n        return\n    end\n    if port.name == \"else\" then return end\n    if port.predicate == nil then\n        err(errors, \"port '\" .. port.name .. \"' missing predicate (only 'else' may omit it)\")\n        return\n    end\n    local p = port.predicate\n    if p.op == nil then\n        err(errors, \"port '\" .. port.name .. \"' predicate missing 'op'\")\n    elseif not valid_ops[p.op] then\n        err(errors, \"port '\" .. port.name .. \"' predicate has unknown op '\" .. p.op .. \"'\")\n    end\n    if p.value == nil then\n        err(errors, \"port '\" .. port.name .. \"' predicate missing 'value'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_connection\nlocal function validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- each connection links one output port to one input port on another box\n    if c.from_output == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_output'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_port_connection\nlocal function validate_port_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- branch box connections reference a named port instead of from_output\n    if c.from_port == nil then\n        err(errors, \"branch connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_port'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"branch connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"branch connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_box\nfunction M.validate_box(box)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(box) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"box must be a table\" }\n    end\n\n    if box.id == nil or type(box.id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'id'\")\n    end\n    if box.label == nil or type(box.label) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'label'\")\n    end\n    if box.kind == nil or not valid_kinds[box.kind] then\n        err(errors, \"missing or invalid 'kind' (must be call, branch, or data)\")\n    end\n\n    if box.kind == \"call\" then\n        if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"call box missing 'ref'\")\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        if box.outputs ~= nil and type(box.outputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'outputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n\n    elseif box.kind == \"branch\" then\n        if box.inputs == nil or type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"branch box missing 'inputs'\")\n        end\n        if box.ports == nil or type(box.ports) ~= \"table\" or #box.ports == 0 then\n            err(errors, \"branch box missing 'ports' array\")\n        else\n            local has_else = false\n            for i, p in ipairs(box.ports) do\n                validate_port(p, i, errors)\n                if p.name == \"else\" then has_else = true end\n            end\n            if not has_else then\n                err(errors, \"branch box missing required 'else' port\")\n            end\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_port_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a table\")\n        elseif box.ui.x == nil or box.ui.y == nil then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must have 'x' and 'y' fields\")\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or type(meta.name) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'name'\")\n    end\n    if meta.entry_box_id == nil or type(meta.entry_box_id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'entry_box_id'\")\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_drivers\nfunction M.validate_drivers(drivers)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(drivers) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"drivers.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    for ext, path in pairs(drivers) do\n        if type(ext) ~= \"string\" or ext:sub(1, 1) ~= \".\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver key '\" .. tostring(ext) .. \"' must be a dot-prefixed extension\")\n        end\n        if type(path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver value for '\" .. ext .. \"' must be a string path\")\n        end\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",

        }

          "content":"# 001-schema.lua — Public API\n\nSchema validators for all SoraMech map file types.\nReturns error arrays (empty = valid). Used by runner and server before any write.\n\n## M.validate_box(box: table) -> errors: string[]\n\nValidates a parsed box file table. Checks id, label, kind, and kind-specific\nfields. For \"call\" boxes: ref, optional fn, inputs/outputs arrays, connections.\nFor \"branch\" boxes: inputs, ports array (each port needs predicate except \"else\"),\n\"else\" port must be present.\n\n## M.validate_meta(meta: table) -> errors: string[]\n\nValidates a parsed meta.json table. enforces branch box rules.\n-- Run: luajit src/002-validate-map.lua <map-dir>\n-- Exits 0 if valid, non-zero with error report if not.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\n-- allow running from any directory by finding libs relative to DIR\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal json   = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal schema = require(\"001-schema\")\n\n-- {{{ read_file\nlocal function read_file(path)\n    local f, ferr = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then return nil, ferr end\n    local contents = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    return contents\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ parse_json_file\nlocal function parse_json_file(path)\n    local raw, ferr = read_file(path)\n    if not raw then return nil, \"cannot open \" .. path .. \": \" .. ferr end\n    local obj, _, jerr = json.decode(raw)\n    if not obj then return nil, \"JSON error in \" .. path .. \": \" .. jerr end\n    return obj\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ load_boxes\nlocal function load_boxes(map_dir)\n    -- returns table of {id -> box_table} and a list of errors\n    local boxes = {}\n    local errors = {}\n    local boxes_dir = map_dir .. \"/boxes\"\n\n    local handle = io.popen(\"ls \" .. boxes_dir .. \"/*.json 2>/dev/null\")\n    if not handle then\n        return boxes, { \"cannot list \" .. boxes_dir }\n    end\n    local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n    handle:close()\n\n    for path in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n        local box, berr = parse_json_file(path)\n        if not box then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = berr\n        else\n            local box_errors = schema.validate_box(box)\n            if #box_errors > 0 then\n                for _, e in ipairs(box_errors) do\n                    errors[#errors + 1] = path .. \": \" .. e\n                end\n            else\n                boxes[box.id] = box\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    return boxes, errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ check_connections\nlocal function check_connections(boxes, errors)\n    -- every connection must have a reciprocal entry in the target box\n    for id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        local conns = box.connections or {}\n        for _, c in ipairs(conns) do\n            local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n            if target == nil then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection to unknown box '\" .. c.to_box .. \"'\"\n            else\n                -- find a reciprocal connection in target pointing back to this box\n                -- reciprocal means: target has a connection with to_box == id\n                -- (an incoming connection is recorded as an outgoing from id in target)\n                -- the spec stores connections as outgoing in the source box,\n                -- but the target box must also list this connection\n                local found = false\n                for _, tc in ipairs(target.connections or {}) do\n                    if tc.to_box == id or (tc.from_output ~= nil and c.to_box == id) then\n                        -- check the target has a record referencing this source\n                        found = true\n                        break\n                    end\n                end\n                -- reciprocal check: look for an entry in target that names id as to_box\n                -- OR look for a separate \"incoming\" field — per spec, connections are\n                -- written to both ends, so we look for target having a connection that\n                -- references the source box.\n                -- Simplified: target must have a connection where to_box == id OR\n                -- a connection where from_output == c.to_input (coming from this box).\n                -- The spec says both ends list it — so target.connections should include\n                -- a record from_port/from_output matching back to id.\n                -- For v1 validate: check that target has any connection referencing id.\n                found = false\n                for _, tc in ipairs(target.connections or {}) do\n                    if tc.to_box == id then\n                        found = true\n                        break\n                    end\n                end\n                if not found then\n                    errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"' -> '\" .. c.to_box ..\n                        \"': connection not reciprocated in target box file\"\n                end\n            end\n        end\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ check_branch_else\nlocal function check_branch_else(boxes, errors)\n    -- branch boxes must have an \"else\" port (enforced by schema, re-checked here\n    -- for clarity), and numeric/string-predicate branch boxes must wire \"else\"\n    for id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        if box.kind ~= \"branch\" then goto continue end\n\n        local has_else_port = false\n        local has_else_wire = false\n        for _, p in ipairs(box.ports or {}) do\n            if p.name == \"else\" then\n                has_else_port = true\n            end\n        end\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_port == \"else\" then\n                has_else_wire = true\n            end\n        end\n\n        if not has_else_port then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"branch box '\" .. id .. \"' missing 'else' port\"\n        end\n\n        -- if else is unwired, the box must have retry_vary upstream to be valid;\n        -- we cannot check retry_vary here without traversing upstream, so we emit\n        -- a warning rather than a hard error — the runner will enforce at execute time\n        if has_else_port and not has_else_wire then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"branch box '\" .. id ..\n                \"': 'else' port is unwired (valid only for LLM retry; runner will \" ..\n                \"require upstream box to have retry_vary defined)\"\n        end\n\n        ::continue::\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_map\nlocal function validate_map(map_dir)\n    local errors = {}\n\n    -- meta.json\n    local meta, merr = parse_json_file(map_dir .. \"/meta.json\")\n    if not meta then\n        errors[#errors + 1] = merr\n    else\n        local meta_errors = schema.validate_meta(meta)\n        for _, e in ipairs(meta_errors) do\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"meta.json: \" .. e\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- drivers.json\n    local drivers, derr = parse_json_file(map_dir .. \"/drivers.json\")\n    if not drivers then\n        errors[#errors + 1] = derr\n    else\n        local driver_errors = schema.validate_drivers(drivers)\n        for _, e in ipairs(driver_errors) do\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"drivers.json: \" .. e\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- boxes\n    local boxes, box_errors = load_boxes(map_dir)\n    for _, e in ipairs(box_errors) do\n        errors[#errors + 1] = e\n    end\n\n    -- cross-box checks (only if boxes loaded cleanly enough)\n    if #errors == 0 then\n        check_connections(boxes, errors)\n        check_branch_else(boxes, errors)\n\n        -- entry box must exist\n        if meta and meta.entry_box_id then\n            if not boxes[meta.entry_box_id] then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"meta.json entry_box_id '\" ..\n                    meta.entry_box_id .. \"' does not match any box file\"\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ main\nlocal function main(args)\n    local map_dir = args[1]\n    if map_dir == nil then\n        io.stderr:write(\"usage: luajit 002-validate-map.lua <map-dir>\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    local errors = validate_map(map_dir)\n\n    if #errors == 0 then\n        print(\"OK: \" .. map_dir .. \" is valid\")\n        os.exit(0)\n    else\n        io.stderr:write(\"INVALID: \" .. map_dir .. \"\\n\")\n        for _, e in ipairs(errors) do\n            io.stderr:write(\"  error: \" .. e .. \"\\n\")\n        end\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\nmain(arg)\n",

    "content":"-- CLI tool that validates a SoraMech map directory for correctness.\n-- Checks schema of all box files, validates connection endpoints exist\n-- and agree on both ends, and enforces branch box rules.\n-- Run: luajit src/002-validate-map.lua <map-dir>\n-- Exits 0 if valid, non-zero with error report if not.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\n-- allow running from any directory by finding libs relative to DIR\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal json   = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal schema = require(\"001-schema\")\n\n-- {{{ read_file\nlocal function read_file(path)\n    local f, ferr = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then return nil, ferr end\n    local contents = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    return contents\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ parse_json_file\nlocal function parse_json_file(path)\n    local raw, ferr = read_file(path)\n    if not raw then return nil, \"cannot open \" .. path .. \": \" .. ferr end\n    local obj, _, jerr = json.decode(raw)\n    if not obj then return nil, \"JSON error in \" .. path .. \": \" .. jerr end\n    return obj\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ load_boxes\nlocal function load_boxes(map_dir)\n    -- returns table of {id -> box_table} and a list of errors\n    local boxes = {}\n    local errors = {}\n    local boxes_dir = map_dir .. \"/boxes\"\n\n    local handle = io.popen(\"ls \" .. boxes_dir .. \"/*.json 2>/dev/null\")\n    if not handle then\n        return boxes, { \"cannot list \" .. boxes_dir }\n    end\n    local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n    handle:close()\n\n    for path in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n        local box, berr = parse_json_file(path)\n        if not box then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = berr\n        else\n            local box_errors = schema.validate_box(box)\n            if #box_errors > 0 then\n                for _, e in ipairs(box_errors) do\n                    errors[#errors + 1] = path .. \": \" .. e\n                end\n            else\n                boxes[box.id] = box\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    return boxes, errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ check_connections\nlocal function check_connections(boxes, errors)\n    -- every connection must have a reciprocal entry in the target box\n    for id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        local conns = box.connections or {}\n        for _, c in ipairs(conns) do\n            local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n            if target == nil then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection to unknown box '\" .. c.to_box .. \"'\"\n            else\n                -- find a reciprocal connection in target pointing back to this box\n                -- reciprocal means: target has a connection with to_box == id\n                -- (an incoming connection is recorded as an outgoing from id in target)\n                -- the spec stores connections as outgoing in the source box,\n                -- but the target box must also list this connection\n                local found = false\n                for _, tc in ipairs(target.connections or {}) do\n                    if tc.to_box == id or (tc.from_output ~= nil and c.to_box == id) then\n                        -- check the target has a record referencing this source\n                        found = true\n                        break\n                    end\n                end\n                -- reciprocal check: look for an entry in target that names id as to_box\n                -- OR look for a separate \"incoming\" field — per spec, connections are\n                -- written to both ends, so we look for target having a connection that\n                -- references the source box.\n                -- Simplified: target must have a connection where to_box == id OR\n                -- a connection where from_output == c.to_input (coming from this box).\n                -- The spec says both ends list it — so target.connections should include\n                -- a record from_port/from_output matching back to id.\n                -- For v1 validate: check that target has any connection referencing id.\n                found = false\n                for _, tc in ipairs(target.connections or {}) do\n                    if tc.to_box == id then\n                        found = true\n                        break\n                    end\n                end\n                if not found then\n                    errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"' -> '\" .. c.to_box ..\n                        \"': connection not reciprocated in target box file\"\n                end\n            end\n        end\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ check_branch_else\nlocal function check_branch_else(boxes, errors)\n    -- branch boxes must have an \"else\" port (enforced by schema, re-checked here\n    -- for clarity), and numeric/string-predicate branch boxes must wire \"else\"\n    for id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        if box.kind ~= \"branch\" then goto continue end\n\n        local has_else_port = false\n        local has_else_wire = false\n        for _, p in ipairs(box.ports or {}) do\n            if p.name == \"else\" then\n                has_else_port = true\n            end\n        end\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_port == \"else\" then\n                has_else_wire = true\n            end\n        end\n\n        if not has_else_port then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"branch box '\" .. id .. \"' missing 'else' port\"\n        end\n\n        -- if else is unwired, the box must have retry_vary upstream to be valid;\n        -- we cannot check retry_vary here without traversing upstream, so we emit\n        -- a warning rather than a hard error — the runner will enforce at execute time\n        if has_else_port and not has_else_wire then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"branch box '\" .. id ..\n                \"': 'else' port is unwired (valid only for LLM retry; runner will \" ..\n                \"require upstream box to have retry_vary defined)\"\n        end\n\n        ::continue::\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_map\nlocal function validate_map(map_dir)\n    local errors = {}\n\n    -- meta.json\n    local meta, merr = parse_json_file(map_dir .. \"/meta.json\")\n    if not meta then\n        errors[#errors + 1] = merr\n    else\n        local meta_errors = schema.validate_meta(meta)\n        for _, e in ipairs(meta_errors) do\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"meta.json: \" .. e\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- drivers.json\n    local drivers, derr = parse_json_file(map_dir .. \"/drivers.json\")\n    if not drivers then\n        errors[#errors + 1] = derr\n    else\n        local driver_errors = schema.validate_drivers(drivers)\n        for _, e in ipairs(driver_errors) do\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"drivers.json: \" .. e\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- boxes\n    local boxes, box_errors = load_boxes(map_dir)\n    for _, e in ipairs(box_errors) do\n        errors[#errors + 1] = e\n    end\n\n    -- cross-box checks (only if boxes loaded cleanly enough)\n    if #errors == 0 then\n        check_connections(boxes, errors)\n        check_branch_else(boxes, errors)\n\n        -- entry box must exist\n        if meta and meta.entry_box_id then\n            if not boxes[meta.entry_box_id] then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"meta.json entry_box_id '\" ..\n                    meta.entry_box_id .. \"' does not match any box file\"\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ main\nlocal function main(args)\n    local map_dir = args[1]\n    if map_dir == nil then\n        io.stderr:write(\"usage: luajit 002-validate-map.lua <map-dir>\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    local errors = validate_map(map_dir)\n\n    if #errors == 0 then\n        print(\"OK: \" .. map_dir .. \" is valid\")\n        os.exit(0)\n    else\n        io.stderr:write(\"INVALID: \" .. map_dir .. \"\\n\")\n        for _, e in ipairs(errors) do\n            io.stderr:write(\"  error: \" .. e .. \"\\n\")\n        end\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\nmain(arg)\n",

          "content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Creates a new SoraMech map directory with all required files and a tmp/ symlink.\n# The map directory is created under ${DIR}/maps/<name>.\n# Run: scripts/create-map.sh <map-name> [maps-root]\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nMAP_NAME=\"${1}\"\nMAPS_ROOT=\"${2:-${DIR}/maps}\"\n\nif [ -z \"${MAP_NAME}\" ]; then\n    echo \"usage: create-map.sh <map-name> [maps-root]\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nMAP_DIR=\"${MAPS_ROOT}/${MAP_NAME}\"\n\nif [ -d \"${MAP_DIR}\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: map directory already exists: ${MAP_DIR}\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# create directory structure\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/boxes\"\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/data\"\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/src\"\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/drivers\"\n\n# create /tmp target before symlinking — logs/ and cache/ live there at runtime\nTMP_TARGET=\"/tmp/soramech-${MAP_NAME}\"\nmkdir -p \"${TMP_TARGET}\"\n\n# tmp/ is a symlink to /tmp/soramech-<name>/ so ephemeral files stay in RAM\nln -s \"${TMP_TARGET}\" \"${MAP_DIR}/tmp\"\n\n# write meta.json with placeholders\ncat > \"${MAP_DIR}/meta.json\" << METAJSON\n{\n  \"name\": \"${MAP_NAME}\",\n  \"description\": \"\",\n  \"entry_box_id\": \"\"\n}\nMETAJSON\n\n# write drivers.json pointing at the built-in driver scripts in the soramech root\ncat > \"${MAP_DIR}/drivers.json\" << DRIVERSJSON\n{\n  \".lua\": \"${DIR}/drivers/lua.sh\",\n  \".c\":   \"${DIR}/drivers/c.sh\",\n  \".sh\":  \"${DIR}/drivers/bash.sh\"\n}\nDRIVERSJSON\n\necho \"created: ${MAP_DIR}\"\necho \"next: edit meta.json to set entry_box_id, then add boxes in ${MAP_DIR}/boxes/\"\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/scripts/create-map.sh"

  "toolUseResult":{
    "content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Creates a new SoraMech map directory with all required files and a tmp/ symlink.\n# The map directory is created under ${DIR}/maps/<name>.\n# Run: scripts/create-map.sh <map-name> [maps-root]\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nMAP_NAME=\"${1}\"\nMAPS_ROOT=\"${2:-${DIR}/maps}\"\n\nif [ -z \"${MAP_NAME}\" ]; then\n    echo \"usage: create-map.sh <map-name> [maps-root]\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nMAP_DIR=\"${MAPS_ROOT}/${MAP_NAME}\"\n\nif [ -d \"${MAP_DIR}\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: map directory already exists: ${MAP_DIR}\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# create directory structure\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/boxes\"\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/data\"\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/src\"\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/drivers\"\n\n# create /tmp target before symlinking — logs/ and cache/ live there at runtime\nTMP_TARGET=\"/tmp/soramech-${MAP_NAME}\"\nmkdir -p \"${TMP_TARGET}\"\n\n# tmp/ is a symlink to /tmp/soramech-<name>/ so ephemeral files stay in RAM\nln -s \"${TMP_TARGET}\" \"${MAP_DIR}/tmp\"\n\n# write meta.json with placeholders\ncat > \"${MAP_DIR}/meta.json\" << METAJSON\n{\n  \"name\": \"${MAP_NAME}\",\n  \"description\": \"\",\n  \"entry_box_id\": \"\"\n}\nMETAJSON\n\n# write drivers.json pointing at the built-in driver scripts in the soramech root\ncat > \"${MAP_DIR}/drivers.json\" << DRIVERSJSON\n{\n  \".lua\": \"${DIR}/drivers/lua.sh\",\n  \".c\":   \"${DIR}/drivers/c.sh\",\n  \".sh\":  \"${DIR}/drivers/bash.sh\"\n}\nDRIVERSJSON\n\necho \"created: ${MAP_DIR}\"\necho \"next: edit meta.json to set entry_box_id, then add boxes in ${MAP_DIR}/boxes/\"\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/scripts/create-map.sh",
    "structuredPatch":[]
  }
}

    "newString":"-- {{{ check_connections\nlocal function check_connections(boxes, errors)\n    -- every connection must be stored identically in both endpoint box files.\n    -- each connection carries from_box, from_output, to_box, to_input.\n    -- the validator looks for an exact 4-field match in the target box.\n    for id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        local conns = box.connections or {}\n        for _, c in ipairs(conns) do\n            if c.from_box ~= id then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection has from_box='\" ..\n                    tostring(c.from_box) .. \"' but lives in box '\" .. id .. \"'\"\n            end\n\n            local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n            if target == nil then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection to unknown box '\" ..\n                    tostring(c.to_box) .. \"'\"\n            else\n                -- find exact match in target: all four fields must agree\n                local found = false\n                for _, tc in ipairs(target.connections or {}) do\n                    if tc.from_box    == c.from_box   and\n                       tc.from_output == c.from_output and\n                       tc.to_box      == c.to_box      and\n                       tc.to_input    == c.to_input    then\n                        found = true\n                        break\n                    end\n                end\n                if not found then\n                    errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection \" ..\n                        c.from_box .. \".\" .. c.from_output ..\n                        \" -> \" .. c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input ..\n                        \" not found in target box file (both ends must store the same record)\"\n                end\n            end\n        end\n    end\nend\n-- }}}",
    "originalFile":"-- CLI tool that validates a SoraMech map directory for correctness.\n-- Checks schema of all box files, validates connection endpoints exist\n-- and agree on both ends, and running from any directory by finding libs relative to DIR\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal json   = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal schema = require(\"001-schema\")\n\n-- {{{ read_file\nlocal function read_file(path)\n    local f, ferr = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then return nil, ferr end\n    local contents = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    return contents\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ parse_json_file\nlocal function parse_json_file(path)\n    local raw, ferr = read_file(path)\n    if not raw obj\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ load_boxes\nlocal function load_boxes(map_dir)\n    -- returns table of {id -> box_table} and a list of errors\n    local boxes = {}\n    local errors = {}\n    local boxes_dir = map_dir .. \"/boxes\"\n\n    local handle = io.popen(\"ls \" .. boxes_dir .. \"/*.json 2>/dev/null\")\n    if not handle then\n        return boxes, { \"cannot list \" .. boxes_dir }\n    end\n    local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n    handle:close()\n\n    for path in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n        local box, berr = parse_json_file(path)\n        if not box then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = berr\n        else\n            local box_errors = schema.validate_box(box)\n            if #box_errors > 0 then\n                for _, e in ipairs(box_errors) do\n }}}\n\n-- {{{ check_connections\nlocal function check_connections(boxes, errors)\n    -- every connection must have a reciprocal entry in the target box\n    for id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        local conns = box.connections or {}\n        for _, c in ipairs(conns) do\n            local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n            if target == nil then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box  found = true\n                        break\n                    end\n                end\n                if not found then\n                    errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"' -> '\" check_branch_else\nlocal function check_branch_else(boxes, errors)\n    -- branch boxes must have an \"else\" port (enforced by schema, re-checked here\n    -- for clarity), and local has_else_wire = false\n        for _, p in ipairs(box.ports or {}) do\n            if p.name == \"else\" then\n                has_else_port = true\n            end\n        end\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_port == \"else\" then\n                has_else_wire = true\n            end\n        end\n\n        if not has_else_port then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"branch box '\" .. id .. \"' missing 'else' port\"\n        end\n\n        -- if else is unwired, the box must have retry_vary upstream to be valid;\n        -- we cannot check retry_vary here without traversing upstream, so we emit\n        -- a warning rather than a hard error — the runner will enforce at execute time\n        if has_else_port and not has_else_wire then\n meta, merr = parse_json_file(map_dir .. \"/meta.json\")\n    if not meta then\n        errors[#errors + 1] = merr\n    else\n        local meta_errors = schema.validate_meta(meta)\n        for _, e in
