}}}",
          "new_string":"-- {{{ check_connections\nlocal function check_connections(boxes, errors)\n    -- every connection must be stored identically in both endpoint box files.\n    -- each connection carries from_box, from_output, to_box, to_input.\n    -- the validator looks for an exact 4-field match in the target box.\n    for id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        local conns = box.connections or {}\n        for _, c in ipairs(conns) do\n            if c.from_box ~= id then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection has from_box='\" ..\n                    tostring(c.from_box) .. \"' but lives in box '\" .. id .. \"'\"\n            end\n\n            local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n            if target == nil then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection to unknown box '\" ..\n                    tostring(c.to_box) .. \"'\"\n            else\n                -- find exact match in target: all four fields must agree\n                local found = false\n                for _, tc in ipairs(target.connections or {}) do\n                    if tc.from_box    == c.from_box   and\n                       tc.from_output == c.from_output and\n                       tc.to_box      == c.to_box      and\n                       tc.to_input    == c.to_input    then\n                        found = true\n                        break\n                    end\n                end\n                if not found then\n                    errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection \" ..\n                        c.from_box .. \".\" .. c.from_output ..\n                        \" -> \" .. c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input ..\n                        \" not found in target box file (both ends must store the same record)\"\n                end\n            end\n        end\n    end\nend\n-- }}}",

    "originalFile":"-- Schema definitions and validators for SoraMech map files.\n-- Validates box files, meta.json, and drivers.json against the spec\n-- in docs/001-architecture.md. Used by both the runner and the server\n-- before any file is written to disk.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ valid_kinds\nlocal valid_kinds = { call = true, branch = true, data = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ valid_ops\nlocal valid_ops = {\n    eq = true, lt = true, gt = true,\n    lte = true, gte = true, contains = true, matches = true\n}\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ err\nlocal function err(errors, msg)\n    errors[#errors + 1] = msg\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_port\nlocal function validate_port(port, i, errors)\n    -- \"else\" port has no predicate; all others require one\n    if port.name == nil then\n        err(errors, \"port[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'name'\")\n        return\n    end\n    if port.name == \"else\" then return end\n    if port.predicate == nil then\n        err(errors, \"port '\" .. port.name .. \"' missing predicate (only 'else' may omit it)\")\n        return\n    end\n    local p = port.predicate\n    if p.op == nil then\n        err(errors, \"port '\" .. port.name .. \"' predicate missing 'op'\")\n    elseif not valid_ops[p.op] then\n        err(errors, \"port '\" .. port.name .. \"' predicate has unknown op '\" .. p.op .. \"'\")\n    end\n    if p.value == nil then\n        err(errors, \"port '\" .. port.name .. \"' predicate missing 'value'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_connection\nlocal function validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- each connection links one output port to one input port on another box\n    if c.from_output == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_output'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_port_connection\nlocal function validate_port_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- branch box connections reference a named port instead of from_output\n    if c.from_port == nil then\n        err(errors, \"branch connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_port'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"branch connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"branch connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_box\nfunction M.validate_box(box)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(box) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"box must be a table\" }\n    end\n\n    if box.id == nil or type(box.id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'id'\")\n    end\n    if box.label == nil or type(box.label) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'label'\")\n    end\n    if box.kind == nil or not valid_kinds[box.kind] then\n        err(errors, \"missing or invalid 'kind' (must be call, branch, or data)\")\n    end\n\n    if box.kind == \"call\" then\n        if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"call box missing 'ref'\")\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        if box.outputs ~= nil and type(box.outputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'outputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n\n    elseif box.kind == \"branch\" then\n        if box.inputs == nil or type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"branch box missing 'inputs'\")\n        end\n        if box.ports == nil or type(box.ports) ~= \"table\" or #box.ports == 0 then\n            err(errors, \"branch box missing 'ports' array\")\n        else\n            local has_else = false\n            for i, p in ipairs(box.ports) do\n                validate_port(p, i, errors)\n                if p.name == \"else\" then has_else = true end\n            end\n            if not has_else then\n                err(errors, \"branch box missing required 'else' port\")\n            end\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_port_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a table\")\n        elseif box.ui.x == nil or box.ui.y == nil then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must have 'x' and 'y' fields\")\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or type(meta.name) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'name'\")\n    end\n    if meta.entry_box_id == nil or type(meta.entry_box_id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'entry_box_id'\")\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_drivers\nfunction M.validate_drivers(drivers)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(drivers) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"drivers.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    for ext, path in pairs(drivers) do\n        if type(ext) ~= \"string\" or ext:sub(1, 1) ~= \".\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver key '\" .. tostring(ext) .. \"' must be a dot-prefixed extension\")\n        end\n        if type(path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver value for '\" .. ext .. \"' must be a string path\")\n        end\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",

    "originalFile":"-- Schema definitions and validators for SoraMech map files.\n-- Validates box files, meta.json, and drivers.json against the spec\n-- in docs/001-architecture.md. Used by both the runner and the server\n-- before any file is written to disk.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ valid_kinds\nlocal valid_kinds = { call = true, branch = true, data = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ valid_ops\nlocal valid_ops = {\n    eq = true, lt = true, gt = true,\n    lte = true, gte = true, contains = true, matches = true\n}\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ err\nlocal function err(errors, msg)\n    errors[#errors + 1] = msg\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_port\nlocal function validate_port(port, i, errors)\n    -- \"else\" port has no predicate; all others require one\n    if port.name == nil then\n        err(errors, \"port[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'name'\")\n        return\n    end\n    if port.name == \"else\" then return end\n    if port.predicate == nil then\n        err(errors, \"port '\" .. port.name .. \"' missing predicate (only 'else' may omit it)\")\n        return\n    end\n    local p = port.predicate\n    if p.op == nil then\n        err(errors, \"port '\" .. port.name .. \"' predicate missing 'op'\")\n    elseif not valid_ops[p.op] then\n        err(errors, \"port '\" .. port.name .. \"' predicate has unknown op '\" .. p.op .. \"'\")\n    end\n    if p.value == nil then\n        err(errors, \"port '\" .. port.name .. \"' predicate missing 'value'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_connection\nlocal function validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- all four fields must be present; both endpoint files store the same record\n    if c.from_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.from_output == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_output'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_port_connection\nlocal function validate_port_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- branch box connections reference a named port instead of from_output\n    if c.from_port == nil then\n        err(errors, \"branch connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_port'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"branch connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"branch connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_box\nfunction M.validate_box(box)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(box) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"box must be a table\" }\n    end\n\n    if box.id == nil or type(box.id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'id'\")\n    end\n    if box.label == nil or type(box.label) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'label'\")\n    end\n    if box.kind == nil or not valid_kinds[box.kind] then\n        err(errors, \"missing or invalid 'kind' (must be call, branch, or data)\")\n    end\n\n    if box.kind == \"call\" then\n        if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"call box missing 'ref'\")\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        if box.outputs ~= nil and type(box.outputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'outputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n\n    elseif box.kind == \"branch\" then\n        if box.inputs == nil or type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"branch box missing 'inputs'\")\n        end\n        if box.ports == nil or type(box.ports) ~= \"table\" or #box.ports == 0 then\n            err(errors, \"branch box missing 'ports' array\")\n        else\n            local has_else = false\n            for i, p in ipairs(box.ports) do\n                validate_port(p, i, errors)\n                if p.name == \"else\" then has_else = true end\n            end\n            if not has_else then\n                err(errors, \"branch box missing required 'else' port\")\n            end\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_port_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a table\")\n        elseif box.ui.x == nil or box.ui.y == nil then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must have 'x' and 'y' fields\")\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or type(meta.name) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'name'\")\n    end\n    if meta.entry_box_id == nil or type(meta.entry_box_id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'entry_box_id'\")\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_drivers\nfunction M.validate_drivers(drivers)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(drivers) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"drivers.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    for ext, path in pairs(drivers) do\n        if type(ext) ~= \"string\" or ext:sub(1, 1) ~= \".\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver key '\" .. tostring(ext) .. \"' must be a dot-prefixed extension\")\n        end\n        if type(path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver value for '\" .. ext .. \"' must be a string path\")\n        end\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",

    "userModified":false,
    "newString":"  \"connections\": [\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"unique-string\",\n      \"from_output\": \"result\",\n      \"to_box\": \"next-box-id\",\n      \"to_input\": \"text\"\n    }\n  ],",
    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — Architecture\n\n## Three programs, one data format\n\nSoraMech is three independent programs that share a common on-disk format:\nthe map directory. None of the three knows about the others at runtime.\n\n```\n  Browser (index.html)\n       |  HTTP (file CRUD)\n       v\n  soramech-server.lua          [map directory]\n                               maps/<name>/\n                                 boxes/\n                                 data/\n                                 drivers.json\n                                 meta.json\n                                 tmp/ -> /tmp/<name>/\n       ^\n       | reads & writes\n  soramech-runner.lua\n```\n\n### soramech-server.lua\n\nThin HTTP proxy. Receives JSON requests from the browser and translates\nthem into file reads and writes on the map directory. No logic beyond\npath validation and basic consistency checks (e.g., reject a delete if\nthe box is still referenced by another box's connection list).\n\nStarted with: `luajit soramech-server.lua <maps-root> [port]`\nDefault port: 7700\n\nEndpoints (all operate on map files):\n  GET  /maps                        list maps\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes           list box IDs\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      read box file\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      write box file\n  DELETE /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>    remove box (validates no dangling refs)\n  GET  /maps/<name>/data/<name>     read data file\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/data/<name>     write data file\n  GET  /maps/<name>/drivers         read drivers.json\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/drivers         write drivers.json\n  GET  /maps/<name>/meta            read meta.json\n\n### soramech-runner.lua\n\nFSM execution engine. Loads a map directory, validates the graph, then\nexecutes boxes in dependency order. Each box invocation is wrapped in a\n`task_fn(inputs) -> outputs` call — matching the 3d-rts thread pool's\naction chain signature for future threading compatibility.\n\nStarted with: `luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>`\n\nExecution steps:\n  1. Read all box files from boxes/\n  2. Validate: all connection endpoints exist, branch \"else\" handled\n  3. Determine entry box from meta.json\n  4. Execute: resolve inputs, invoke driver, collect outputs, fire wires\n  5. On completion, write last-run snapshot to tmp/last-run.json\n\n### index.html\n\nStatic HTML + vanilla JS. Infinite-scroll canvas. Box diagram editor.\nTalks to soramech-server.lua for all file operations. No run button —\nthe user starts the runner separately from the terminal.\n\n## Map directory format\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/\n  meta.json          — { name, description, entry_box_id }\n  drivers.json       — { \".lua\": \"drivers/lua.sh\", \".c\": \"drivers/c.sh\", ... }\n  boxes/\n    <id>.json        — one file per box (see Box file format below)\n  data/\n    <name>.json      — lua table as JSON; sections have \"constant\": bool\n  drivers/\n    lua.sh           — built-in lua driver (shipped with soramech)\n    c.sh             — built-in C driver\n    bash.sh          — built-in bash driver\n  tmp/               — symlink to /tmp/<name>/\n    last-run.json    — snapshot of last run (ephemeral)\n    logs/            — run logs\n    cache/           — compiled binaries (C driver cache)\n```\n\n## Box file format\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"unique-string\",\n  \"label\": \"Human name\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\",\n  \"fn\": \"trim\",\n  \"inputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"text\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"outputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"result\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"connections\": [\n    {\n      \"from_output\": \"result\",\n      \"to_box\": \"next-box-id\",\n      \"to_input\": \"text\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 120, \"y\": 340 }\n}\n```\n\nFor branch boxes (`\"kind\": \"branch\"`):\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"classify\",\n  \"kind\": \"branch\",\n  \"inputs\": [{ \"name\": \"value\", \"type\": \"string\" }],\n  \"ports\": [\n    { \"name\": \"rogue\", \"predicate\": { \"op\": \"eq\", \"value\": \"rogue\" } },\n    { \"name\": \"wizard\", \"predicate\": { \"op\": \"eq\", \"value\": \"wizard\" } },\n    { \"name\": \"else\" }\n  ],\n  \"connections\": [...]\n}\n```\n\nConnections are written to BOTH endpoint box files. The runner validates\nat load time that both ends agree. Disagreement is a hard error.\n\n## Language driver interface\n\nDrivers are shell scripts. The engine invokes them as:\n\n  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg1> <arg2> ...]\n\nOutputs are returned as JSON on stdout. Exit code non-zero = box failure.\nSee docs/003-driver-system.md for the full driver contract.\n\n## Execution model (v1 — synchronous)\n\nThe runner walks the graph depth-first from the entry box. Each box call:\n\n  1. Collect inputs: read wired output values from predecessor boxes\n  2. Invoke driver: shell out to the appropriate driver script\n  3. Collect outputs: parse JSON from driver stdout\n  4. Store outputs: held in runner memory, keyed by box id + output name\n  5. Fire connections: enqueue boxes whose input dependencies are now met\n\nEach step is wrapped in a `task_fn` boundary so the runner can be\nthreaded later by substituting the synchronous executor with one backed\nby effil-jit or the custom thread pool from the 3d-rts project.\n\n## Data files\n\nPersistent data lives in data/<name>.json. Format:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"constant\": false,\n  \"fields\": {\n    \"history\": [],\n    \"config\": { \"constant\": true, \"value\": { \"model\": \"soramind-default\" } }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nTop-level `constant: true` makes the whole file read-only. Individual\nfields can be flagged constant within an otherwise mutable file.\n\nEphemeral state (scratch tables, logs, last-run snapshot) goes to tmp/,\nwhich is a symlink to /tmp/<map-name>/. It survives the run but not a\nreboot — intentionally.\n",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/docs/001-architecture.md",

      }]
  }

    "oldString":"-- {{{ check_connections\nlocal function check_connections(boxes, errors)\n    -- every connection must be stored identically in both endpoint box files.\n    -- each connection carries from_box, from_output, to_box, to_input.\n    -- the validator looks for an exact 4-field match in the target box.\n    for id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        local conns = box.connections or {}\n        for _, c in ipairs(conns) do\n            if c.from_box ~= id then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection has from_box='\" ..\n                    tostring(c.from_box) .. \"' but lives in box '\" .. id .. \"'\"\n            end\n\n            local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n            if target == nil then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection to unknown box '\" ..\n                    tostring(c.to_box) .. \"'\"\n            else\n                -- find exact match in target: all four fields must agree\n                local found = false\n                for _, tc in ipairs(target.connections or {}) do\n                    if tc.from_box    == c.from_box   and\n                       tc.from_output == c.from_output and\n                       tc.to_box      == c.to_box      and\n                       tc.to_input    == c.to_input    then\n                        found = true\n                        break\n                    end\n                end\n                if not found then\n                    errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection \" ..\n                        c.from_box .. \".\" .. c.from_output ..\n                        \" -> \" .. c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input ..\n                        \" not found in target box file (both ends must store the same record)\"\n                end\n            end\n        end\n    end\nend\n-- }}}",
    "userModified":false,
    "newString":"-- {{{ check_connections\nlocal function check_connections(boxes, errors)\n    -- each connection is stored in BOTH endpoint box files as the same 4-field record.\n    -- we only process connections where from_box == this box's id (outgoing connections).\n    -- incoming reciprocal records (from_box != id) are skipped here; they are validated\n    -- implicitly when we process the source box.\n    for id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        local conns = box.connections or {}\n        for _, c in ipairs(conns) do\n            if c.from_box ~= id then\n                -- this is the reciprocal copy stored for reference; skip\n                goto next_conn\n            end\n\n            local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n            if target == nil then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection to unknown box '\" ..\n                    tostring(c.to_box) .. \"'\"\n            else\n                -- find exact match in target: all four fields must agree\n                local found = false\n                for _, tc in ipairs(target.connections or {}) do\n                    if tc.from_box    == c.from_box   and\n                       tc.from_output == c.from_output and\n                       tc.to_box      == c.to_box      and\n                       tc.to_input    == c.to_input    then\n                        found = true\n                        break\n                    end\n                end\n                if not found then\n                    errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection \" ..\n                        c.from_box .. \".\" .. c.from_output ..\n                        \" -> \" .. c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input ..\n                        \" not found in target box file (both ends must store the same record)\"\n                end\n            end\n\n            ::next_conn::\n        end\n    end\nend\n-- }}}",
    "originalFile":"-- CLI tool that validates a SoraMech map directory for correctness.\n-- Checks schema of all box files, validates connection endpoints exist\n-- and agree on both ends, and enforces branch box rules.\n-- Run: luajit src/002-validate-map.lua <map-dir>\n-- Exits 0 if valid, non-zero with error report if not.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\n-- allow running from any directory by finding libs relative to DIR\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal json   = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal schema = require(\"001-schema\")\n\n-- {{{ read_file\nlocal function read_file(path)\n    local f, ferr = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then return nil, ferr end\n    local contents = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    return contents\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ parse_json_file\nlocal function parse_json_file(path)\n    local raw, ferr = read_file(path)\n    if not raw then return nil, \"cannot open \" .. path .. \": \" .. ferr end\n    local obj, _, jerr = json.decode(raw)\n    if not obj then return nil, \"JSON error in \" .. path .. \": \" .. jerr end\n    return obj\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ load_boxes\nlocal function load_boxes(map_dir)\n    -- returns table of {id -> box_table} and a list of errors\n    local boxes = {}\n    local errors = {}\n    local boxes_dir = map_dir .. \"/boxes\"\n\n    local handle = io.popen(\"ls \" .. boxes_dir .. \"/*.json 2>/dev/null\")\n    if not handle then\n        return boxes, { \"cannot list \" .. boxes_dir }\n    end\n    local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n    handle:close()\n\n    for path in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n        local box, berr = parse_json_file(path)\n        if not box then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = berr\n        else\n            local box_errors = schema.validate_box(box)\n            if #box_errors > 0 then\n                for _, e in ipairs(box_errors) do\n                    errors[#errors + 1] = path .. \": \" .. e\n                end\n            else\n                boxes[box.id] = box\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    return boxes, errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ check_connections\nlocal function check_connections(boxes, errors)\n    -- every connection must be stored identically in both endpoint box files.\n    -- each connection carries from_box, from_output, to_box, to_input.\n    -- the validator looks for an exact 4-field match in the target box.\n    for id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        local conns = box.connections or {}\n        for _, c in ipairs(conns) do\n            if c.from_box ~= id then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection has from_box='\" ..\n                    tostring(c.from_box) .. \"' but lives in box '\" .. id .. \"'\"\n            end\n\n            local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n            if target == nil then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection to unknown box '\" ..\n                    tostring(c.to_box) .. \"'\"\n            else\n                -- find exact match in target: all four fields must agree\n                local found = false\n                for _, tc in ipairs(target.connections or {}) do\n                    if tc.from_box    == c.from_box   and\n                       tc.from_output == c.from_output and\n                       tc.to_box      == c.to_box      and\n                       tc.to_input    == c.to_input    then\n                        found = true\n                        break\n                    end\n                end\n                if not found then\n                    errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection \" ..\n                        c.from_box .. \".\" .. c.from_output ..\n                        \" -> \" .. c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input ..\n                        \" not found in target box file (both ends must store the same record)\"\n                end\n            end\n        end\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ check_branch_else\nlocal function check_branch_else(boxes, errors)\n    -- branch boxes must have an \"else\" port (enforced by schema, re-checked here\n    -- for clarity), and numeric/string-predicate branch boxes must wire \"else\"\n    for id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        if box.kind ~= \"branch\" then goto continue end\n\n        local has_else_port = false\n        local has_else_wire = false\n        for _, p in ipairs(box.ports or {}) do\n            if p.name == \"else\" then\n                has_else_port = true\n            end\n        end\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_port == \"else\" then\n                has_else_wire = true\n            end\n        end\n\n        if not has_else_port then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"branch box '\" .. id .. \"' missing 'else' port\"\n        end\n\n        -- if else is unwired, the box must have retry_vary upstream to be valid;\n        -- we cannot check retry_vary here without traversing upstream, so we emit\n        -- a warning rather than a hard error — the runner will enforce at execute time\n        if has_else_port and not has_else_wire then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"branch box '\" .. id ..\n                \"': 'else' port is unwired (valid only for LLM retry; runner will \" ..\n                \"require upstream box to have retry_vary defined)\"\n        end\n\n        ::continue::\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_map\nlocal function validate_map(map_dir)\n    local errors = {}\n\n    -- meta.json\n    local meta, merr = parse_json_file(map_dir .. \"/meta.json\")\n    if not meta then\n        errors[#errors + 1] = merr\n    else\n        local meta_errors = schema.validate_meta(meta)\n        for _, e in ipairs(meta_errors) do\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"meta.json: \" .. e\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- drivers.json\n    local drivers, derr = parse_json_file(map_dir .. \"/drivers.json\")\n    if not drivers then\n        errors[#errors + 1] = derr\n    else\n        local driver_errors = schema.validate_drivers(drivers)\n        for _, e in ipairs(driver_errors) do\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"drivers.json: \" .. e\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- boxes\n    local boxes, box_errors = load_boxes(map_dir)\n    for _, e in ipairs(box_errors) do\n        errors[#errors + 1] = e\n    end\n\n    -- cross-box checks (only if boxes loaded cleanly enough)\n    if #errors == 0 then\n        check_connections(boxes, errors)\n        check_branch_else(boxes, errors)\n\n        -- entry box must exist\n        if meta and meta.entry_box_id then\n            if not boxes[meta.entry_box_id] then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"meta.json entry_box_id '\" ..\n                    meta.entry_box_id .. \"' does not match any box file\"\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ main\nlocal function main(args)\n    local map_dir = args[1]\n    if map_dir == nil then\n        io.stderr:write(\"usage: luajit 002-validate-map.lua <map-dir>\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    local errors = validate_map(map_dir)\n\n    if #errors == 0 then\n        print(\"OK: \" .. map_dir .. \" is valid\")\n        os.exit(0)\n    else\n        io.stderr:write(\"INVALID: \" .. map_dir .. \"\\n\")\n        for _, e in ipairs(errors) do\n            io.stderr:write(\"  error: \" .. e .. \"\\n\")\n        end\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\nmain(arg)\n",

The runner has no mechanism to invoke functions\n10\tin any language. There is no defined contract for how a driver receives\n11\targuments or returns values.\n12\t\n13\t## Intended behavior\n14\t\n15\tA drivers/ directory exists alongside soramech-runner.lua containing\n16\tthree built-in driver scripts: lua.sh, c.sh, and bash.sh. Each follows\n17\tthe same interface. The runner invokes any driver identically regardless\n18\tof language. A user can write a fourth driver for any language by copying\n19\tthe pattern.\n20\t\n21\tDriver invocation contract:\n22\t  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n23\t\n24\tAll args are strings. Structured values are JSON strings. Driver writes\n25\tone JSON value (or JSON array for tuples) to stdout on success. Exits\n26\tnon-zero on failure, error message to stderr.\n27\t\n28\t## Suggested implementation steps\n29\t\n30\t1. Write drivers/lua.sh — sources the target .lua file via luajit,\n31\t   calls the named function with decoded JSON args, encodes return value\n32\t   to JSON on stdout. Single-value and multi-value (tuple) returns both\n33\t   produce a JSON array.\n34\t2. Write drivers/c.sh — checks mtime of .c file against cached binary\n35\t   in tmp/cache/. Compiles if stale (using gcc or cc, flags configurable\n36\t   via env). Invokes the binary with args as argv. Binary must write JSON\n37\t   to stdout per the contract.\n38\t3. Write drivers/bash.sh — sources the .sh file, calls the named\n39\t   function with args as positional params. Function must echo JSON to\n40\t   stdout.\n41\t4. Write a small test map maps/driver-test/ with one box per driver type\n42\t   to verify each driver works end-to-end before the runner is built.\n43\t5. Document the driver contract in drivers/README (plain text, short).\n44\t\n45\t## Related documents\n46\t\n47\t- docs/003-driver-system.md — full driver system spec\n48\t- issues/101 — map scaffold (tmp/cache/ directory created there)\n49\t- issues/103 — runner uses these drivers once they exist\n50\t\n51\t## Notes\n52\t\n53\tFor lua.sh: luajit must be on PATH. The script should fail with a clear\n54\terror if luajit is not found, not silently produce wrong output.\n55\t\n56\tFor c.sh: the cache key for compiled binaries is the absolute path of the\n57\tsource file. A sha1 or md5 of the path is sufficient; the binary is\n58\tstored as tmp/cache/<hash>. Stale check: stat both files, compare mtimes.\n59\t\n60\tFor bash.sh: functions in a sourced file may have side effects and access\n61\tthe filesystem. This is expected and correct — bash boxes are intentionally\n62\tless constrained than lua or C boxes.\n63\t\n64\tThe \"no special cases in the runner\" constraint means the runner must not\n65\thave any if-elseif chain on file extension. All dispatch goes through\n66\tthe driver table loaded from drivers.json.\n67\t",

    "file":{
      "content":"# 102 — Language driver interface\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo driver scripts exist. The runner has no mechanism to invoke functions\nin any language. There is no defined contract for how a driver receives\narguments or returns values.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA drivers/ directory exists alongside soramech-runner.lua containing\nthree built-in driver scripts: lua.sh, c.sh, and bash.sh. Each follows\nthe same interface. The runner invokes any driver identically regardless\nof language. A user can write a fourth driver for any language by copying\nthe pattern.\n\nDriver invocation contract:\n  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n\nAll args are strings. Structured values are JSON strings. Driver writes\none JSON value (or JSON array for tuples) to stdout on success. Exits\nnon-zero on failure, error message to stderr.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Write drivers/lua.sh — sources the target .lua file via luajit,\n   calls the named function with decoded JSON args, encodes return value\n   to JSON on stdout. Single-value and multi-value (tuple) returns both\n   produce a JSON array.\n2. Write drivers/c.sh — checks mtime of .c file against cached binary\n   in tmp/cache/. Compiles if stale (using gcc or cc, flags configurable\n   via env). Invokes the binary with args as argv. Binary must write JSON\n   to stdout per the contract.\n3. Write drivers/bash.sh — sources the .sh file, calls the named\n   function with args as positional params. Function must echo JSON to\n   stdout.\n4. Write a small test map maps/driver-test/ with one box per driver type\n   to verify each driver works end-to-end before the runner is built.\n5. Document the driver contract in drivers/README (plain text, short).\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/003-driver-system.md — full driver system spec\n- issues/101 — map scaffold (tmp/cache/ directory created there)\n- issues/103 — runner uses these drivers once they exist\n\n## Notes\n\nFor lua.sh: luajit must be on PATH. The script should fail with a clear\nerror if luajit is not found, not silently produce wrong output.\n\nFor c.sh: the cache key for compiled binaries is the absolute path of the\nsource file. A sha1 or md5 of the path is sufficient; the binary is\nstored as tmp/cache/<hash>. Stale check: stat both files, compare mtimes.\n\nFor bash.sh: functions in a sourced file may have side effects and access\nthe filesystem. This is expected and correct — bash boxes are intentionally\nless constrained than lua or C boxes.\n\nThe \"no special cases in the runner\" constraint means the runner must not\nhave any if-elseif chain on file extension. All dispatch goes through\nthe driver table loaded from drivers.json.\n",
      "startLine":1,
      "totalLines":67,
      "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/102-language-driver-interface.md",
      "numLines":67
    }
  }
}

then\n    echo \"lua.sh: missing file-path or fn-name\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif ! command -v luajit > /dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"lua.sh: luajit not found on PATH\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif [ ! -f \"${FILE_PATH}\" ]; then\n    echo \"lua.sh: file not found: ${FILE_PATH}\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# build a JSON array of the raw argument strings for passing into lua\nARGS_JSON=\"[\"\nSEP=\"\"\nfor ARG in \"$@\"; do\n    ARGS_JSON=\"${ARGS_JSON}${SEP}${ARG}\"\n    SEP=\",\"\ndone\nARGS_JSON=\"${ARGS_JSON}]\"\n\n# run luajit with the driver shim inline; the shim loads the module,\n# decodes arguments, calls the function, and encodes the result\nluajit - \"${FILE_PATH}\" \"${FN_NAME}\" \"${ARGS_JSON}\" << 'LUASHIM'\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\n\n-- read driver arguments\nlocal file_path = arg[1]\nlocal fn_name   = arg[2]\nlocal args_raw  = arg[3]\n\n-- locate libs (DIR symlink is not available inside heredoc; use the file's dir)\nlocal script_dir = file_path:match(\"^(.+)/[^/]+$\") or \".\"\npackage.path = script_dir .. \"/../../libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\n-- decode args array\nlocal args_table, _, jerr = json.decode(args_raw)\nif not args_table then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: failed to decode args JSON: \" .. tostring(jerr) .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- load the module\nlocal ok, mod = pcall(dofile, file_path)\nif not ok then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: error loading \" .. file_path .. \": \" .. tostring(mod) .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- resolve the function\nlocal fn = mod[fn_name]\nif type(fn) ~= \"function\" then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: no public function '\" .. fn_name .. \"' in \" .. file_path .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- decode each arg from JSON to lua value; strings are passed as-is\nlocal call_args = {}\nfor i, raw_arg in ipairs(args_table) do\n    local val, _, aerr = json.decode(raw_arg)\n    if aerr then\n        -- not valid JSON — treat as a plain string\n        call_args[i] = raw_arg\n    else\n        call_args[i] = val\n    end\nend\n\n-- call the function; collect all return values into a table\nlocal results = table.pack(fn(table.unpack(call_args)))\n\n-- encode results as a JSON array (each return value is one element)\nlocal encoded = {}\nfor i = 1, results.n do\n    encoded[i] = json.encode(results[i])\nend\nprint(json.encode(encoded))\nLUASHIM\n",

strings are passed as-is\nlocal call_args = {}\nfor i, raw_arg in ipairs(args_table) do\n    local val, _, aerr = json.decode(raw_arg)\n    if aerr then\n        -- not valid JSON — treat as a plain string\n        call_args[i] = raw_arg\n    else\n        call_args[i] = val\n    end\nend\n\n-- call the function; collect all return values into a table\nlocal results = table.pack(fn(table.unpack(call_args)))\n\n-- encode results as a JSON array (each return value is one element)\nlocal encoded = {}\nfor i = 1, results.n do\n    encoded[i] = json.encode(results[i])\nend\nprint(json.encode(encoded))\nLUASHIM\n",

          "content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# C language driver for SoraMech.\n# Compiles the .c file if the source is newer than the cached binary,\n# then invokes the binary with arguments. The binary must write a JSON\n# array to stdout per the driver contract.\n# Contract: <script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n# The fn-name is passed as argv[1] so the binary can dispatch to the right function.\n# Cache location: TMP_DIR/cache/<md5-of-absolute-path>\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nFILE_PATH=\"${1}\"\nFN_NAME=\"${2}\"\nARG_COUNT=\"${3}\"\nshift 3\n\nif [ -z \"${FILE_PATH}\" ] || [ -z \"${FN_NAME}\" ]; then\n    echo \"c.sh: missing file-path or fn-name\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif [ ! -f \"${FILE_PATH}\" ]; then\n    echo \"c.sh: file not found: ${FILE_PATH}\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# resolve to absolute path for stable cache key\nABS_PATH=$(realpath \"${FILE_PATH}\")\n\n# the map's tmp/cache dir lives relative to the file; walk up to find it\n# convention: src/ is one level below the map root, cache is in tmp/cache/\nMAP_ROOT=$(dirname \"$(dirname \"${ABS_PATH}\")\")\nCACHE_DIR=\"${MAP_ROOT}/tmp/cache\"\nmkdir -p \"${CACHE_DIR}\"\n\n# cache key: md5 of the absolute source path (not contents — path is stable per binary)\nCACHE_KEY=$(echo -n \"${ABS_PATH}\" | md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1)\nBINARY=\"${CACHE_DIR}/${CACHE_KEY}\"\n\n# compile if binary is missing or source is newer than the binary\nNEEDS_COMPILE=0\nif [ ! -f \"${BINARY}\" ]; then\n    NEEDS_COMPILE=1\nelif [ \"${ABS_PATH}\" -nt \"${BINARY}\" ]; then\n    NEEDS_COMPILE=1\nfi\n\nif [ \"${NEEDS_COMPILE}\" -eq 1 ]; then\n    CC=\"${CC:-gcc}\"\n    CFLAGS=\"${CFLAGS:--O2 -Wall}\"\n    \"${CC}\" ${CFLAGS} -o \"${BINARY}\" \"${ABS_PATH}\" 2>&1\n    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then\n        echo \"c.sh: compilation failed for ${FILE_PATH}\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\nfi\n\n# invoke binary: fn-name as first arg, then the caller's args\n\"${BINARY}\" \"${FN_NAME}\" \"$@\"\n",

  "toolUseResult":{
    "content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# C language driver for SoraMech.\n# Compiles the .c file if the source is newer than the cached binary,\n# then invokes the binary with arguments. The binary must write a JSON\n# array to stdout per the driver contract.\n# Contract: <script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n# The fn-name is passed as argv[1] so the binary can dispatch to the right function.\n# Cache location: TMP_DIR/cache/<md5-of-absolute-path>\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nFILE_PATH=\"${1}\"\nFN_NAME=\"${2}\"\nARG_COUNT=\"${3}\"\nshift 3\n\nif [ -z \"${FILE_PATH}\" ] || [ -z \"${FN_NAME}\" ]; then\n    echo \"c.sh: missing file-path or fn-name\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif [ ! -f \"${FILE_PATH}\" ]; then\n    echo \"c.sh: file not found: ${FILE_PATH}\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# resolve to absolute path for stable cache key\nABS_PATH=$(realpath \"${FILE_PATH}\")\n\n# the map's tmp/cache dir lives relative to the file; walk up to find it\n# convention: src/ is one level below the map root, cache is in tmp/cache/\nMAP_ROOT=$(dirname \"$(dirname \"${ABS_PATH}\")\")\nCACHE_DIR=\"${MAP_ROOT}/tmp/cache\"\nmkdir -p \"${CACHE_DIR}\"\n\n# cache key: md5 of the absolute source path (not contents — path is stable per binary)\nCACHE_KEY=$(echo -n \"${ABS_PATH}\" | md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1)\nBINARY=\"${CACHE_DIR}/${CACHE_KEY}\"\n\n# compile if binary is missing or source is newer than the binary\nNEEDS_COMPILE=0\nif [ ! -f \"${BINARY}\" ]; then\n    NEEDS_COMPILE=1\nelif [ \"${ABS_PATH}\" -nt \"${BINARY}\" ]; then\n    NEEDS_COMPILE=1\nfi\n\nif [ \"${NEEDS_COMPILE}\" -eq 1 ]; then\n    CC=\"${CC:-gcc}\"\n    CFLAGS=\"${CFLAGS:--O2 -Wall}\"\n    \"${CC}\" ${CFLAGS} -o \"${BINARY}\" \"${ABS_PATH}\" 2>&1\n    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then\n        echo \"c.sh: compilation failed for ${FILE_PATH}\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\nfi\n\n# invoke binary: fn-name as first arg, then the caller's args\n\"${BINARY}\" \"${FN_NAME}\" \"$@\"\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/drivers/c.sh",

      "content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Lua/LuaJIT language driver for SoraMech.\n# Loads a .lua module, calls the named function with JSON-decoded arguments,\n# and writes the return value(s) as a JSON array to stdout.\n# Contract: <script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nFILE_PATH=\"${1}\"\nFN_NAME=\"${2}\"\nARG_COUNT=\"${3}\"\nshift 3\n\nif [ -z \"${FILE_PATH}\" ] || [ -z \"${FN_NAME}\" ]; then\n    echo \"lua.sh: missing file-path or fn-name\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif ! command -v luajit > /dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"lua.sh: luajit not found on PATH\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif [ ! -f \"${FILE_PATH}\" ]; then\n    echo \"lua.sh: file not found: ${FILE_PATH}\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# build a JSON array of the raw argument strings for passing into lua\nARGS_JSON=\"[\"\nSEP=\"\"\nfor ARG in \"$@\"; do\n    ARGS_JSON=\"${ARGS_JSON}${SEP}${ARG}\"\n    SEP=\",\"\ndone\nARGS_JSON=\"${ARGS_JSON}]\"\n\n# run luajit with the driver shim inline; the shim loads the module,\n# decodes arguments, calls the function, and encodes the result\nluajit - \"${FILE_PATH}\" \"${FN_NAME}\" \"${ARGS_JSON}\" << 'LUASHIM'\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\n\n-- read driver arguments\nlocal file_path = arg[1]\nlocal fn_name   = arg[2]\nlocal args_raw  = arg[3]\n\n-- locate libs (DIR symlink is not available inside heredoc; use the file's dir)\nlocal script_dir = file_path:match(\"^(.+)/[^/]+$\") or \".\"\npackage.path = script_dir .. \"/../../libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\n-- decode args array\nlocal args_table, _, jerr = json.decode(args_raw)\nif not args_table then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: failed to decode args JSON: \" .. tostring(jerr) .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- load the module\nlocal ok, mod = pcall(dofile, file_path)\nif not ok then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: error loading \" .. file_path .. \": \" .. tostring(mod) .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- resolve the function\nlocal fn = mod[fn_name]\nif type(fn) ~= \"function\" then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: no public function '\" .. fn_name .. \"' in \" .. file_path .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- decode each arg from JSON to lua value; strings are passed as-is\nlocal call_args = {}\nfor i, raw_arg in ipairs(args_table) do\n    local val, _, aerr = json.decode(raw_arg)\n    if aerr then\n        -- not valid JSON — treat as a plain string\n        call_args[i] = raw_arg\n    else\n        call_args[i] = val\n    end\nend\n\n-- call the function; collect all return values into a table\nlocal results = table.pack(fn(table.unpack(call_args)))\n\n-- encode results as a JSON array (each return value is one element)\nlocal encoded = {}\nfor i = 1, results.n do\n    encoded[i] = json.encode(results[i])\nend\nprint(json.encode(encoded))\nLUASHIM\n",

          "content":"SoraMech Language Drivers\n=========================\n\nEach file here is a driver script. The SoraMech runner invokes any driver\nidentically, regardless of language. Adding support for a new language means\nadding one script to this directory and one entry in drivers.json.\n\nContract\n--------\n\nThe runner calls a driver as:\n\n  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n\n  file-path   absolute or relative path to the source file\n  fn-name     name of the function to call within that file\n  arg-count   number of arguments that follow\n  args        zero or more argument strings; structured values are JSON strings\n\nOn success:\n  - exit code 0\n  - stdout: a JSON array where each element is one return value\n    single-value functions: [\"result\"]\n    multi-value (tuple) functions: [\"val1\", \"val2\", ...]\n\nOn failure:\n  - exit code non-zero\n  - stderr: human-readable error message\n  - stdout: empty or ignored\n\nBuilt-in drivers\n----------------\n\n  lua.sh    — calls a function in a .lua module via luajit\n  bash.sh   — sources a .sh file and calls a bash function\n  c.sh      — compiles a .c file (caches binary in tmp/cache/) and runs it\n\nRegistering a driver\n--------------------\n\nIn the map's drivers.json:\n\n  { \".rs\": \"drivers/rust.sh\" }\n\nWrite drivers/rust.sh following the contract above. The runner has no\nknowledge of any language — it reads the extension, finds the script, calls it.\n\nWriting a driver\n----------------\n\nMinimum viable driver (bash pseudocode):\n\n  FILE=\"${1}\"   FN=\"${2}\"   N=\"${3}\"   shift 3\n  # compile / interpret FILE if needed\n  # invoke FN with \"$@\" as arguments\n  # print result as JSON array to stdout\n  # exit 0 on success, non-zero on failure\n\nThe arg-count field is informational. Drivers may use \"$@\" directly.\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/drivers/README"
        }
      }],

    "content":"-- Graph loader for the SoraMech runner.\n-- Reads a map directory into an in-memory graph structure and validates\n-- its integrity before execution begins. The graph is the runner's\n-- internal representation of the map.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal json   = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal schema = require(\"001-schema\")\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ read_json_file\nlocal function read_json_file(path)\n    local f, ferr = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then return nil, \"cannot open \" .. path .. \": \" .. ferr end\n    local raw = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    local obj, _, jerr = json.decode(raw)\n    if not obj then return nil, \"JSON error in \" .. path .. \": \" .. tostring(jerr) end\n    return obj\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ load_drivers\nlocal function load_drivers(map_dir)\n    -- map-local drivers take priority; fall back to global drivers alongside the runner\n    local local_path  = map_dir .. \"/drivers.json\"\n    local global_path = DIR .. \"/drivers.json\"\n\n    local drivers = {}\n\n    -- load global first so local can override\n    local gd, _ = read_json_file(global_path)\n    if gd then\n        for ext, path in pairs(gd) do drivers[ext] = path end\n    end\n\n    local ld, _ = read_json_file(local_path)\n    if ld then\n        for ext, path in pairs(ld) do drivers[ext] = path end\n    end\n\n    return drivers\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ list_box_files\nlocal function list_box_files(boxes_dir)\n    local files = {}\n    local handle = io.popen(\"ls \" .. boxes_dir .. \"/*.json 2>/dev/null\")\n    if not handle then return files end\n    local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n    handle:close()\n    for path in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n        files[#files + 1] = path\n    end\n    return files\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ extension_of\nlocal function extension_of(path)\n    return path:match(\"%.([^./]+)$\") and (\".\" .. path:match(\"%.([^./]+)$\")) or \"\"\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ detect_cycles\n-- depth-first search from start_id; branch boxes are cycle-break nodes\n-- (a cycle that passes through a branch box is the retry pattern — allowed)\nlocal function detect_cycles(boxes, start_id)\n    local visited  = {}\n    local in_stack = {}\n    local errors   = {}\n\n    local function dfs(id)\n        if in_stack[id] then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"cycle detected at box '\" .. id ..\n                \"' that does not pass through a branch box\"\n            return\n        end\n        if visited[id] then return end\n        visited[id]  = true\n        in_stack[id] = true\n\n        local box = boxes[id]\n        if not box then\n            in_stack[id] = false\n            return\n        end\n\n        -- branch boxes break cycles — stop DFS at them (retry loops are valid)\n        if box.kind == \"branch\" then\n            in_stack[id] = false\n            return\n        end\n\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box == id then\n                dfs(c.to_box)\n            end\n        end\n\n        in_stack[id] = false\n    end\n\n    dfs(start_id)\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ load_map\nfunction M.load_map(map_dir)\n    local errors = {}\n\n    -- meta.json\n    local meta, merr = read_json_file(map_dir .. \"/meta.json\")\n    if not meta then\n        return nil, { merr }\n    end\n    local meta_errs = schema.validate_meta(meta)\n    for _, e in ipairs(meta_errs) do errors[#errors + 1] = \"meta.json: \" .. e end\n\n    -- drivers\n    local drivers = load_drivers(map_dir)\n\n    -- boxes\n    local boxes = {}\n    local box_files = list_box_files(map_dir .. \"/boxes\")\n    for _, path in ipairs(box_files) do\n        local box, berr = read_json_file(path)\n        if not box then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = berr\n        else\n            local box_errs = schema.validate_box(box)\n            if #box_errs > 0 then\n                for _, e in ipairs(box_errs) do\n                    errors[#errors + 1] = path .. \": \" .. e\n                end\n            else\n                boxes[box.id] = box\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if #errors > 0 then return nil, errors end\n\n    local graph = {\n        meta    = meta,\n        boxes   = boxes,\n        entry   = meta.entry_box_id,\n        drivers = drivers,\n        map_dir = map_dir,\n    }\n\n    return graph, {}\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_graph\nfunction M.validate_graph(graph)\n    local errors = {}\n    local boxes  = graph.boxes\n    local drivers = graph.drivers\n\n    -- entry box must exist\n    if not boxes[graph.entry] then\n        errors[#errors + 1] = \"entry_box_id '\" .. tostring(graph.entry) ..\n            \"' does not match any box\"\n    end\n\n    for id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        -- connection integrity: reciprocal check (outgoing connections only)\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box ~= id then goto next_conn end\n\n            local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n            if target == nil then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id ..\n                    \"': connection to unknown box '\" .. tostring(c.to_box) .. \"'\"\n                goto next_conn\n            end\n\n            local found = false\n            for _, tc in ipairs(target.connections or {}) do\n                if tc.from_box    == c.from_box   and\n                   tc.from_output == c.from_output and\n                   tc.to_box      == c.to_box      and\n                   tc.to_input    == c.to_input    then\n                    found = true\n                    break\n                end\n            end\n            if not found then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection \" ..\n                    c.from_box .. \".\" .. (c.from_output or c.from_port) ..\n                    \" -> \" .. c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input ..\n                    \" not reciprocated in target\"\n            end\n\n            ::next_conn::\n        end\n\n        -- driver must exist for call boxes with a ref\n        if box.kind == \"call\" and box.ref then\n            local ext = extension_of(box.ref)\n            -- binary callers (no fn) don't need a driver — they are the driver\n            if box.fn and ext ~= \"\" and not drivers[ext] then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id ..\n                    \"': no driver defined for extension '\" .. ext .. \"'\"\n            end\n        end\n\n        -- branch box: else port must exist; unwired else is warned (not errored here)\n        if box.kind == \"branch\" then\n            local has_else = false\n            for _, p in ipairs(box.ports or {}) do\n                if p.name == \"else\" then has_else = true end\n            end\n            if not has_else then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"branch box '\" .. id .. \"' missing 'else' port\"\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- cycle detection from entry box\n    if boxes[graph.entry] then\n        local cycle_errors = detect_cycles(boxes, graph.entry)\n        for _, e in ipairs(cycle_errors) do\n            errors[#errors + 1] = e\n        end\n    end\n\n    return #errors == 0, errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/003-loader.lua",

  }
}

        "input":{
          "content":"-- Graph loader for the SoraMech runner.\n-- Reads a map directory into an in-memory graph structure and validates\n-- its integrity before execution begins. The graph is the runner's\n-- internal representation of the map.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal json   = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal schema = require(\"001-schema\")\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ read_json_file\nlocal function read_json_file(path)\n    local f, ferr = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then return nil, \"cannot open \" .. path .. \": \" .. ferr end\n    local raw = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    local obj, _, jerr = json.decode(raw)\n    if not obj then return nil, \"JSON error in \" .. path .. \": \" .. tostring(jerr) end\n    return obj\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ load_drivers\nlocal function load_drivers(map_dir)\n    -- map-local drivers take priority; fall back to global drivers alongside the runner\n    local local_path  = map_dir .. \"/drivers.json\"\n    local global_path = DIR .. \"/drivers.json\"\n\n    local drivers = {}\n\n    -- load global first so local can override\n    local gd, _ = read_json_file(global_path)\n    if gd then\n        for ext, path in pairs(gd) do drivers[ext] = path end\n    end\n\n    local ld, _ = read_json_file(local_path)\n    if ld then\n        for ext, path in pairs(ld) do drivers[ext] = path end\n    end\n\n    return drivers\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ list_box_files\nlocal function list_box_files(boxes_dir)\n    local files = {}\n    local handle = io.popen(\"ls \" .. boxes_dir .. \"/*.json 2>/dev/null\")\n    if not handle then return files end\n    local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n    handle:close()\n    for path in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n        files[#files + 1] = path\n    end\n    return files\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ extension_of\nlocal function extension_of(path)\n    return path:match(\"%.([^./]+)$\") and (\".\" .. path:match(\"%.([^./]+)$\")) or \"\"\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ detect_cycles\n-- depth-first search from start_id; branch boxes are cycle-break nodes\n-- (a cycle that passes through a branch box is the retry pattern — allowed)\nlocal function detect_cycles(boxes, start_id)\n    local visited  = {}\n    local in_stack = {}\n    local errors   = {}\n\n    local function dfs(id)\n        if in_stack[id] then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"cycle detected at box '\" .. id ..\n                \"' that does not pass through a branch box\"\n            return\n        end\n        if visited[id] then return end\n        visited[id]  = true\n        in_stack[id] = true\n\n        local box = boxes[id]\n        if not box then\n            in_stack[id] = false\n            return\n        end\n\n        -- branch boxes break cycles — stop DFS at them (retry loops are valid)\n        if box.kind == \"branch\" then\n            in_stack[id] = false\n            return\n        end\n\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box == id then\n                dfs(c.to_box)\n            end\n        end\n\n        in_stack[id] = false\n    end\n\n    dfs(start_id)\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ load_map\nfunction M.load_map(map_dir)\n    local errors = {}\n\n    -- meta.json\n    local meta, merr = read_json_file(map_dir .. \"/meta.json\")\n    if not meta then\n        return nil, { merr }\n    end\n    local meta_errs = schema.validate_meta(meta)\n    for _, e in ipairs(meta_errs) do errors[#errors + 1] = \"meta.json: \" .. e end\n\n    -- drivers\n    local drivers = load_drivers(map_dir)\n\n    -- boxes\n    local boxes = {}\n    local box_files = list_box_files(map_dir .. \"/boxes\")\n    for _, path in ipairs(box_files) do\n        local box, berr = read_json_file(path)\n        if not box then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = berr\n        else\n            local box_errs = schema.validate_box(box)\n            if #box_errs > 0 then\n                for _, e in ipairs(box_errs) do\n                    errors[#errors + 1] = path .. \": \" .. e\n                end\n            else\n                boxes[box.id] = box\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if #errors > 0 then return nil, errors end\n\n    local graph = {\n        meta    = meta,\n        boxes   = boxes,\n        entry   = meta.entry_box_id,\n        drivers = drivers,\n        map_dir = map_dir,\n    }\n\n    return graph, {}\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_graph\nfunction M.validate_graph(graph)\n    local errors = {}\n    local boxes  = graph.boxes\n    local drivers = graph.drivers\n\n    -- entry box must exist\n    if not boxes[graph.entry] then\n        errors[#errors + 1] = \"entry_box_id '\" .. tostring(graph.entry) ..\n            \"' does not match any box\"\n    end\n\n    for id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        -- connection integrity: reciprocal check (outgoing connections only)\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box ~= id then goto next_conn end\n\n            local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n            if target == nil then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id ..\n                    \"': connection to unknown box '\" .. tostring(c.to_box) .. \"'\"\n                goto next_conn\n            end\n\n            local found = false\n            for _, tc in ipairs(target.connections or {}) do\n                if tc.from_box    == c.from_box   and\n                   tc.from_output == c.from_output and\n                   tc.to_box      == c.to_box      and\n                   tc.to_input    == c.to_input    then\n                    found = true\n                    break\n                end\n            end\n            if not found then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection \" ..\n                    c.from_box .. \".\" .. (c.from_output or c.from_port) ..\n                    \" -> \" .. c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input ..\n                    \" not reciprocated in target\"\n            end\n\n            ::next_conn::\n        end\n\n        -- driver must exist for call boxes with a ref\n        if box.kind == \"call\" and box.ref then\n            local ext = extension_of(box.ref)\n            -- binary callers (no fn) don't need a driver — they are the driver\n            if box.fn and ext ~= \"\" and not drivers[ext] then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id ..\n                    \"': no driver defined for extension '\" .. ext .. \"'\"\n            end\n        end\n\n        -- branch box: else port must exist; unwired else is warned (not errored here)\n        if box.kind == \"branch\" then\n            local has_else = false\n            for _, p in ipairs(box.ports or {}) do\n                if p.name == \"else\" then has_else = true end\n            end\n            if not has_else then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"branch box '\" .. id .. \"' missing 'else' port\"\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- cycle detection from entry box\n    if boxes[graph.entry] then\n        local cycle_errors = detect_cycles(boxes, graph.entry)\n        for _, e in ipairs(cycle_errors) do\n            errors[#errors + 1] = e\n        end\n    end\n\n    return #errors == 0, errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/003-loader.lua"
        }
      }],

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-07T23:07:39.668Z",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",

    "content":[{
        "name":"Write",
        "id":"toolu_01Wx7aorKQm4ZyK7pPr9evwr",
        "type":"tool_use",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "content":"-- Synchronous FSM executor for the SoraMech runner.\n-- Walks the graph from the entry box, invokes language drivers for each\n-- box in dependency order, and threads output values through wires.\n-- Each box call is isolated in run_task() — the future thread pool swap point.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal M    = {}\n\n-- {{{ eval_predicate\nlocal function eval_predicate(pred, value)\n    -- structured predicates only; no arbitrary lua eval\n    local op  = pred.op\n    local lit = pred.value\n\n    if op == \"eq\"       then return value == lit\n    elseif op == \"lt\"   then return value <  lit\n    elseif op == \"gt\"   then return value >  lit\n    elseif op == \"lte\"  then return value <= lit\n    elseif op == \"gte\"  then return value >= lit\n    elseif op == \"contains\" then\n        return type(value) == \"string\" and value:find(lit, 1, true) ~= nil\n    elseif op == \"matches\" then\n        return type(value) == \"string\" and value:match(lit) ~= nil\n    end\n    return false\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ shell_quote\nlocal function shell_quote(s)\n    -- wrap a string in single quotes, escaping any embedded single quotes\n    return \"'\" .. tostring(s):gsub(\"'\", \"'\\\\''\") .. \"'\"\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ driver_path_for\nlocal function driver_path_for(ref, drivers)\n    -- binary callers (no extension mapping needed — they are executable directly)\n    -- source callers: look up extension in driver table\n    local ext = ref:match(\"%.([^./]+)$\")\n    if not ext then return ref end  -- no extension: treat as binary\n    local driver = drivers[\".\" .. ext]\n    return driver\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ run_task\n-- The task boundary. In v1: synchronous. Future: hand this signature to\n-- the thread pool. Returns outputs table and ok/err.\nlocal function run_task(box, inputs, drivers, map_dir)\n    local ref = box.ref\n    local fn  = box.fn\n\n    -- locate the driver for this ref\n    local driver = driver_path_for(ref, drivers)\n    if not driver then\n        return nil, \"no driver found for ref '\" .. ref .. \"'\"\n    end\n\n    -- resolve ref relative to map_dir\n    local abs_ref = map_dir .. \"/\" .. ref\n\n    -- build argument list: file fn arg_count [args...]\n    local args = {}\n    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n        local val = inputs[port.name]\n        if val == nil then\n            -- nil input becomes JSON null\n            args[#args + 1] = shell_quote(json.encode(nil))\n        else\n            args[#args + 1] = shell_quote(json.encode(val))\n        end\n    end\n\n    local cmd\n    if fn then\n        -- source caller: driver file fn arg_count [args...]\n        cmd = driver .. \" \" .. shell_quote(abs_ref) .. \" \" ..\n              shell_quote(fn) .. \" \" .. #args\n        for _, a in ipairs(args) do cmd = cmd .. \" \" .. a end\n    else\n        -- binary caller: run ref directly with args\n        cmd = abs_ref .. \" \" .. #args\n        for _, a in ipairs(args) do cmd = cmd .. \" \" .. a end\n    end\n\n    -- invoke driver; capture stdout; errors go to stderr (visible in terminal)\n    local handle = io.popen(cmd .. \" 2>&1_STDERR_REDIR_NOT_SUPPORTED\", \"r\")\n    -- io.popen doesn't support stderr separation in standard lua; run via sh -c\n    -- and capture both, then split on a sentinel\n    handle:close()\n\n    -- run properly: use sh -c with stderr redirected to a tmp file\n    local tmpfile = map_dir .. \"/tmp/driver-stderr-\" .. box.id .. \".txt\"\n    local full_cmd = \"sh -c \" .. shell_quote(cmd .. \" 2>\" .. tmpfile)\n    local ph = io.popen(full_cmd, \"r\")\n    local stdout = ph:read(\"*a\")\n    local ok_close = ph:close()\n\n    -- read stderr if any\n    local sf = io.open(tmpfile, \"r\")\n    local stderr_text = sf and sf:read(\"*a\") or \"\"\n    if sf then sf:close() end\n    os.remove(tmpfile)\n\n    if not ok_close then\n        local err_msg = \"driver failed for box '\" .. box.id .. \"'\"\n        if stderr_text and #stderr_text > 0 then\n            err_msg = err_msg .. \": \" .. stderr_text:gsub(\"%s+$\", \"\")\n        end\n        return nil, err_msg\n    end\n\n    -- parse output JSON array from stdout\n    local result_arr, _, jerr = json.decode(stdout)\n    if not result_arr then\n        return nil, \"box '\" .. box.id .. \"': driver stdout is not valid JSON: \" ..\n            tostring(jerr) .. \" (got: \" .. tostring(stdout):sub(1, 80) .. \")\"\n    end\n    if type(result_arr) ~= \"table\" then\n        return nil, \"box '\" .. box.id .. \"': driver output must be a JSON array\"\n    end\n\n    -- map positional results to named output ports\n    local outputs = {}\n    for i, port in ipairs(box.outputs or {}) do\n        local raw = result_arr[i]\n        if raw ~= nil then\n            -- each element in the outer array is itself a JSON-encoded value\n            local val, _, aerr = json.decode(raw)\n            outputs[port.name] = aerr and raw or val\n        end\n    end\n\n    return outputs, nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ inputs_satisfied\nlocal function inputs_satisfied(box, store)\n    -- a box is ready inputs[port.name] = store[box.id .. \".\" .. port.name]\n    end\n    return inputs\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ fire_connections\nlocal function fire_connections(box, outputs, store, queue, boxes, local input_val = outputs[\"_branch_input\"]\n        local fired = false\n        for _, port in ipairs(box.ports or {}) do\n            if port.name == \"else\" then goto next_port end\n            if port.predicate and eval_predicate(port.predicate, input_val) then\n                -- find and fire connections from this port\n                for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n c.to_box\n                    end\n                end\n                fired = true\n                break\n            end\n            ::next_port::\n        end\n\n        if not fired then\n            -- fire \"else\" port\n            for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n                if c.from_box == box.id and c.from_port == \"else\" then\n                    store[c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input] = input_val\n                    queue[#queue + 1] = c.to_box\n                    fired = true\n                end\n            end\n\n            if not fired then\n input ports\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box ~= box.id then goto next_conn end\n            local val = outputs[c.from_output]\n            store[c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input] = val\n            -- enqueue target if all its inputs are now satisfied\n            local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n            if target and boxes[entry_id]\n    if entry_box and #(entry_box.inputs or {}) == 0 then\n        -- no inputs needed; ready immediately\n    end\n\n    local queue   = { entry_id }\n    local visited = {}  -- boxes that have been run (prevent double-execution)\n    local run_log = {}  -- per-box execution records for last-run.json\n    local map_ok  = true\n    local map_err = nil\n\n    while #queue > 0 do\n        -- dequeue\n        local id = table.remove(queue, 1)\n\n        local box = boxes[id]\n        if not box then\n            map_ok  = false\n            map_err = \"unknown box in queue: '\" .. id .. \"'\"\n            break\n        end\n\n        -- skip boxes whose inputs are not yet satisfied (they'll be re-enqueued)\n        if not inputs_satisfied(box, store) then\n            goto next_iter\n        end\n\n        if visited[id] and box.kind ~= \"branch\" then\n            goto next_iter\n        end\n        visited[id] = true\n\n        local inputs = collect_inputs(box, store)\n\n        -- branch box is handled specially: it doesn't invoke a driver,\n        -- it routes based on its single input value\n        local outputs, task_err\n        if box.kind == \"branch\" then\n            -- the branch input is the value wired to its single input port\n            local branch_val = inputs[(box.inputs or {})[1] and box.inputs[1].name or \"value\"]\n            outputs = { _branch_input = branch_val }\n            task_err = nil\n        else\n            outputs, task_err = run_task(box, inputs, drivers, map_dir)\n        end\n\n        run_log[id] = {\n
