err(errors, \"call box missing 'ref'\")\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n\n    elseif box.kind err(errors, \"branch box missing required 'else' port\")\n            end\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_port_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or     "originalFile":"// Inspector sidebar: shows and edits the selected box's fields.\n// Fires PUT to the server on every field change (autosave).\n\nconst Inspector = (() => {\n  const panel  = document.getElementById('inspector');\n  const title  = document.getElementById('inspector-title');\n  const fields = document.getElementById('inspector-fields');\n\n  let current_box = null;\n  let on_change_cb = null;\n\n  // {{{ hide\n  function hide() {\n    panel.classList.add('hidden');\n    current_box = null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ save\n  async function save() {\n    if (!current_box) return;\n    try {\n      await API.put_box(current_box.id, current_box);\n      if (on_change_cb) on_change_cb(current_box);\n    } catch(e) {\n      console.error('autosave failed:', e.message);\n      status_msg('save error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_row\n  function mk_row(label_text, input_el) {\n    const row = document.createElement('div');\n    row.className = 'field-row';\n    const lbl = document.createElement('label');\n    lbl.textContent = label_text;\n    row.appendChild(lbl);\n    row.appendChild(input_el);\n    return row;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_text_input\n  function mk_text_input(value, on_input) {\n    const inp = document.createElement('input');\n    inp.type  = 'text';\n    inp.value = value || '';\n    inp.addEventListener('input', () => { on_input(inp.value); save(); });\n    return inp;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_port_list\n  function mk_port_list(ports, on_change) {\n    const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    wrap.className = 'port-list';\n\n    const render_ports = () => {\n      wrap.innerHTML = '';\n      ports.forEach((p, i) => {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className = 'port-row';\n\n        const name_inp = document.createElement('input');\n        name_inp.type  = 'text';\n        name_inp.value = p.name || '';\n        name_inp.placeholder = 'name';\n        name_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { ports[i].name = name_inp.value; on_change(); save(); });\n\n        const type_inp = document.createElement('input');\n        type_inp.type  = 'text';\n        type_inp.value = p.type || '';\n        type_inp.placeholder = 'type';\n        type_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { ports[i].type = type_inp.value; on_change(); save(); });\n\n        const del_btn = document.createElement('button');\n        del_btn.textContent = '×';\n        del_btn.className   = 'port-del';\n        del_btn.addEventListener('click', () => { ports.splice(i, 1); render_ports(); on_change(); save(); });\n\n        row.appendChild(name_inp);\n        row.appendChild(type_inp);\n        row.appendChild(del_btn);\n        wrap.appendChild(row);\n      });\n\n      const add_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      add_btn.textContent = '+ port';\n      add_btn.className   = 'add-port';\n      add_btn.addEventListener('click', () => {\n        ports.push({ name: '', type: 'string' });\n        render_ports();\n        on_change();\n        save();\n      });\n      wrap.appendChild(add_btn);\n    };\n\n    render_ports();\n    return wrap;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_branch_port_list\n  function mk_branch_port_list(ports, on_change) {\n    const OPS = ['eq','lt','gt','lte','gte','contains','matches'];\n    const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    wrap.className = 'port-list';\n\n    const render_ports = () => {\n      wrap.innerHTML = '';\n      ports.forEach((p, i) => {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className = 'port-row branch-port-row';\n\n        const name_inp = document.createElement('input');\n        name_inp.type  = 'text';\n        name_inp.value = p.name || '';\n        name_inp.placeholder = 'port name';\n        name_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { ports[i].name = name_inp.value; on_change(); save(); });\n        row.appendChild(name_inp);\n\n        if (p.name !== 'else') {\n          if (!p.predicate) p.predicate = { op: 'eq', value: '' };\n\n          const op_sel = document.createElement('select');\n          OPS.forEach(op => {\n            const opt = document.createElement('option');\n            opt.value = op; opt.textContent = op;\n            if (op === p.predicate.op) opt.selected = true;\n            op_sel.appendChild(opt);\n          });\n          op_sel.addEventListener('change', () => { ports[i].predicate.op = op_sel.value; save(); });\n\n          const val_inp = document.createElement('input');\n          val_inp.type  = 'text';\n          val_inp.value = p.predicate.value ?? '';\n          val_inp.placeholder = 'value';\n          val_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { ports[i].predicate.value = val_inp.value; save(); });\n\n          row.appendChild(op_sel);\n          row.appendChild(val_inp);\n        }\n\n        // can't delete the else port\n        if (p.name !== 'else') {\n          const del_btn = document.createElement('button');\n          del_btn.textContent = '×';\n          del_btn.className   = 'port-del';\n          del_btn.addEventListener('click', () => { ports.splice(i, 1); render_ports(); on_change(); save(); });\n          row.appendChild(del_btn);\n        }\n\n        wrap.appendChild(row);\n      });\n\n      const add_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      add_btn.textContent = '+ port';\n      add_btn.className   = 'add-port';\n      add_btn.addEventListener('click', () => {\n        // insert before else\n        const else_i = ports.findIndex(p => p.name === 'else');\n        const new_port = { name: '', predicate: { op: 'eq', value: '' } };\n        if (else_i >= 0) ports.splice(else_i, 0, new_port);\n        else ports.push(new_port);\n        render_ports(); on_change(); save();\n      });\n      wrap.appendChild(add_btn);\n    };\n\n    render_ports();\n    return wrap;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ show\n  function show(box, on_changed) {\n    current_box  = box;\n    on_change_cb = on_changed;\n    panel.classList.remove('hidden');\n    title.textContent = box.id;\n    fields.innerHTML  = '';\n\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('label',\n      mk_text_input(box.label, v => { current_box.label = v; })));\n\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('kind', (() => {\n      const sel = document.createElement('select');\n      ['call','branch','data'].forEach(k => {\n        const opt = document.createElement('option');\n        opt.value = k; opt.textContent = k;\n        if (k === box.kind) opt.selected = true;\n        sel.appendChild(opt);\n      });\n      sel.addEventListener('change', () => { current_box.kind = sel.value; show(current_box, on_change_cb); save(); });\n      return sel;\n    })()));\n\n    if (box.kind === 'call' || box.kind === 'data') {\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('ref',\n        mk_text_input(box.ref, v => { current_box.ref = v; })));\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('fn',\n        mk_text_input(box.fn, v => { current_box.fn = v; })));\n    }\n\n    const inputs_sec = document.createElement('div');\n    inputs_sec.className = 'section-label';\n    inputs_sec.textContent = 'inputs';\n    fields.appendChild(inputs_sec);\n    if (!current_box.inputs) current_box.inputs = [];\n    fields.appendChild(mk_port_list(current_box.inputs, () => {}));\n\n    if (box.kind === 'branch') {\n      if (!current_box.ports) current_box.ports = [{ name: 'else' }];\n      const ports_sec = document.createElement('div');\n      ports_sec.className = 'section-label';\n      ports_sec.textContent = 'ports';\n      fields.appendChild(ports_sec);\n      fields.appendChild(mk_branch_port_list(current_box.ports, () => {}));\n    } else {\n      if (!current_box.outputs) current_box.outputs = [];\n      const out_sec = document.createElement('div');\n      out_sec.className = 'section-label';\n      out_sec.textContent = 'outputs';\n      fields.appendChild(out_sec);\n      fields.appendChild(mk_port_list(current_box.outputs, () => {}));\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { show, hide };\n})();\n",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/js/004-inspector.js",
    "replaceAll":false,

      "type":"text",
      "file":{
        "content":"-- Value producer and result writer for branch-test map.\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal M    = {}\n\n-- {{{ get_value\n-- Reads \"n\" from data/state.json and returns it as a number.\nfunction M.get_value()\n    local path = (SORAMECH_MAP_DIR or \".\") .. \"/data/state.json\"\n    local f    = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then return 42 end\n    local raw  = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    local obj = json.decode(raw)\n    return (obj and obj.fields and obj.fields.n and obj.fields.n.value) or 42\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ write_result\n-- Writes the routed value and which branch fired to data/state.json.\nfunction M.write_result(n)\n    local path = (SORAMECH_MAP_DIR or \".\") .. \"/data/state.json\"\n    local f    = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then return end\n    local raw  = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    local obj  = json.decode(raw) or { constant = false, fields = {} }\n    obj.fields.result = { constant = false, value = tostring(n) }\n    local tmp  = path .. \".tmp\"\n    local fw   = io.open(tmp, \"w\")\n    if not fw then return end\n    fw:write(json.encode(obj, { indent = true }))\n    fw:close()\n    os.rename(tmp, path)\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",
        "startLine":1,
        "totalLines":38,
        "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/maps/branch-test/src/values.lua",
        "numLines":38
      }
    },
    "displayPath":"maps/branch-test/src/values.lua",
    "filename":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/maps/branch-test/src/values.lua"
  }

err(errors, \"branch connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_port'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"branch connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"branch connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_box\nfunction M.validate_box(box)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(box) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"box must be a table\" }\n    end\n\n    if box.id == nil or type(box.id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'id'\")\n  err(errors, \"missing or invalid 'kind' (must be call, branch, or data)\")\n    end\n\n    if box.kind == \"call\" then\n        if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n\n    elseif box.kind err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- err(errors, \"branch connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_port'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"branch connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if i .. \"] missing both 'from_output' and 'from_port'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        if box.outputs ~= nil and type(box.outputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'outputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n\n    elseif box.kind ==          end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a table\")\n        elseif box.ui.x == nil or box.ui.y == nil then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must have 'x' and 'y' fields\")\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",

The built-in retry is for the common case of\n\"ask the LLM again with a different temperature.\"\n",

        "lines":[" "," ## Status"," ","-open","+complete"," ","+## Implementation notes","+","+Schema fix (2026-05-07): `src/001-schema.lua` `validate_box` previously applied","+kind-specific connection validation to ALL connections in a box file. Since both","+endpoint boxes store the identical 4-field connection record, a call box file","+can contain a reciprocal record with `from_port` (from a branch box), and a","+branch box file can contain a reciprocal record with `from_output` (from a call","+box). Fixed by routing connection validation on `c.from_box == box.id`:","+outgoing records get the strict kind-specific validator; incoming reciprocal","+records get a looser validator (`validate_incoming_connection`) that accepts","+either `from_output` or `from_port`.","+","+Executor retry: branch inputs are cleared from the store on retry so the","+upstream box re-fires cleanly. `retry_vary` fields are pseudo-randomized in","+the range before the upstream box is re-queued.","+","+Verified with `maps/branch-test/`: n=30 routes to write-low (result=\"30\"),","+n=70 routes to write-high (result=\"70\"). hello and driver-test maps pass","+regression.","+"," ## Blockers"," "," - 104 (executor must exist; predicate evaluation is added to it here)"]

then\n    echo \"lua.sh: missing file-path or fn-name\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif ! command -v luajit > /dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"lua.sh: luajit not found on PATH\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif [ ! -f \"${FILE_PATH}\" ]; then\n    echo \"lua.sh: file not found: ${FILE_PATH}\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# build a JSON array of the raw argument strings for passing into lua\nARGS_JSON=\"[\"\nSEP=\"\"\nfor ARG in \"$@\"; do\n    ARGS_JSON=\"${ARGS_JSON}${SEP}${ARG}\"\n    SEP=\",\"\ndone\nARGS_JSON=\"${ARGS_JSON}]\"\n\n# set LUA_PATH so dkjson is findable before the shim runs its first require\nexport LUA_PATH=\"${DIR}/libs/?.lua;${LUA_PATH:-;}\"\n\n# run luajit with the driver shim inline; the shim loads the module,\n# decodes arguments, calls the function, and encodes the result\nluajit - \"${FILE_PATH}\" \"${FN_NAME}\" \"${ARGS_JSON}\" << 'LUASHIM'\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\n\n-- read driver arguments\nlocal file_path = arg[1]\nlocal fn_name   = arg[2]\nlocal args_raw  = arg[3]\n\n-- add libs and the module's own directory to the path for any further requires\nlocal script_dir = file_path:match(\"^(.+)/[^/]+$\") or \".\"\npackage.path = script_dir .. \"/?.lua;\" ..\n               \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\n-- expose map root as a global so box functions can access data files without\n-- needing it wired as an explicit input; convention: src/ is one level below root\nSORAMECH_MAP_DIR = script_dir:match(\"^(.+)/[^/]+$\") or script_dir\n\n-- decode args array\nlocal args_table, _, jerr = json.decode(args_raw)\nif not args_table then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: failed to decode args JSON: \" .. tostring(jerr) .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- load the module\nlocal ok, mod = pcall(dofile, file_path)\nif not ok then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: error loading \" .. file_path .. \": \" .. tostring(mod) .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- resolve the function\nlocal fn = mod[fn_name]\nif type(fn) ~= \"function\" then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: no public function '\" .. fn_name .. \"' in \" .. file_path .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- decode each arg from JSON to lua value; strings are passed as-is\nlocal call_args = {}\nfor i, raw_arg in ipairs(args_table) do\n    local val, _, aerr = json.decode(raw_arg)\n    if aerr then\n        -- not valid JSON — treat as a plain string\n        call_args[i] = raw_arg\n    else\n        call_args[i] = val\n    end\nend\n\n-- call the function; collect all return values into a table\nlocal results = table.pack(fn(table.unpack(call_args)))\n\n-- encode results as a JSON array (each return value is one element)\nlocal encoded = {}\nfor i = 1, results.n do\n    encoded[i] = json.encode(results[i])\nend\nprint(json.encode(encoded))\nLUASHIM"

returns table, err.\nlocal function load_file(path)\n    local f, ferr = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then return nil, \"cannot open \" .. path .. \": \" .. tostring(ferr) end\n    local raw = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    local obj, _, jerr = json.decode(raw)\n    if not obj then return nil, \"JSON decode error in \" .. path .. \": \" .. tostring(jerr) end\n    return obj, nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ write_file\n-- Atomically encodes obj as JSON and writes it to path.\nlocal function write_file(path, obj)\n    local tmp = path .. \".tmp\"\n    local f, ferr = io.open(tmp, \"w\")\n    if not f then return nil, \"cannot write \" .. tmp .. \": \" .. tostring(ferr) end\n    f:write(json.encode(obj, { indent = true }))\n    f:close()\n    local ok, rerr = os.rename(tmp, path)\n    if not ok then return nil, \"rename failed for \" .. path .. \": \" .. tostring(rerr) end\n    return true, nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ resolve_path\n-- Builds the full filesystem path for a data file.\n-- dir is map_dir/data or map_dir/tmp; filename is e.g. \"state.json\".\nlocal function resolve_path(dir, filename)\n    -- strip any path separators from filename to prevent traversal\n    local safe = filename:gsub(\"[/\\\\]\", \"\")\n    return dir .. \"/\" .. safe\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ get_field\n-- Walks a dot-separated field_path into a nested table; returns value or nil.\nlocal function get_field(obj, field_path)\n    local node = obj\n    for key in field_path:gmatch(\"[^.]+\") do\n        if type(node) ~= \"table\" then return nil end\n        -- data files store values inside {constant, value} wrappers at each leaf\n        if node[key] ~= nil then\n            node = node[key]\n        elseif node.fields and node.fields[key] ~= nil then\n            node = node.fields[key]\n        else\n            return nil\n        end\n    end\n    -- unwrap leaf {constant, value} if present\n    if type(node) == \"table\" and node.value ~= nil then\n        return node.value\n    end\n    return node\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ is_constant\n-- Returns true if the field at field_path is marked constant.\nlocal function is_constant(obj, field_path)\n    if obj.constant then return true end\n    local node = obj\n    local keys = {}\n    for key in field_path:gmatch(\"[^.]+\") do keys[#keys + 1] = key end\n    for i, key in ipairs(keys) do\n        if type(node) ~= \"table\" then return false end\n        local next_node = nil\n        if node[key] ~= nil then\n            next_node = node[key]\n        elseif node.fields and node.fields[key] ~= nil then\n            next_node = node.fields[key]\n        else\n            return false\n        end\n        -- check constant on the intermediate or leaf node\n        if type(next_node) == \"table\" and next_node.constant then\n            return true\n        end\n        node = next_node\n    end\n    return false\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ set_field\n-- Writes value to the field at field_path inside obj, creating intermediates.\n-- Returns ok, err. Does not touch the file itself.\nlocal function set_field(obj, field_path, value)\n    local keys = {}\n    for key in field_path:gmatch(\"[^.]+\") do keys[#keys + 1] = key end\n    if #keys == 0 then return nil, \"empty field_path\" end\n\n    -- walk to the parent of the leaf\n    local node = obj\n    for i = 1, #keys - 1 do\n        local key = keys[i]\n        if node.fields and node.fields[key] ~= nil then\n            node = node.fields[key]\n        elseif node[key] ~= nil then\n            node = node[key]\n        else\n            return nil, \"field path '\" .. field_path .. \"' not found at '\" .. key .. \"'\"\n        end\n    end\n\n    local leaf_key = keys[#keys]\n    -- write into the wrapper table if it exists, else set directly\n    local target = nil\n    if node.fields and node.fields[leaf_key] ~= nil then\n        target = node.fields[leaf_key]\n    elseif node[leaf_key] ~= nil then\n        target = node[leaf_key]\n    end\n\n    if type(target) == \"table\" and target.value ~= nil then\n        target.value = value\n    elseif node.fields then\n        node.fields[leaf_key] = { constant = false, value = value }\n    else\n        node[leaf_key] = value\n    end\n    return true, nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.load\n-- Loads an entire data file and returns the decoded table.\n-- dir is the directory containing the file (e.g. map_dir .. \"/data\").\nfunction M.load(dir, filename)\n    local path = resolve_path(dir, filename)\n    return load_file(path)\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.get\n-- Reads a single field from a data file by dot-separated field_path.\n-- Returns the value (unwrapped from {constant, value} wrapper if present).\nfunction M.get(dir, filename, field_path)\n    local path = resolve_path(dir, filename)\n    local obj, err = load_file(path)\n    if not obj then return nil, err end\n    local val = get_field(obj, field_path)\n    if val == nil then\n        return nil, \"field '\" .. field_path .. \"' not found in \" .. filename\n    end\n    return val, nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.set\n-- Writes a single field in a data file; refuses writes to constant fields.\n-- Returns true on success, nil + error string on failure.\nfunction M.set(dir, filename, field_path, value)\n    local path = resolve_path(dir, filename)\n    local obj, err = load_file(path)\n    if not obj then return nil, err end\n\n    if is_constant(obj, field_path) then\n        return nil, \"field '\" .. field_path .. \"' in \" .. filename .. \" is constant (read-only)\"\n    end\n\n    local ok, serr = set_field(obj, field_path, value)\n    if not ok then return nil, serr end\n\n    return write_file(path, obj)\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",

    "content":"-- Data file access library for SoraMech map boxes.\n-- Reads and writes JSON data files in a map's data/ or tmp/ directory.\n-- Enforces constant flags; all writes are atomic (write-tmp-then-rename).\n\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal M    = {}\n\n-- {{{ load_file\n-- Reads and JSON-decodes a data file; returns table, err.\nlocal function load_file(path)\n    local f, ferr = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then return nil, \"cannot open \" .. path .. \": \" .. tostring(ferr) end\n    local raw = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    local obj, _, jerr = json.decode(raw)\n    if not obj then return nil, \"JSON decode error in \" .. path .. \": \" .. tostring(jerr) end\n    return obj, nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ write_file\n-- Atomically encodes obj as JSON and writes it to path.\nlocal function write_file(path, obj)\n    local tmp = path .. \".tmp\"\n    local f, ferr = io.open(tmp, \"w\")\n    if not f then return nil, \"cannot write \" .. tmp .. \": \" .. tostring(ferr) end\n    f:write(json.encode(obj, { indent = true }))\n    f:close()\n    local ok, rerr = os.rename(tmp, path)\n    if not ok then return nil, \"rename failed for \" .. path .. \": \" .. tostring(rerr) end\n    return true, nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ resolve_path\n-- Builds the full filesystem path for a data file.\n-- dir is map_dir/data or map_dir/tmp; filename is e.g. \"state.json\".\nlocal function resolve_path(dir, filename)\n    -- strip any path separators from filename to prevent traversal\n    local safe = filename:gsub(\"[/\\\\]\", \"\")\n    return dir .. \"/\" .. safe\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ get_field\n-- Walks a dot-separated field_path into a nested table; returns value or nil.\nlocal function get_field(obj, field_path)\n    local node = obj\n    for key in field_path:gmatch(\"[^.]+\") do\n        if type(node) ~= \"table\" then return nil end\n        -- data files store values inside {constant, value} wrappers at each leaf\n        if node[key] ~= nil then\n            node = node[key]\n        elseif node.fields and node.fields[key] ~= nil then\n            node = node.fields[key]\n        else\n            return nil\n        end\n    end\n    -- unwrap leaf {constant, value} if present\n    if type(node) == \"table\" and node.value ~= nil then\n        return node.value\n    end\n    return node\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ is_constant\n-- Returns true if the field at field_path is marked constant.\nlocal function is_constant(obj, field_path)\n    if obj.constant then return true end\n    local node = obj\n    local keys = {}\n    for key in field_path:gmatch(\"[^.]+\") do keys[#keys + 1] = key end\n    for i, key in ipairs(keys) do\n        if type(node) ~= \"table\" then return false end\n        local next_node = nil\n        if node[key] ~= nil then\n            next_node = node[key]\n        elseif node.fields and node.fields[key] ~= nil then\n            next_node = node.fields[key]\n        else\n            return false\n        end\n        -- check constant on the intermediate or leaf node\n        if type(next_node) == \"table\" and next_node.constant then\n            return true\n        end\n        node = next_node\n    end\n    return false\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ set_field\n-- Writes value to the field at field_path inside obj, creating intermediates.\n-- Returns ok, err. Does not touch the file itself.\nlocal function set_field(obj, field_path, value)\n    local keys = {}\n    for key in field_path:gmatch(\"[^.]+\") do keys[#keys + 1] = key end\n    if #keys == 0 then return nil, \"empty field_path\" end\n\n    -- walk to the parent of the leaf\n    local node = obj\n    for i = 1, #keys - 1 do\n        local key = keys[i]\n        if node.fields and node.fields[key] ~= nil then\n            node = node.fields[key]\n        elseif node[key] ~= nil then\n            node = node[key]\n        else\n            return nil, \"field path '\" .. field_path .. \"' not found at '\" .. key .. \"'\"\n        end\n    end\n\n    local leaf_key = keys[#keys]\n    -- write into the wrapper table if it exists, else set directly\n    local target = nil\n    if node.fields and node.fields[leaf_key] ~= nil then\n        target = node.fields[leaf_key]\n    elseif node[leaf_key] ~= nil then\n        target = node[leaf_key]\n    end\n\n    if type(target) == \"table\" and target.value ~= nil then\n        target.value = value\n    elseif node.fields then\n        node.fields[leaf_key] = { constant = false, value = value }\n    else\n        node[leaf_key] = value\n    end\n    return true, nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.load\n-- Loads an entire data file and returns the decoded table.\n-- dir is the directory containing the file (e.g. map_dir .. \"/data\").\nfunction M.load(dir, filename)\n    local path = resolve_path(dir, filename)\n    return load_file(path)\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.get\n-- Reads a single field from a data file by dot-separated field_path.\n-- Returns the value (unwrapped from {constant, value} wrapper if present).\nfunction M.get(dir, filename, field_path)\n    local path = resolve_path(dir, filename)\n    local obj, err = load_file(path)\n    if not obj then return nil, err end\n    local val = get_field(obj, field_path)\n    if val == nil then\n        return nil, \"field '\" .. field_path .. \"' not found in \" .. filename\n    end\n    return val, nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.set\n-- Writes a single field in a data file; refuses writes to constant fields.\n-- Returns true on success, nil + error string on failure.\nfunction M.set(dir, filename, field_path, value)\n    local path = resolve_path(dir, filename)\n    local obj, err = load_file(path)\n    if not obj then return nil, err end\n\n    if is_constant(obj, field_path) then\n        return nil, \"field '\" .. field_path .. \"' in \" .. filename .. \" is constant (read-only)\"\n    end\n\n    local ok, serr = set_field(obj, field_path, value)\n    if not ok then return nil, serr end\n\n    return write_file(path, obj)\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",

require(\"dkjson\")\n\n-- {{{ local function fail\nlocal function fail(msg)\n    io.stderr:write(\"[FAIL] \" .. msg .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ local function pass\nlocal function pass(msg)\n    io.write(\"[PASS] \" .. msg .. \"\\n\")\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ local function write_fixture\n-- Writes a known data file into a temp directory for the test.\nlocal function f:write(json.encode(obj, { indent = true }))\n    f:close()\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ local function setup_tmp\n-- Creates a unique temp dir under /tmp for this test run.\nlocal function setup_tmp()\n    local tmpdir = \"/tmp/soramech-data-test-\" .. tostring(os.time())\n    os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. tmpdir)\n    return tmpdir\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- set up temp dir and fixture\nlocal tmp = setup_tmp()\nlocal fixture = {\n    constant = false,\n    fields = {\n        score   = { constant = false, value = 42 },\n        name    = { constant = false, value = \"player1\" },\n        locked  = { constant = true,  value = \"do-not-change\" },\n    }\n}\nwrite_fixture(tmp, \"state.json\", fixture)\n\n-- ── test: load returns the full table ──────────────────────────────────────\nlocal obj, err = data.load(tmp, \"state.json\")\nif not obj then fail(\"load returned error: \" .. tostring(err)) end\nif type(obj) ~= \"table\" then fail(\"load did not return a table\") end\npass(\"load returns table\")\n\n-- ── test: get reads a numeric field ────────────────────────────────────────\nlocal score, gerr = data.get(tmp, \"state.json\", \"score\")\nif gerr then fail(\"get score: \" .. gerr) end\nif score ~= 42 then fail(\"get score expected 42, got \" .. tostring(score)) end\npass(\"get numeric field\")\n\n-- ── test: get reads a string field ─────────────────────────────────────────\nlocal name, nerr = data.get(tmp, \"state.json\", \"name\")\nif nerr then fail(\"get name: \" .. nerr) end\nif name ~= \"player1\" then fail(\"get name expected 'player1', got \" .. tostring(name)) end\npass(\"get string field\")\n\n-- ── test: set writes a new value and it round-trips through get ─────────────\nlocal ok, serr = data.set(tmp, \"state.json\", \"score\", 99)\nif not ok then fail(\"set score: \" .. tostring(serr)) end\nlocal new_score, rgerr = data.get(tmp, \"state.json\", \"score\")\nif rgerr then fail(\"get after set: \" .. rgerr) end\nif new_score ~= 99 then fail(\"set score: expected 99, got \" .. tostring(new_score)) end\npass(\"set and round-trip get\")\n\n-- ── test: set on a constant field returns an error ──────────────────────────\nlocal bad_ok, bad_err = data.set(tmp, \"state.json\", \"locked\", \"changed\")\nif bad_ok then fail(\"set on constant field should fail but returned ok\") end\nif not bad_err then fail(\"set on constant field returned no error string\") end\npass(\"set on constant field returns error\")\n\n-- ── test: constant value is unchanged after failed write   fail(\"constant field mutated: got \" .. tostring(locked_val))\nend\npass(\"constant field unchanged after refused write\")\n\n-- ── test: file-level constant blocks all writes \"readonly.json\", \"x\", 2)\nif fok then fail(\"set on file-level-constant should fail but returned ok\") end\nif not ferr then fail(\"set on file-level-constant returned no error\") end\npass(\"file-level constant blocks write\")\n\n-- ── test: get on missing field returns error ────────────────────────────────\nlocal mv, merr = data.get(tmp, \"state.json\", \"nonexistent\")\nif function pass(msg)\n    io.write(\"[PASS] \" .. msg .. \"\\n\")\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ local function write_fixture\n-- Writes a known data file into a temp directory for the test.\nlocal function f:write(json.encode(obj, { indent = true }))\n    f:close()\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ local function setup_tmp\n-- Creates a unique temp dir under /tmp for this test run.\nlocal function setup_tmp()\n    local tmpdir = \"/tmp/soramech-data-test-\" .. tostring(os.time())\n    os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. tmpdir)\n    return tmpdir\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- set up temp dir and fixture\nlocal tmp = setup_tmp()\nlocal fixture = {\n    constant = false,\n    fields = {\n        score   = { constant = false, value = 42 },\n        name    = { constant = false, value = \"player1\" },\n        locked  = { constant = true,  value = \"do-not-change\" },\n    }\n}\nwrite_fixture(tmp, \"state.json\", fixture)\n\n-- ── test: load returns the full table ──────────────────────────────────────\nlocal obj, returns table\")\n\n-- ── test: get reads a numeric field ────────────────────────────────────────\nlocal score, gerr = data.get(tmp, \"state.json\", \"score\")\nif gerr then fail(\"get score: \" ..         "input":{
          "content":"# soramech-data.lua\n\nData file access library for SoraMech map boxes. Works with any directory\nof JSON data files — `data/` for persistent storage, `tmp/` for ephemeral.\n\nAll JSON files use the wrapper format:\n```json\n{\n  \"constant\": false,\n  \"fields\": {\n    \"key\": { \"constant\": false, \"value\": <any> }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## M.load(dir, filename) → table, err\n\nLoads and decodes the entire file. Returns the raw decoded table (with\n`constant` and `fields` wrappers intact). Useful when you need to inspect\nthe structure or iterate all fields.\n\n| param    | type   | description                                  |\n|----------|--------|----------------------------------------------|\n| dir      | string | directory path (e.g. `map_dir .. \"/data\"`)   |\n| filename | string | file name, e.g. `\"state.json\"` (no slashes)  |\n\nReturns: `table, nil` on success; `nil, err_string` on failure.\n\n---\n\n## M.get(dir, filename, field_path) → value, err\n\nReads a single field by dot-separated path. Unwraps the `{constant, value}`\nwrapper automatically — you get the plain value back.\n\n| param      | type   | description                              |\n|------------|--------|------------------------------------------|\n| dir        | string | directory path                           |\n| filename   | string | file name                                |\n| field_path | string | dot-separated key, e.g. `\"config.model\"` |\n\nReturns: `value, nil` on success; `nil, err_string` if file missing, JSON\ninvalid, or field not found.\n\n---\n\n## M.set(dir, filename, field_path, value) → ok, err\n\nWrites a single field atomically. Refuses writes to any field (or entire\nfile) whose `constant` flag is true.\n\n| param      | type   | description                                     |\n|------------|--------|-------------------------------------------------|\n| dir        | string | directory path                                  |\n| filename   | string | file name                                       |\n| field_path | string | dot-separated key                               |\n| value      | any    | new value (must be JSON-encodable)              |\n\nReturns: `true, nil` on success; `nil, err_string` if file unreadable,\nconstant violation, or write failure.\n\n**Error conditions:**\n- File does not exist → error\n- JSON parse failure → error\n- `constant: true` on file or targeted field → error (value unchanged)\n- Intermediate key in path does not exist → error\n- Rename fails after write → error\n\n---\n\n## Notes\n\n- `field_path` supports only string keys separated by `.` — no array indexing.\n- `filename` has path separators stripped; only files in `dir` are reachable.\n- Writes go to `<path>.tmp` first, then `os.rename` to the real path —\n  atomic on POSIX, so readers always see a complete file.\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/soramech-data.info.md"
        }
      }],

  "toolUseResult":{
    "content":"# soramech-data.lua\n\nData file access library for SoraMech map boxes. Works with any directory\nof JSON data files — `data/` for persistent storage, `tmp/` for ephemeral.\n\nAll JSON files use the wrapper format:\n```json\n{\n  \"constant\": false,\n  \"fields\": {\n    \"key\": { \"constant\": false, \"value\": <any> }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## M.load(dir, filename) → table, err\n\nLoads and decodes the entire file. Returns the raw decoded table (with\n`constant` and `fields` wrappers intact). Useful when you need to inspect\nthe structure or iterate all fields.\n\n| param    | type   | description                                  |\n|----------|--------|----------------------------------------------|\n| dir      | string | directory path (e.g. `map_dir .. \"/data\"`)   |\n| filename | string | file name, e.g. `\"state.json\"` (no slashes)  |\n\nReturns: `table, nil` on success; `nil, err_string` on failure.\n\n---\n\n## M.get(dir, filename, field_path) → value, err\n\nReads a single field by dot-separated path. Unwraps the `{constant, value}`\nwrapper automatically — you get the plain value back.\n\n| param      | type   | description                              |\n|------------|--------|------------------------------------------|\n| dir        | string | directory path                           |\n| filename   | string | file name                                |\n| field_path | string | dot-separated key, e.g. `\"config.model\"` |\n\nReturns: `value, nil` on success; `nil, err_string` if file missing, JSON\ninvalid, or field not found.\n\n---\n\n## M.set(dir, filename, field_path, value) → ok, err\n\nWrites a single field atomically. Refuses writes to any field (or entire\nfile) whose `constant` flag is true.\n\n| param      | type   | description                                     |\n|------------|--------|-------------------------------------------------|\n| dir        | string | directory path                                  |\n| filename   | string | file name                                       |\n| field_path | string | dot-separated key                               |\n| value      | any    | new value (must be JSON-encodable)              |\n\nReturns: `true, nil` on success; `nil, err_string` if file unreadable,\nconstant violation, or write failure.\n\n**Error conditions:**\n- File does not exist → error\n- JSON parse failure → error\n- `constant: true` on file or targeted field → error (value unchanged)\n- Intermediate key in path does not exist → error\n- Rename fails after write → error\n\n---\n\n## Notes\n\n- `field_path` supports only string keys separated by `.` — no array indexing.\n- `filename` has path separators stripped; only files in `dir` are reachable.\n- Writes go to `<path>.tmp` first, then `os.rename` to the real path —\n  atomic on POSIX, so readers always see a complete file.\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/soramech-data.info.md",
    "structuredPatch":[]
  }
}

Field path walks the `fields` wrapper structure used\nby all data files. Constant enforcement checks both the file-level flag and\neach field's wrapper flag before writing. Writes are atomic via\nwrite-to-.tmp-then-os.rename.\n\n`tests/003-data-test.lua` covers: load table, get numeric, get string, set\nround-trip, constant field rejection, file-level constant rejection, missing\nfield error, missing file error. All 9 tests pass.\n\n`libs/soramech-data.info.md` documents all three public functions with param\ntables and error conditions.\n\nThe lua driver already exported `libs/` on `LUA_PATH` before the shim runs,\nso `require(\"soramech-data\")` works in any lua box function without changes.",
    "originalFile":"# 109 — Data files: persistent and ephemeral storage\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 101 (map directory and tmp/ symlink created there)\n- 104 (executor must exist; data file access added to driver interface here)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo data file access exists. Boxes cannot read or write named data from\nwithin their functions. There is no distinction between persistent and\nephemeral storage in the map directory.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA map's data/ directory contains JSON files. Each file is a lua table\nserialized with dkjson. A section-level \"constant\" flag marks individual\nfields as read-only. A file-level \"constant\" flag makes the entire file\nread-only.\n\nBoxes access data files through a lua library (libs/soramech-data.lua)\nthat the driver for lua boxes includes in the lua environment. The library\nis not built into the runner — it is imported by the lua driver like any\nother library.\n\n  data.get(map_dir, filename, field_path) -> value\n  data.set(map_dir, filename, field_path, value) -> ok, err\n  data.load(map_dir, filename) -> table, err\n\ndata.set refuses writes to constant fields and returns an error string.\nThe caller decides whether to propagate the error or halt.\n\nEphemeral data (state during a run, logs, last-run snapshot) goes to\ntmp/, which is a symlink to /tmp/<map-name>/. The same library works\nwith tmp/ as a directory argument — no special case. Tmp files are not\nbacked up and are expected to disappear on reboot.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Write libs/soramech-data.lua — implements data.get, data.set, data.load.\n   Uses dkjson for all encode/decode. data.set reads the current file,\n   modifies the specified field path (dot-separated key), validates the\n   constant flag, and writes the file back atomically (write to .tmp then\n   rename).\n2. Define field_path as a dot-separated key string: \"config.model\" accesses\n   table[\"config\"][\"model\"]. Supports only string keys (no array indexing\n   in v1).\n3. Write tests/003-data-test.lua — creates a temp data file, calls\n   data.set, reads back with data.get, asserts value matches. Tries to\n   write a constant field, asserts error returned.\n4. Document in libs/soramech-data.info.md: each public function with\n   inputs, outputs, and error conditions.\n5. Update drivers/lua.sh to add libs/ to the luajit package path so\n   soramech-data.lua is available to any lua box function without\n   explicit path manipulation.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/001-architecture.md — data file format and tmp/ symlink\n- issues/101 — tmp/ symlink creation\n- issues/102 — lua driver (package path updated in step 5)\n- issues/104 — executor (data library available to boxes during execution)\n\n## Notes\n\nAtomic writes (write-to-tmp-then-rename) are important for data files\nthat a running map and the browser editor might both touch. Rename is\natomic on POSIX filesystems; the reader always sees either the old or\nthe new file, never a partial write.\n\nConstant field validation: when data.set is called on a constant field,\nreturn an error string rather than panicking. The driver should propagate\nthis to the runner as a non-zero exit (write the error to stderr). The\nrunner then halts the map with a descriptive message. Prefer hard errors\nover silent skips here.\n\nThe library design (separate from the runner, imported by the driver) is\nintentional. It means the library works identically in a standalone lua\nscript, in a test, and inside a running map. No runner context is needed\nto use it.\n",

Field path walks the `fields` wrapper structure used","+by all data files. Constant enforcement checks both the file-level flag and","+each field's wrapper flag before writing. Writes are atomic via","+write-to-.tmp-then-os.rename.","+","+`tests/003-data-test.lua` covers: load table, get numeric, get string, set","+round-trip, constant field rejection, file-level constant rejection, missing","+field error, missing file error. All 9 tests pass.","+","+`libs/soramech-data.info.md` documents all three public functions with param","+tables and error conditions.","+","+The lua driver already exported `libs/` on `LUA_PATH` before the shim runs,","+so `require(\"soramech-data\")` works in any lua box function without changes.","+"," ## Blockers"," "," - 101 (map directory and tmp/ symlink created there)"]

In v1: synchronous. Future: hand this signature to\n55\t-- the thread pool. Returns outputs table and ok/err.\n56\tlocal function run_task(box, inputs, drivers, map_dir)\n57\t    local ref = box.ref\n58\t    local fn  = box.fn\n59\t\n60\t    -- locate the driver for this ref\n61\t    local driver = driver_path_for(ref, drivers)\n62\t    if not driver then\n63\t        return nil, \"no driver found for ref '\" .. ref .. \"'\"\n64\t    end\n65\t\n66\t    -- resolve ref relative to map_dir\n67\t    local abs_ref = map_dir .. \"/\" .. ref\n68\t\n69\t    -- build argument list: file fn arg_count [args...]\n70\t    local args = {}\n71\t    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n72\t        local val = inputs[port.name]\n73\t        if val == nil then\n74\t            -- nil input becomes JSON null\n75\t            args[#args + 1] = shell_quote(json.encode(nil))\n76\t        else\n77\t            args[#args + 1] = shell_quote(json.encode(val))\n78\t        end\n79\t    end\n80\t",

      "content":"-- Synchronous FSM executor for the SoraMech runner.\n-- Walks the graph from the entry box, invokes language drivers for each\n-- box in dependency order, and threads output values through wires.\n-- Each box call is isolated in run_task() — the future thread pool swap point.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal M    = {}\n\n-- {{{ eval_predicate\nlocal function eval_predicate(pred, value)\n    -- structured predicates only; no arbitrary lua eval\n    local op  = pred.op\n    local lit = pred.value\n\n    if op == \"eq\"       then return value == lit\n    elseif op == \"lt\"   then return value <  lit\n    elseif op == \"gt\"   then return value >  lit\n    elseif op == \"lte\"  then return value <= lit\n    elseif op == \"gte\"  then return value >= lit\n    elseif op == \"contains\" then\n        return type(value) == \"string\" and value:find(lit, 1, true) ~= nil\n    elseif op == \"matches\" then\n        return type(value) == \"string\" and value:match(lit) ~= nil\n    end\n    return false\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ shell_quote\nlocal function shell_quote(s)\n    -- wrap a string in single quotes, escaping any embedded single quotes\n    return \"'\" .. tostring(s):gsub(\"'\", \"'\\\\''\") .. \"'\"\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ driver_path_for\nlocal function driver_path_for(ref, drivers)\n    -- binary callers (no extension mapping needed — they are executable directly)\n    -- source callers: look up extension in driver table\n    local ext = ref:match(\"%.([^./]+)$\")\n    if not ext then return ref end  -- no extension: treat as binary\n    local driver = drivers[\".\" .. ext]\n    return driver\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ run_task\n-- The task boundary. In v1: synchronous. Future: hand this signature to\n-- the thread pool. Returns outputs table and ok/err.\nlocal function run_task(box, inputs, drivers, map_dir)\n    local ref = box.ref\n    local fn  = box.fn\n\n    -- locate the driver for this ref\n    local driver = driver_path_for(ref, drivers)\n    if not driver then\n        return nil, \"no driver found for ref '\" .. ref .. \"'\"\n    end\n\n    -- resolve ref relative to map_dir\n    local abs_ref = map_dir .. \"/\" .. ref\n\n    -- build argument list: file fn arg_count [args...]\n    local args = {}\n    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n        local val = inputs[port.name]\n        if val == nil then\n            -- nil input becomes JSON null\n            args[#args + 1] = shell_quote(json.encode(nil))\n        else\n            args[#args + 1] = shell_quote(json.encode(val))\n        end\n    end\n",

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-07T23:37:32.497Z",
  "slug":"reactive-toasting-squid",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",

    "content":[{
        "name":"Write",
        "id":"toolu_01KZz3oV2DBfcJbMYE5d56Um",
        "type":"tool_use",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "content":"# 111 — Bash driver output format and driver-test silent skip\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nTwo related problems found while building the phase-1 demo:\n\n1. **driver-test silent skip**: `maps/driver-test/` meta.json sets `entry_box_id`\n   to `lua-box`, which declares two inputs (`a`, `b`). The executor starts with\n   the entry box in the queue but immediately skips it because `inputs_satisfied`\n   returns false. No boxes run. The runner reports \"OK\" and writes\n   `{\"ok\":true,\"boxes\":[]}` to last-run.json. The map appears to pass but does\n   nothing.\n\n2. **bash function output format**: The existing `stringify` function in\n   `maps/driver-test/src/utils.sh` outputs `\"42\"` (a bare JSON string). The\n   executor expects a JSON array `[\"...\"]` where each element is itself a\n   JSON-encoded value. Passing a bare JSON string fails the type check\n   (`type(result_arr) ~= \"table\"`) — but this was never hit because no boxes ran.\n   The bash driver contract (function must output a JSON array) was not enforced\n   or tested.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n1. driver-test entry box should have no inputs (reads inputs from a data file via\n   `SORAMECH_MAP_DIR`), so it fires immediately. All three driver boxes\n   (lua → bash → C) should run and produce verifiable output.\n\n2. Bash functions must output a JSON array matching the same format as the lua\n   driver: `[\"<json-encoded-result>\"]` for a single return value. The bash driver\n   comment and driver spec in docs/003-driver-system.md should state this\n   explicitly. A test in tests/ should verify a bash box end-to-end.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Redesign driver-test: change lua-box to read its inputs from a data file\n   (no wired inputs), so it is the true entry with no dependencies.\n2. Update `utils.sh` stringify to output `[\"\\\"<result>\\\"\"]` format.\n3. Run driver-test end-to-end and confirm all three boxes appear in last-run.json.\n4. Update docs/003-driver-system.md to document the required JSON array format\n   for all driver outputs.\n5. Add a test (tests/004-bash-driver-test.lua or a bash script) that invokes\n   drivers/bash.sh directly and asserts the output format.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/003-driver-system.md — driver output format spec\n- maps/driver-test/ — the broken map\n- issues/102 — original driver interface design\n\n## Notes\n\nThe classify-demo (issue 110) was built using a correct bash function that\noutputs `[\"...\"]` from the start, so it works. driver-test is the only broken\ncase. Fix driver-test after classify-demo demo is documented.\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/111-bash-output-format-and-driver-test-entry.md"
        }
      }],

  "toolUseResult":{
    "content":"# 111 — Bash driver output format and driver-test silent skip\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nTwo related problems found while building the phase-1 demo:\n\n1. **driver-test silent skip**: `maps/driver-test/` meta.json sets `entry_box_id`\n   to `lua-box`, which declares two inputs (`a`, `b`). The executor starts with\n   the entry box in the queue but immediately skips it because `inputs_satisfied`\n   returns false. No boxes run. The runner reports \"OK\" and writes\n   `{\"ok\":true,\"boxes\":[]}` to last-run.json. The map appears to pass but does\n   nothing.\n\n2. **bash function output format**: The existing `stringify` function in\n   `maps/driver-test/src/utils.sh` outputs `\"42\"` (a bare JSON string). The\n   executor expects a JSON array `[\"...\"]` where each element is itself a\n   JSON-encoded value. Passing a bare JSON string fails the type check\n   (`type(result_arr) ~= \"table\"`) — but this was never hit because no boxes ran.\n   The bash driver contract (function must output a JSON array) was not enforced\n   or tested.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n1. driver-test entry box should have no inputs (reads inputs from a data file via\n   `SORAMECH_MAP_DIR`), so it fires immediately. All three driver boxes\n   (lua → bash → C) should run and produce verifiable output.\n\n2. Bash functions must output a JSON array matching the same format as the lua\n   driver: `[\"<json-encoded-result>\"]` for a single return value. The bash driver\n   comment and driver spec in docs/003-driver-system.md should state this\n   explicitly. A test in tests/ should verify a bash box end-to-end.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Redesign driver-test: change lua-box to read its inputs from a data file\n   (no wired inputs), so it is the true entry with no dependencies.\n2. Update `utils.sh` stringify to output `[\"\\\"<result>\\\"\"]` format.\n3. Run driver-test end-to-end and confirm all three boxes appear in last-run.json.\n4. Update docs/003-driver-system.md to document the required JSON array format\n   for all driver outputs.\n5. Add a test (tests/004-bash-driver-test.lua or a bash script) that invokes\n   drivers/bash.sh directly and asserts the output format.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/003-driver-system.md — driver output format spec\n- maps/driver-test/ — the broken map\n- issues/102 — original driver interface design\n\n## Notes\n\nThe classify-demo (issue 110) was built using a correct bash function that\noutputs `[\"...\"]` from the start, so it works. driver-test is the only broken\ncase. Fix driver-test after classify-demo demo is documented.\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/111-bash-output-format-and-driver-test-entry.md",
    "structuredPatch":[]
  }
}

  "toolUseResult":{

        },
        "input":{
          "content":"# Phase 1 Demo — classify-demo\n\nDemonstrates every phase 1 capability in one coherent run:\nlua driver, bash driver, branch routing, data file access.\n\n## Map: maps/classify-demo/\n\n```\nread-input (lua)\n    reads name from data/input.json\n    returns \"hello, <name>\"\n        ↓ greeting\nstamp (bash)\n    appends ISO timestamp\n        ↓ stamped\nrouter (branch)\n    contains \"SoraMech\" → greeting port → write-result\n    else              → else port    → write-error\n        ↓ (greeting)            ↓ (else)\nwrite-result (lua)      write-error (lua)\ndata/output.json        data/error.json\n```\n\n## Running\n\n```bash\nluajit soramech-runner.lua maps/classify-demo/\n```\n\nInput name is set in `maps/classify-demo/data/input.json`.\n\n## Expected outputs (name = \"SoraMech\")\n\n`data/output.json`:\n```json\n{\"fields\":{\"result\":{\"value\":\"hello, SoraMech [<timestamp>]\",\"constant\":false}},\"constant\":false}\n```\n\n## Testing the else path (name = \"stranger\")\n\nSet `data/input.json` field `name` to `\"stranger\"`. Re-run. The greeting\n`\"hello, stranger [ts]\"` does not contain \"SoraMech\", so the else port fires.\n`data/error.json` receives the message instead of output.json.\n\n## Phase 1 checklist\n\n- [x] Create a box in the browser and save it to disk (editor, issue 106/107)\n- [x] Wire two boxes together in the browser (issue 107)\n- [x] Run a 3-box+ map from the CLI and see outputs written to disk (this map)\n- [x] Write a custom driver and have the runner use it (bash stamp.sh)\n- [x] Branch box routes correctly based on a predicate (router box)\n- [x] Data file read and write from within a box function (input.json / output.json)\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/completed/demos/phase-1-classify-demo/README.md"
        }
      }],

  "toolUseResult":{
    "content":"# Phase 1 Demo — classify-demo\n\nDemonstrates every phase 1 capability in one coherent run:\nlua driver, bash driver, branch routing, data file access.\n\n## Map: maps/classify-demo/\n\n```\nread-input (lua)\n    reads name from data/input.json\n    returns \"hello, <name>\"\n        ↓ greeting\nstamp (bash)\n    appends ISO timestamp\n        ↓ stamped\nrouter (branch)\n    contains \"SoraMech\" → greeting port → write-result\n    else              → else port    → write-error\n        ↓ (greeting)            ↓ (else)\nwrite-result (lua)      write-error (lua)\ndata/output.json        data/error.json\n```\n\n## Running\n\n```bash\nluajit soramech-runner.lua maps/classify-demo/\n```\n\nInput name is set in `maps/classify-demo/data/input.json`.\n\n## Expected outputs (name = \"SoraMech\")\n\n`data/output.json`:\n```json\n{\"fields\":{\"result\":{\"value\":\"hello, SoraMech [<timestamp>]\",\"constant\":false}},\"constant\":false}\n```\n\n## Testing the else path (name = \"stranger\")\n\nSet `data/input.json` field `name` to `\"stranger\"`. Re-run. The greeting\n`\"hello, stranger [ts]\"` does not contain \"SoraMech\", so the else port fires.\n`data/error.json` receives the message instead of output.json.\n\n## Phase 1 checklist\n\n- [x] Create a box in the browser and save it to disk (editor, issue 106/107)\n- [x] Wire two boxes together in the browser (issue 107)\n- [x] Run a 3-box+ map from the CLI and see outputs written to disk (this map)\n- [x] Write a custom driver and have the runner use it (bash stamp.sh)\n- [x] Branch box routes correctly based on a predicate (router box)\n- [x] Data file read and write from within a box function (input.json / output.json)\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/completed/demos/phase-1-classify-demo/README.md",

  }
}

The run script\nlives in the project root as demo.sh:\n  #!/usr/bin/env bash\n  # Runs the phase 1 demo\n  luajit soramech-runner.lua maps/classify-demo/\n\n## Related documents\n\n- issues/phase-1-progress.md — phase checklist updated here\n- docs/002-roadmap.md — phase 1 goal definition\n\n## Notes\n\nThe demo is part of the deliverable, not just a development artifact.           "content":"-- Regression test for the driver-test map.\n-- Verifies all three driver boxes (lua, bash, C) run and produce correct output.\n-- Guards against the silent-skip bug where entry box inputs are unsatisfied.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" .. package.path\n\nlocal json   = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal loader = dofile(DIR .. \"/src/003-loader.lua\")\nlocal exec   = dofile(DIR .. \"/src/004-executor.lua\")\n\n-- {{{ local function fail\nlocal function fail(msg)\n    io.stderr:write(\"[FAIL] \" .. msg .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ local function pass\nlocal function pass(msg)\n    io.write(\"[PASS] \" .. msg .. \"\\n\")\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ local function read_json\nlocal function read_json(path)\n    local f = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then fail(\"cannot open: \" .. path) end\n    local raw = f:read(\"*a\"); f:close()\n    local obj, _, err = json.decode(raw)\n    if not obj then fail(\"JSON error in \" .. path .. \": \" .. tostring(err)) end\n    return obj\nend\n-- }}}\n\nlocal map_dir = DIR .. \"/maps/driver-test\"\n\n-- load and validate graph\nlocal graph, errs = loader.load_map(map_dir)\nif not graph then\n    fail(\"load_map failed: \" .. table.concat(errs or {}, \"; \"))\nend\nlocal ok, verrs = loader.validate_graph(graph)\nif not ok then\n    fail(\"validate_graph failed: \" .. table.concat(verrs or {}, \"; \"))\nend\npass(\"graph loads and validates\")\n\n-- run the map\nlocal run_ok, run_err = exec.execute(graph, map_dir)\nif not run_ok then fail(\"execute failed: \" .. tostring(run_err)) end\npass(\"execute returned ok\")\n\n-- read last-run.json\nlocal run_log = read_json(map_dir .. \"/tmp/last-run.json\")\nif not run_log.ok then fail(\"last-run.json reports not ok: \" .. tostring(run_log.error)) end\n\n-- verify all three boxes ran\nlocal boxes = run_log.boxes\nif type(boxes) ~= \"table\" then fail(\"last-run.json boxes is not a table\") end\n\nif not boxes[\"lua-box\"] then fail(\"lua-box did not run\") end\nif not boxes[\"bash-box\"] then fail(\"bash-box did not run\") end\nif not boxes[\"c-box\"]    then fail(\"c-box did not run\") end\npass(\"all three driver boxes ran\")\n\n-- verify output chain: 3+5=8, stringified: 8, STRINGIFIED: 8\nlocal sum = boxes[\"lua-box\"].outputs and boxes[\"lua-box\"].outputs.sum\nif sum ~= 8 then fail(\"lua-box sum expected 8, got \" .. tostring(sum)) end\npass(\"lua-box output: sum=8\")\n\nlocal text = boxes[\"bash-box\"].outputs and boxes[\"bash-box\"].outputs.text\nif text ~= \"stringified: 8\" then\n    fail(\"bash-box text expected 'stringified: 8', got \" .. tostring(text))\nend\npass(\"bash-box output: text='stringified: 8'\")\n\nlocal result = boxes[\"c-box\"].outputs and boxes[\"c-box\"].outputs.result\nif result ~= \"STRINGIFIED: 8\" then\n    fail(\"c-box result expected 'STRINGIFIED: 8', got \" .. tostring(result))\nend\npass(\"c-box output: result='STRINGIFIED: 8'\")\n\nio.write(\"\\nAll driver-test regression tests passed.\\n\")\nos.exit(0)\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/tests/004-driver-test-runner.lua"

    "content":"-- Regression test for the driver-test map.\n-- Verifies all three driver boxes (lua, bash, C) run and produce correct output.\n-- Guards against the silent-skip bug where entry box inputs are unsatisfied.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" .. package.path\n\nlocal json   = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal loader = dofile(DIR .. \"/src/003-loader.lua\")\nlocal exec   = dofile(DIR .. \"/src/004-executor.lua\")\n\n-- {{{ local function fail\nlocal function fail(msg)\n    io.stderr:write(\"[FAIL] \" .. msg .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ local function pass\nlocal function pass(msg)\n    io.write(\"[PASS] \" .. msg .. \"\\n\")\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ local function read_json\nlocal function read_json(path)\n    local f = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then fail(\"cannot open: \" .. path) end\n    local raw = f:read(\"*a\"); f:close()\n    local obj, _, err = json.decode(raw)\n    if not obj then fail(\"JSON error in \" .. path .. \": \" .. tostring(err)) end\n    return obj\nend\n-- }}}\n\nlocal map_dir = DIR .. \"/maps/driver-test\"\n\n-- load and validate graph\nlocal graph, errs = loader.load_map(map_dir)\nif not graph then\n    fail(\"load_map failed: \" .. table.concat(errs or {}, \"; \"))\nend\nlocal ok, verrs = loader.validate_graph(graph)\nif not ok then\n    fail(\"validate_graph failed: \" .. table.concat(verrs or {}, \"; \"))\nend\npass(\"graph loads and validates\")\n\n-- run the map\nlocal run_ok, run_err = exec.execute(graph, map_dir)\nif not run_ok then fail(\"execute failed: \" .. tostring(run_err)) end\npass(\"execute returned ok\")\n\n-- read last-run.json\nlocal run_log = read_json(map_dir .. \"/tmp/last-run.json\")\nif not run_log.ok then fail(\"last-run.json reports not ok: \" .. tostring(run_log.error)) end\n\n-- verify all three boxes ran\nlocal boxes = run_log.boxes\nif type(boxes) ~= \"table\" then fail(\"last-run.json boxes is not a table\") end\n\nif not boxes[\"lua-box\"] then fail(\"lua-box did not run\") end\nif not boxes[\"bash-box\"] then fail(\"bash-box did not run\") end\nif not boxes[\"c-box\"]    then fail(\"c-box did not run\") end\npass(\"all three driver boxes ran\")\n\n-- verify output chain: 3+5=8, stringified: 8, STRINGIFIED: 8\nlocal sum = boxes[\"lua-box\"].outputs and boxes[\"lua-box\"].outputs.sum\nif sum ~= 8 then fail(\"lua-box sum expected 8, got \" .. tostring(sum)) end\npass(\"lua-box output: sum=8\")\n\nlocal text = boxes[\"bash-box\"].outputs and boxes[\"bash-box\"].outputs.text\nif text ~= \"stringified: 8\" then\n    fail(\"bash-box text expected 'stringified: 8', got \" .. tostring(text))\nend\npass(\"bash-box output: text='stringified: 8'\")\n\nlocal result = boxes[\"c-box\"].outputs and boxes[\"c-box\"].outputs.result\nif result ~= \"STRINGIFIED: 8\" then\n    fail(\"c-box result expected 'STRINGIFIED: 8', got \" .. tostring(result))\nend\npass(\"c-box output: result='STRINGIFIED: 8'\")\n\nio.write(\"\\nAll driver-test regression tests passed.\\n\")\nos.exit(0)\n",

The executor's `json.decode(raw)`\nfails gracefully on a plain string (not valid JSON), so `outputs[\"text\"]`\nreceives the raw string directly.     "originalFile":"# 111 — Bash driver output format and driver-test silent skip\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nTwo related problems found while building the phase-1 demo:\n\n1. **driver-test silent skip**: `maps/driver-test/` meta.json sets `entry_box_id`\n   to `lua-box`, which declares two inputs (`a`, `b`). The executor starts with\n   the entry box in the queue but immediately skips it because `inputs_satisfied`\n   returns false. No boxes run. The map appears to pass but does\n   nothing.\n\n2. **bash function output format**: The existing `stringify` function in\n   `maps/driver-test/src/utils.sh` outputs `\"42\"` (a bare JSON string). The\n   executor expects a JSON array `[\"...\"]` where each element is itself a\n   JSON-encoded value. Passing a bare JSON string fails the type check\n   (`type(result_arr) ~= \"table\"`) — but this was never hit because no boxes ran.\n   The bash driver contract (function must output a JSON array) was not enforced\n   or tested.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n1. driver-test entry box should have no inputs (reads inputs from a data file via\n   `SORAMECH_MAP_DIR`), so it fires immediately. All three driver boxes\n   (lua → bash → C) should run and produce verifiable output.\n\n2. Bash functions must output a JSON array matching the same format as the lua\n   driver: `[\"<json-encoded-result>\"]` for a single return value. The bash driver\n   comment and driver spec in docs/003-driver-system.md should state this\n   explicitly. A test in tests/ should verify a bash box end-to-end.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Redesign driver-test: change lua-box to read its inputs from a data file\n   (no wired inputs), so it is the true entry with no dependencies.\n2. Update `utils.sh` stringify to output `[\"\\\"<result>\\\"\"]` format.\n3. Run driver-test end-to-end and confirm all three boxes appear in last-run.json.\n4. Update docs/003-driver-system.md to document the required JSON array format\n   for all driver outputs.\n5. Add a test (tests/004-bash-driver-test.lua or a bash script) that invokes\n   drivers/bash.sh directly and asserts the output format.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/003-driver-system.md — driver output format spec\n- maps/driver-test/ — the broken map\n- issues/102 — original driver interface design\n\n## Notes\n\nThe classify-demo (issue 110) was built using a correct bash function that\noutputs `[\"...\"]` from the start, so it works. driver-test is the only broken\ncase. Fix driver-test after classify-demo demo is documented.\n",

        "text":"Default port is **7700**.\n\n---\n\n**Starting the server, opening the editor, and running maps:**\n\n**1 — Start the HTTP server** (leave this running in a terminal):\n```bash\nluajit /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/soramech-server.lua /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/maps\n```\nThat binds to `http://localhost:7700`. You can pass a different port as the second argument.\n\n**2 — Open the editor in your browser:**\n```\nfile:///mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/index.html\n```\nOr if your browser blocks `file://` + `localhost` fetch (CORS), serve it through the server itself — the server already serves `assets/` on `GET /`. So just open:\n```\nhttp://localhost:7700/\n```\nIn the editor sidebar, set the **Server URL** to `http://localhost:7700` and the **Map name** to whatever map you want to edit (e.g. `classify-demo`). Then click Load.\n\n**3 — Run a map** (separate terminal, any time you like):\n```bash\nluajit /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/soramech-runner.lua /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/maps/classify-demo\n```\nThe runner is completely independent of the server — it just reads the box files, executes the graph, and writes `tmp/last-run.json`. You can run it while the server is up or down.\n\nThe phase 1 demo script wraps this for you:\n```bash\nbash /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/demo.sh 1\n```"
