#(entry_box.inputs or {}) == 0 then\n        -- no inputs needed; ready immediately\n    end\n\n    local queue   = { entry_id }\n    local visited = {}  -- boxes that have been run (prevent double-execution)\n    local run_log = {}  -- per-box execution records for last-run.json\n    local map_ok  = true\n    local map_err = nil\n\n    while #queue > 0 do\n        -- dequeue\n        local id = table.remove(queue, 1)\n\n        local box = boxes[id]\n        if not box then\n            map_ok  = false\n            map_err = \"unknown box in queue: '\" .. id .. \"'\"\n            break\n        end\n\n        -- skip boxes whose inputs are not yet satisfied (they'll be re-enqueued)\n        if not inputs_satisfied(box, store) then\n            goto next_iter\n        end\n\n        if visited[id] and box.kind ~= \"branch\" then\n            goto next_iter\n        end\n        visited[id] = true\n\n        local inputs = collect_inputs(box, store)\n\n        -- branch box is handled specially: it doesn't invoke a driver,\n        -- it routes based on its single input value\n        local outputs, task_err\n        if box.kind == \"branch\" then\n            -- the branch input is the value wired to its single input port\n            local branch_val = inputs[(box.inputs or {})[1] and box.inputs[1].name or \"value\"]\n            outputs = { _branch_input = branch_val }\n            task_err = nil\n        else\n            outputs, task_err = run_task(box, inputs, drivers, map_dir)\n        end\n\n        run_log[id] = {\n            inputs  = inputs,\n            outputs = outputs or {},\n            status  = task_err and \"error\" or \"ok\",\n            error   = task_err,\n        }\n\n        if task_err then\n            map_ok  = false\n            map_err = task_err\n            io.stderr:write(\"executor: \" .. task_err .. \"\\n\")\n            break\n        end\n\n        -- fire connections and enqueue newly-ready boxes\n        local signal = fire_connections(box, outputs, store, queue, boxes, retry_counts)\n        if signal == \"retry\" then\n            local max_retries = box.retry_limit or 3\n            retry_counts[id] = (retry_counts[id] or 0) + 1\n            if retry_counts[id] > max_retries then\n                map_ok  = false\n                map_err = \"branch box '\" .. id .. \"' exceeded retry limit (\" ..\n                    max_retries .. \")\"\n                break\n            end\n            -- find the upstream box(es) that feed this branch box and re-queue them\n            for src_id, src_box in pairs(boxes) do\n                for _, c in ipairs(src_box.connections or {}) do\n                    if c.from_box ~= src_id then goto next_src_conn end\n                    if c.to_box ~= id then goto next_src_conn end\n\n                    visited[src_id] = nil\n\n                    -- clear the branch box's input from the store so it\n                    -- re-fills when the upstream box runs again\n                    for _, p in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n                        store[id .. \".\" .. p.name] = nil\n                    end\n\n                    -- apply retry_vary: randomize specified input fields on the\n                    -- upstream box before re-running it\n                    local vary = src_box.retry_vary\n                    if vary then\n                        for field_name, range in pairs(vary) do\n                            local lo = tonumber(range.min) or 0\n                            local hi = tonumber(range.max) or 1\n                            local val = lo + math.random() * (hi - lo)\n                            store[src_id .. \".\" .. field_name] = val\n                        end\n                    end\n\n                    queue[#queue + 1] = src_id\n                    ::next_src_conn::\n                end\n            end\n        end\n\n        ::next_iter::\n    end\n\n    -- write last-run snapshot to tmp/\n    write_last_run(map_dir, {\n        ok     = map_ok,\n        error  = map_err,\n        boxes  = run_log,\n    })\n\n    return map_ok, map_err\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",

        "input":{
          "content":"# 208 — Port literal values\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nInput ports on a box can only receive values from wired connections. If no wire\nis connected to an input port, the box never becomes \"ready\" and the runner\nskips it silently. There is no way to supply a constant value to an input from\nthe editor.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nEach input port has an optional literal value editable directly in the inspector\npanel. If the value field is non-empty and no wire is connected to that port,\nthe literal value is used at runtime. If a wire IS connected, the wire's value\noverwrites the literal at runtime — wires always win.\n\nThe value field accepts JSON notation (numbers, strings with quotes, arrays,\nobjects) or bare strings for convenience. The executor tries JSON.decode first;\nif that fails, the raw string is used.\n\nThis lets a box be fully configured from the inspector without needing a\ndedicated \"data\" box wired to it for every constant.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. **Data model** — port objects in `box.inputs` gain an optional `value`\n   string field. No schema change needed (extra fields are already tolerated).\n\n2. **Inspector (`004-inspector.js`)** — `mk_port_display()` gains a\n   `show_value` boolean parameter. When true, each port row shows a second\n   text input for the value alongside the name input. On change, updates\n   `ports[i].value` and calls `save()`.\n\n3. **Executor (`004-executor.lua`)** — add a pre-seeding pass before the main\n   execution loop: for every box, for every input port that has a non-empty\n   `value`, write `store[box_id..\".\"..port.name]` with the parsed value.\n   Existing `inputs_satisfied` and `collect_inputs` logic requires no changes\n   because they only read from the store.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — mk_port_display, show\n- src/004-executor.lua — execute, inputs_satisfied\n- docs/001-architecture.md — store model, box.inputs schema\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/208-port-literal-values.md"
        }
      }],

  "toolUseResult":{
    "content":"# 208 — Port literal values\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nInput ports on a box can only receive values from wired connections. If no wire\nis connected to an input port, the box never becomes \"ready\" and the runner\nskips it silently. There is no way to supply a constant value to an input from\nthe editor.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nEach input port has an optional literal value editable directly in the inspector\npanel. If the value field is non-empty and no wire is connected to that port,\nthe literal value is used at runtime. If a wire IS connected, the wire's value\noverwrites the literal at runtime — wires always win.\n\nThe value field accepts JSON notation (numbers, strings with quotes, arrays,\nobjects) or bare strings for convenience. The executor tries JSON.decode first;\nif that fails, the raw string is used.\n\nThis lets a box be fully configured from the inspector without needing a\ndedicated \"data\" box wired to it for every constant.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. **Data model** — port objects in `box.inputs` gain an optional `value`\n   string field. No schema change needed (extra fields are already tolerated).\n\n2. **Inspector (`004-inspector.js`)** — `mk_port_display()` gains a\n   `show_value` boolean parameter. When true, each port row shows a second\n   text input for the value alongside the name input. On change, updates\n   `ports[i].value` and calls `save()`.\n\n3. **Executor (`004-executor.lua`)** — add a pre-seeding pass before the main\n   execution loop: for every box, for every input port that has a non-empty\n   `value`, write `store[box_id..\".\"..port.name]` with the parsed value.\n   Existing `inputs_satisfied` and `collect_inputs` logic requires no changes\n   because they only read from the store.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — mk_port_display, show\n- src/004-executor.lua — execute, inputs_satisfied\n- docs/001-architecture.md — store model, box.inputs schema\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/208-port-literal-values.md",
    "structuredPatch":[]
  }
}

          "new_string":"  // {{{ mk_port_display\n  // Port name is editable; type is read-only (derived from source).\n  // show_value: when true (inputs only), adds a literal value field.\n  function mk_port_display(ports, show_value) {\n    const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    wrap.className = 'port-display';\n    if (!ports || ports.length === 0) {\n      const empty = document.createElement('span');\n      empty.className   = 'port-display-empty';\n      empty.textContent = '(none)';\n      wrap.appendChild(empty);\n    } else {\n      ports.forEach((p, i) => {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className = 'port-display-row';\n\n        const name_inp = document.createElement('input');\n        name_inp.type  = 'text';\n        name_inp.value = p.name || '';\n        name_inp.className = 'port-name-inp';\n        name_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { ports[i].name = name_inp.value; save(); });\n        row.appendChild(name_inp);\n\n        if (p.type && p.type !== 'any') {\n          const type_el = document.createElement('span');\n          type_el.className   = 'port-type';\n          type_el.textContent = ':' + p.type;\n          row.appendChild(type_el);\n        }\n\n        if (show_value) {\n          const val_inp = document.createElement('input');\n          val_inp.type        = 'text';\n          val_inp.value       = p.value !== undefined ? ## [1399]

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T01:05:08.093Z",
  "slug":"reactive-toasting-squid",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"`src/004-executor.lua` is the runtime engine for SoraMech — the thing that actually *runs* a map you've built in the editor.\n\nWhen you invoke `soramech-runner.lua` on a map, the executor:\n\n1. **Loads the graph** — reads all the box JSON files, the connections between them, and the driver table\n2. **Pre-seeds the store** — a flat key-value table keyed by `\"box_id.port_name\"`. Literal values you set in the inspector get written here before anything runs\n3. **Starts at the entry box** — whichever box is flagged as the entry point, it gets queued first\n4. **Works through the queue** — for each box:\n   - Checks whether all its input ports have values in the store (`inputs_satisfied`)\n   - If yes: calls the appropriate language driver (lua, bash, etc.), gets back the output values\n   - Pushes those outputs into the store under the target box's input keys\n   - Enqueues any downstream boxes that are now fully satisfied\n5. **Branch boxes** are special — they don't call a driver, they just look at their single input value and route it to the matching output port based on predicates (eq, contains, etc.)\n\nSo in terms of dataflow: the store is the \"wire memory.\" A wired connection writes a value into `\"to_box.to_port\"` at runtime. A literal value pre-writes into `\"box_id.port_name\"` before the loop. If a wire later fires to the same key, it overwrites it — wires win.\n\nThe executor is currently synchronous (one box at a time, in queue order). The comment at the top of `run_task` marks it as the future thread pool swap point — when multiple boxes are independently ready, they'd be handed off to worker threads instead of run in sequence."
      }],

        },
        "input":{
          "content":"-- Ollama API client — shared library and ready-to-use box source.\n-- require(\"ollama\") from any Lua function, or copy to a map's src/ directory\n-- to use it directly as a call box via the file browser.\n-- Uses curl; no extra Lua packages needed beyond dkjson.\n\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal M    = {}\n\nlocal DEFAULT_HOST  = \"http://localhost:11434\"\nlocal DEFAULT_MODEL = \"llama3.2\"\n\n-- {{{ shell_quote\nlocal function shell_quote(s)\n    return \"'\" .. tostring(s):gsub(\"'\", \"'\\\\''\") .. \"'\"\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ curl_post\nlocal function curl_post(url, payload)\n    local cmd = \"curl -s --max-time 120 -X POST \" .. shell_quote(url) ..\n                \" -H \" .. shell_quote(\"Content-Type: application/json\") ..\n                \" -d \" .. shell_quote(payload)\n    local ph  = io.popen(cmd)\n    local out = ph:read(\"*a\")\n    ph:close()\n    return out\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.query\n-- Plain text generation. model and host are optional; nil or empty uses defaults.\nfunction M.query(prompt, model, host)\n    model = (model ~= nil and model ~= \"\") and model or DEFAULT_MODEL\n    host  = (host  ~= nil and host  ~= \"\") and host  or DEFAULT_HOST\n    local out  = curl_post(host .. \"/api/generate\", json.encode({\n        model  = model,\n        prompt = tostring(prompt),\n        stream = false,\n    }))\n    local resp, _, err = json.decode(out)\n    if not resp then\n        io.stderr:write(\"ollama.query: bad response: \" .. tostring(err) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n    if resp.error then\n        io.stderr:write(\"ollama.query: \" .. tostring(resp.error) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n    return resp.response\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.chat\n-- Chat-style query. system prompt is optional; nil or empty omits it.\n-- model and host default when nil or empty.\nfunction M.chat(prompt, system, model, host)\n    model = (model ~= nil and model ~= \"\") and model or DEFAULT_MODEL\n    host  = (host  ~= nil and host  ~= \"\") and host  or DEFAULT_HOST\n    local messages = {}\n    if system ~= nil and system ~= \"\" then\n        messages[#messages + 1] = { role = \"system\", content = tostring(system) }\n    end\n    messages[#messages + 1] = { role = \"user\", content = tostring(prompt) }\n    local out  = curl_post(host .. \"/api/chat\", json.encode({\n        model    = model,\n        messages = messages,\n        stream   = false,\n    }))\n    local resp, _, err = json.decode(out)\n    if not resp then\n        io.stderr:write(\"ollama.chat: bad response: \" .. tostring(err) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n    if resp.error then\n        io.stderr:write(\"ollama.chat: \" .. tostring(resp.error) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n    return resp.message and resp.message.content or nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/ollama.lua"
        }
      }],

    "content":"-- Ollama API client — shared library and ready-to-use box source.\n-- require(\"ollama\") from any Lua function, or copy to a map's src/ directory\n-- to use it directly as a call box via the file browser.\n-- Uses curl; no extra Lua packages needed beyond dkjson.\n\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal M    = {}\n\nlocal DEFAULT_HOST  = \"http://localhost:11434\"\nlocal DEFAULT_MODEL = \"llama3.2\"\n\n-- {{{ shell_quote\nlocal function shell_quote(s)\n    return \"'\" .. tostring(s):gsub(\"'\", \"'\\\\''\") .. \"'\"\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ curl_post\nlocal function curl_post(url, payload)\n    local cmd = \"curl -s --max-time 120 -X POST \" .. shell_quote(url) ..\n                \" -H \" .. shell_quote(\"Content-Type: application/json\") ..\n                \" -d \" .. shell_quote(payload)\n    local ph  = io.popen(cmd)\n    local out = ph:read(\"*a\")\n    ph:close()\n    return out\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.query\n-- Plain text generation. model and host are optional; nil or empty uses defaults.\nfunction M.query(prompt, model, host)\n    model = (model ~= nil and model ~= \"\") and model or DEFAULT_MODEL\n    host  = (host  ~= nil and host  ~= \"\") and host  or DEFAULT_HOST\n    local out  = curl_post(host .. \"/api/generate\", json.encode({\n        model  = model,\n        prompt = tostring(prompt),\n        stream = false,\n    }))\n    local resp, _, err = json.decode(out)\n    if not resp then\n        io.stderr:write(\"ollama.query: bad response: \" .. tostring(err) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n    if resp.error then\n        io.stderr:write(\"ollama.query: \" .. tostring(resp.error) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n    return resp.response\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.chat\n-- Chat-style query. system prompt is optional; nil or empty omits it.\n-- model and host default when nil or empty.\nfunction M.chat(prompt, system, model, host)\n    model = (model ~= nil and model ~= \"\") and model or DEFAULT_MODEL\n    host  = (host  ~= nil and host  ~= \"\") and host  or DEFAULT_HOST\n    local messages = {}\n    if system ~= nil and system ~= \"\" then\n        messages[#messages + 1] = { role = \"system\", content = tostring(system) }\n    end\n    messages[#messages + 1] = { role = \"user\", content = tostring(prompt) }\n    local out  = curl_post(host .. \"/api/chat\", json.encode({\n        model    = model,\n        messages = messages,\n        stream   = false,\n    }))\n    local resp, _, err = json.decode(out)\n    if not resp then\n        io.stderr:write(\"ollama.chat: bad response: \" .. tostring(err) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n    if resp.error then\n        io.stderr:write(\"ollama.chat: \" .. tostring(resp.error) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n    return resp.message and resp.message.content or nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/ollama.lua",

  }

The file browser will auto-populate the ports:\n\n- **`query`** — inputs: `prompt, model, host` → output: `result`\n- **`chat`** — inputs: `prompt, system, model, host` → output: `result`\n\nWire `prompt` from an upstream box. Set `model`, `host`, and `system` as **literal port values** in the inspector (leave them blank to use the defaults: `llama3.2` + `localhost:11434`).     "role":"user",
    "content":"Okay. Can we make another box type that's like the previous one, except it's more like control flow? It should take in some text, generated by the previous box. Then, it should have another input option (probably user defined) that takes in more text. The first text is the output of the previous LLM call - the second text is the comparison operator. So the user would say something like \"if the text has this-or-that quality, return 1. If the text has that-or-this quality, return 2.\" we should be able to have multiple output ports, with the user being able to add more. Any ideas how we could implement the \"add more output ports\" mechanic?\n\nalso, we need a better method of including new lib files. Maybe... when the user clicks \"browse\" can we have a button at the top that says \"add a new library directory\" or similar which will mark a specified directory as being included in the project, even if it's not in the src/ directory? Then, it should show up in the browse filesystem view. Also, if we have directories in that view, can we collapse them with a plus button to the left?"
  },

      "content":"// Thin fetch wrapper for the soramech-server REST API.\n// All functions are async and throw on non-2xx responses.\n\nconst API = (() => {\n  let base_url = '';\n  let map_name = '';\n\n  // {{{ init\n  function init(url, name) { base_url = url.replace(/\\/$/, ''); map_name = name; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ request\n  async function request(method, path, body) {\n    const opts = { method, headers: {} };\n    if (body !== undefined) {\n      opts.headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json';\n      opts.body = JSON.stringify(body);\n    }\n    const res = await fetch(base_url + path, opts);\n    const text = await res.text();\n    let data;\n    try { data = JSON.parse(text); } catch { data = { error: text }; }\n    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(data.error || `HTTP ${res.status}`);\n    return data;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_maps\n  async function list_maps() { return request('GET', '/maps'); }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_boxes\n  async function list_boxes() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_box\n  async function get_box(id) {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ put_box\n  async function put_box(id, data) {\n    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`, data);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ delete_box\n  async function delete_box(id) {\n    return request('DELETE', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_meta\n  async function get_meta() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/meta`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ put_meta\n  async function put_meta(data) {\n    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/meta`, data);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_src_files\n  async function list_src_files() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/src`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_src_file\n  // Returns raw text, not JSON — the request() helper would mis-parse source code.\n  async function get_src_file(filename) {\n    const res = await fetch(base_url + `/maps/${map_name}/src/${encodeURIComponent(filename)}`);\n    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);\n    return res.text();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_data\n  async function get_data(filename) {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/data/${filename}`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ put_data\n  async function put_data(filename, data) {\n    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/data/${filename}`, data);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { init, list_maps, list_boxes, get_box, put_box, delete_box,\n           get_meta, put_meta, get_data, put_data,\n           list_src_files, get_src_file };\n})();\n",

        "input":{
          "content":"# 210 — LLM route box\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nRouting between box paths is done by the `branch` box kind using hard-coded\npredicates (eq, contains, matches). There is no way to use an LLM judgment\nto decide which path to take.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA new box kind `llm-route` combines an Ollama call and a routing decision in\none box. It takes text input (typically from a previous LLM call), a prompt\ninstruction describing the routing criteria, and produces N named output ports\n— one per possible route. The LLM is asked to reply with exactly one of the\nport names; that port's wire fires and passes the original text through.\n\nInspector UI mirrors the branch box: manually-configurable inputs (with literal\nvalue fields), and a user-addable output port list (just names — no predicates).\n\nDefault inputs on a fresh llm-route box: `text`, `prompt`, `model`, `host`.\nThe text value flows through whichever port is selected by the LLM. An `else`\nport can be added to catch unmatched replies.\n\nConnections from this box use `from_port` (same as branch) so wires render\nwith per-port palette colors.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `006-wires.js` — add `llm-route` to the `from_port` branch in\n   `create_connection`, and to the colored-wire logic in `draw_all`.\n2. `004-inspector.js` — add `'llm-route'` to kind dropdown; add\n   `mk_simple_port_list()` (addable port rows, name only); add show() section.\n3. `004-executor.lua` — add `llm_route_call()` helper (require ollama, compose\n   routing prompt, match reply to port name); handle in execute loop and\n   fire_connections.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/006-wires.js — create_connection, draw_all\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — show, mk_branch_port_list\n- src/004-executor.lua — execute, fire_connections\n- libs/ollama.lua — M.query used for routing call\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/210-llm-route-box.md"
        }
      }],

    "content":"# 210 — LLM route box\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nRouting between box paths is done by the `branch` box kind using hard-coded\npredicates (eq, contains, matches). There is no way to use an LLM judgment\nto decide which path to take.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA new box kind `llm-route` combines an Ollama call and a routing decision in\none box. It takes text input (typically from a previous LLM call), a prompt\ninstruction describing the routing criteria, and produces N named output ports\n— one per possible route. The LLM is asked to reply with exactly one of the\nport names; that port's wire fires and passes the original text through.\n\nInspector UI mirrors the branch box: manually-configurable inputs (with literal\nvalue fields), and a user-addable output port list (just names — no predicates).\n\nDefault inputs on a fresh llm-route box: `text`, `prompt`, `model`, `host`.\nThe text value flows through whichever port is selected by the LLM. An `else`\nport can be added to catch unmatched replies.\n\nConnections from this box use `from_port` (same as branch) so wires render\nwith per-port palette colors.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `006-wires.js` — add `llm-route` to the `from_port` branch in\n   `create_connection`, and to the colored-wire logic in `draw_all`.\n2. `004-inspector.js` — add `'llm-route'` to kind dropdown; add\n   `mk_simple_port_list()` (addable port rows, name only); add show() section.\n3. `004-executor.lua` — add `llm_route_call()` helper (require ollama, compose\n   routing prompt, match reply to port name); handle in execute loop and\n   fire_connections.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/006-wires.js — create_connection, draw_all\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — show, mk_branch_port_list\n- src/004-executor.lua — execute, fire_connections\n- libs/ollama.lua — M.query used for routing call\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/210-llm-route-box.md",
    "structuredPatch":[]
  }
}

          "content":"# 211 — File browser library directories\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe file browser only shows files in the map's own `src/` directory. Shared\nlibraries in `libs/` or other directories cannot be browsed or selected as a\nbox ref without manually typing the path.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA button at the top of the file browser (\"+ library dir\") prompts the user\nfor an absolute directory path and stores it in `meta.json.extra_src_dirs`.\nThese directories appear as collapsible groups in the browser alongside `src/`.\nA `▶/▼` toggle collapses or expands each group. Files in extra dirs are fetched\nand parsed identically to src/ files.\n\nServer adds two routes:\n- `GET /maps/:name/extrasrc` — returns extra dirs and their file listings\n- `GET /maps/:name/extrasrc/:index/:file` — returns a file from extra dir at\n  that index as text/plain\n\nExtra dirs are stored as absolute paths in `meta.json.extra_src_dirs`. The\nserver reads them at request time; no restart needed when dirs are added.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `src/005-http-server.lua` — add `handle_list_extrasrc` and\n   `handle_get_extrasrc`; add both to the dispatch table.\n2. `assets/js/003-api.js` — add `list_extra_src()` and `get_extra_src_file(i, f)`.\n3. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — refactor `render()` to load both src/ and\n   extra dirs; render as collapsible groups with toggle state in a local Set;\n   add \"+ library dir\" button that calls `API.put_meta`.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- src/005-http-server.lua — handle_list_src, dispatch table\n- assets/js/003-api.js — get_meta, put_meta\n- assets/js/007-filebrowser.js — render, render_fn_list\n- maps/*/meta.json — extra_src_dirs field\n",

    "content":"# 211 — File browser library directories\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe file browser only shows files in the map's own `src/` directory. Shared\nlibraries in `libs/` or other directories cannot be browsed or selected as a\nbox ref without manually typing the path.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA button at the top of the file browser (\"+ library dir\") prompts the user\nfor an absolute directory path and stores it in `meta.json.extra_src_dirs`.\nThese directories appear as collapsible groups in the browser alongside `src/`.\nA `▶/▼` toggle collapses or expands each group. Files in extra dirs are fetched\nand parsed identically to src/ files.\n\nServer adds two routes:\n- `GET /maps/:name/extrasrc` — returns extra dirs and their file listings\n- `GET /maps/:name/extrasrc/:index/:file` — returns a file from extra dir at\n  that index as text/plain\n\nExtra dirs are stored as absolute paths in `meta.json.extra_src_dirs`. The\nserver reads them at request time; no restart needed when dirs are added.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `src/005-http-server.lua` — add `handle_list_extrasrc` and\n   `handle_get_extrasrc`; add both to the dispatch table.\n2. `assets/js/003-api.js` — add `list_extra_src()` and `get_extra_src_file(i, f)`.\n3. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — refactor `render()` to load both src/ and\n   extra dirs; render as collapsible groups with toggle state in a local Set;\n   add \"+ library dir\" button that calls `API.put_meta`.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- src/005-http-server.lua — handle_list_src, dispatch table\n- assets/js/003-api.js — get_meta, put_meta\n- assets/js/007-filebrowser.js — render, render_fn_list\n- maps/*/meta.json — extra_src_dirs field\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/211-file-browser-library-dirs.md",
    "structuredPatch":[]
  }
}

1, label = label, path = dir_path, files = files }\n    end\n    json_ok(client, result)\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ handle_get_extrasrc\n-- Returns the raw text of a file from extra_src_dirs[index].\nlocal function handle_get_extrasrc(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local dir_index = tonumber(req.parts[4])\n    local file_name = req.parts[5]\n    if not dir_index or not file_name then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"missing dir index or filename\")\n    end\n    -- reject traversal attempts in the filename\n    if file_name:find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) or file_name:find(\"/\", 1, true) then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid filename\")\n    end\n\n    local meta_path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"meta.json\")\n    if not meta_path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n\n    local raw, _ = read_file(meta_path)\n    if not raw then return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", \"meta.json not found\") end\n    local meta, _, _ = json.decode(raw)\n    if not meta then return json_err(client, \"500 Internal Server Error\", \"bad meta.json\") end\n\n    local extra_dirs = meta.extra_src_dirs or {}\n    local dir_path   = extra_dirs[dir_index + 1]  -- lua 1-indexed\n    if not dir_path then return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", \"no extra dir at index \" .. dir_index) end\n\n    local file_path = dir_path .. \"/\" .. file_name\n    local content, ferr = read_file(file_path)\n    if not content then return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", tostring(ferr)) end\n    respond(client, \"200 OK\", content, \"text/plain\")\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ handle_get_src\nlocal function handle_get_src(client, req, maps_root)",

    "newString":"  // {{{ get_src_file\n  // Returns raw text, not JSON — the request() helper would mis-parse source code.\n  async function get_src_file(filename) {\n    const res = await fetch(base_url + `/maps/${map_name}/src/${encodeURIComponent(filename)}`);\n    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);\n    return res.text();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_extra_src\n  async function list_extra_src() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/extrasrc`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_extra_src_file\n  async function get_extra_src_file(dir_index, filename) {\n    const res = await fetch(base_url + `/maps/${map_name}/extrasrc/${dir_index}/${encodeURIComponent(filename)}`);\n    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);\n    return res.text();\n  }\n  // }}}",
    "originalFile":"// Thin fetch wrapper for the soramech-server REST API.\n// All functions are async and throw on non-2xx responses.\n\nconst API = (() => {\n  let base_url = '';\n  let map_name = '';\n\n  // {{{ init\n  function init(url, name) { base_url = url.replace(/\\/$/, ''); map_name = name; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ request\n  async function request(method, path, body) {\n    const opts = { method, headers: {} };\n    if (body !== undefined) {\n      opts.headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json';\n      opts.body = JSON.stringify(body);\n    }\n    const res = await fetch(base_url + path, opts);\n    const text = await res.text();\n    let data;\n    try { data = JSON.parse(text); } catch { data = { error: text }; }\n    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(data.error || `HTTP ${res.status}`);\n    return data;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_maps\n  async function list_maps() { return request('GET', '/maps'); }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_boxes\n  async function list_boxes() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_box\n  async function get_box(id) {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ put_box\n  async function put_box(id, data) {\n    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`, data);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ delete_box\n  async function delete_box(id) {\n    return request('DELETE', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_meta\n  async function get_meta() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/meta`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ put_meta\n  async function put_meta(data) {\n    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/meta`, data);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_src_files\n  async function list_src_files() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/src`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_src_file\n  // Returns raw text, not JSON — the request() helper would mis-parse source code.\n  async function get_src_file(filename) {\n    const res = await fetch(base_url + `/maps/${map_name}/src/${encodeURIComponent(filename)}`);\n    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);\n    return res.text();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_data\n  async function get_data(filename) {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/data/${filename}`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ put_data\n  async function put_data(filename, data) {\n    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/data/${filename}`, data);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { init, list_maps, list_boxes, get_box, put_box, delete_box,\n           get_meta, put_meta, get_data, put_data,\n           list_src_files, get_src_file };\n})();\n",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/js/003-api.js",
    "replaceAll":false,

    "originalFile":"// Thin fetch wrapper for the soramech-server REST API.\n// All functions are async and throw on non-2xx responses.\n\nconst API = (() => {\n  let base_url = '';\n  let map_name = '';\n\n  // {{{ init\n  function init(url, name) { base_url = url.replace(/\\/$/, ''); map_name = name; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ request\n  async function request(method, path, body) {\n    const opts = { method, headers: {} };\n    if (body !== undefined) {\n      opts.headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json';\n      opts.body = JSON.stringify(body);\n    }\n    const res = await fetch(base_url + path, opts);\n    const text = await res.text();\n    let data;\n    try { data = JSON.parse(text); } catch { data = { error: text }; }\n    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(data.error || `HTTP ${res.status}`);\n    return data;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_maps\n  async function list_maps() { return request('GET', '/maps'); }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_boxes\n  async function list_boxes() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_box\n  async function get_box(id) {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ put_box\n  async function put_box(id, data) {\n    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`, data);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ delete_box\n  async function delete_box(id) {\n    return request('DELETE', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_meta\n  async function get_meta() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/meta`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ put_meta\n  async function put_meta(data) {\n    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/meta`, data);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_src_files\n  async function list_src_files() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/src`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_src_file\n  // Returns raw text, not JSON — the request() helper would mis-parse source code.\n  async function get_src_file(filename) {\n    const res = await fetch(base_url + `/maps/${map_name}/src/${encodeURIComponent(filename)}`);\n    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);\n    return res.text();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_extra_src\n  async function list_extra_src() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/extrasrc`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_extra_src_file\n  async function get_extra_src_file(dir_index, filename) {\n    const res = await fetch(base_url + `/maps/${map_name}/extrasrc/${dir_index}/${encodeURIComponent(filename)}`);\n    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);\n    return res.text();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_data\n  async function get_data(filename) {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/data/${filename}`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ put_data\n  async function put_data(filename, data) {\n    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/data/${filename}`, data);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { init, list_maps, list_boxes, get_box, put_box, delete_box,\n           get_meta, put_meta, get_data, put_data,\n           list_src_files, get_src_file };\n})();\n",

const tok = /\\b(function|if|while|for|repeat|do|end|until)\\b/g;\n    tok.lastIndex = body_start;\n    let depth = 1;\n    let m;\n    while ((m = tok.exec(content)) !== null) {\n      const kw = m[1];\n      if (kw === 'end' || kw === 'until') {\n        depth--;\n        if (depth === 0) return m.index;\n      } else {\n        depth++;\n      }\n    }\n    return content.length;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ parse_lua_returns\n  // Scans a function body for return statements; returns an array of output names.\n  function parse_lua_returns(body) {\n    const re    = ## [1527]

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T01:24:27.110Z",
  "slug":"reactive-toasting-squid",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"The `ollama.lua` call box and the `llm-route` box solve different problems, and the executor treats them very differently.\n\n**`call` box using `ollama.lua`:**\n\nThe executor doesn't know or care that it's talking to Ollama. It just sees a box with `kind: \"call\"`, looks up the driver (`drivers/lua.sh`), spawns a subprocess, passes the inputs as JSON arguments, and collects the return values as named output ports. The Lua function does the HTTP call internally. The executor's job is done after the function returns — it pushes the output values into the store and enqueues whatever downstream boxes are now satisfied.\n\n**`llm-route` box:**\n\nThe executor handles it directly in `fire_connections` without spawning any subprocess. There's no driver involved. Instead, when the box runs, `llm_route_call()` in the executor itself calls `require(\"ollama\")` and makes the Ollama request inline in Lua. The result isn't an output value pushed to downstream ports — it's a **routing decision**. The executor looks at which output port name matches the LLM's reply, then fires only that port's wire, passing the original `text` input through as the value. The other ports stay silent.\n\nSo the key difference is **data flow vs. control flow**:\n\n- `call` box: produces output values, all wired outputs fire, downstream boxes receive data\n- `llm-route` box: produces no data of its own, exactly one output wire fires, that wire carries the input text through — the box is a switch, not a transformer\n\nIt's the same distinction as between a `call` box and a `branch` box. In fact `llm-route` is implemented almost identically to `branch` in the executor — the only difference is that `branch` evaluates a hard-coded predicate (eq, contains, etc.) while `llm-route` asks Ollama to make the judgment call."
      }],

## [1534]

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T01:26:30.283Z",
  "slug":"reactive-toasting-squid",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"It's hard-coded into all three system layers — which is the same situation as `branch`.\n\n**In the executor** (`004-executor.lua`): `llm_route_call()` lives there, and there are two explicit `elseif box.kind == \"llm-route\"` checks — one in the main execution loop, one in `fire_connections`. Touch the executor to add or change it.\n\n**In the inspector** (`004-inspector.js`): the kind dropdown lists it by name, and `show()` has a dedicated block that renders its specific UI. Touch the inspector to change what appears in the panel.\n\n**In the wires** (`006-wires.js`): two more explicit checks — one to use `from_port` instead of `from_output` when drawing a wire from it, one for the colored-wire logic.\n\nSo it's spread across three files and none of it is swappable. Compare that to `ollama.lua`, which is entirely standalone — delete the file and nothing in the system breaks.\n\nThe root issue is that **control flow can't live in a user function**. A `call` box always fires all its output wires after the function returns — the executor doesn't give the function any way to say \"only fire this one port.\" So any box that needs to choose between output paths has to be a special kind that the executor knows about, which means it ends up baked in.\n\nOne way to fix this: give functions a way to return a *route signal* — a special return value that the executor interprets as \"fire this named port with this value.\" Then `llm-route` could just be a Lua function in `libs/` that returns `{ _route = \"positive\", _value = text }`, and the executor would handle it generically for any call box that returns that shape. No new kind, no changes to the inspector or wires.\n\nWorth considering before adding more special kinds."
      }],

    "role":"user",
    "content":"Alright so we need to find a way to decouple it. Let's brainstorm a bit. You say there's no way to have control flow in the user function, but that's definitely not true - here's a quick example in pseudocode:\n\nfunction do_thing(a, b, c)\n  if a < b then return c\n  if a == b then return b or a\n  else return false\n\nin this example, the function is doing control flow. Easy. When the box is executed, only the C, B, or A outputs will trigger. Here's another example to be more explicit:\n\nfunction do_other_thing(d, e, f)\n  if d == 2 then return (e, f)\n  else return d\n\nin this case, there will either be two wires passed to output ports, or one wire. We have to be able to distinguish between them somehow. I'm not sure how to make that work. Any ideas?"
  },

## [1541]

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T01:33:27.037Z",
  "slug":"reactive-toasting-squid",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"The second example is the revealing one. Let me think through it:\n\n```\nfunction do_other_thing(d, e, f)\n  if d == 2 then return (e, f)\n  else return d\n```\n\nThe system has to know: when two values come back, do they go to ports 1 and 2 positionally? Or to specific named ports? And when one value comes back, which port does it go to — the first one, or the one named `d`?\n\nThe current executor maps returns strictly by position: first return value → first output port, second → second, and so on. So there's actually a partial solution already baked in — if a function returns `nil` for a position, the executor skips writing that key to the store, which means the downstream box never becomes satisfied and its wire effectively doesn't fire. But to use it you'd have to write `return nil, e, f` or `return d, nil, nil` and know the port order by heart, which is fragile.\n\nThe cleaner fix is a thin routing wrapper in the standard library:\n\n```lua\nlocal sora = require(\"soramech\")\n\nfunction do_other_thing(d, e, f)\n  if d == 2 then return sora.routes({ e_out = e, f_out = f })\n  else return sora.route(\"d_out\", d)\nend\n```\n\n`sora.route` and `sora.routes` just return a specially-marked table — `{ __soramech_route = true, port = \"d_out\", value = d }`. The driver detects that marker and outputs a different JSON shape. The executor detects it in `fire_connections` and fires only the named ports instead of doing positional mapping.\n\nThe payoff: `llm-route` becomes a regular Lua function in `libs/` that calls Ollama and returns `sora.route(matched_port, text)`. The special kind disappears from the executor, inspector, and wires entirely — replaced by a library call any function can use.\n\nWant me to implement that?"
      }],

## [1548]

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T01:35:53.093Z",
  "slug":"reactive-toasting-squid",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"It solves the naming problem but not the routing problem — let me separate them.\n\n**Naming:** Yes, inheriting names from the function is strictly better than allowing renames. The port named `c` in the inspector is the variable `c` in the source — no mismatch possible. That's a good change and we should make it.\n\n**Routing:** The executor still gets positional return values. When the function does `return c`, the runtime value of `c` arrives at position 1 — the executor doesn't know it was called `c`. So `return c` fires the first output port, not the port *named* `c`.\n\nThe nil convention handles this, but requires the user to be explicit:\n\n```lua\nfunction do_thing(a, b, c)\n  -- output ports in order: a, b, c\n  if a < b    then return nil, nil, c    -- c fires\n  if a == b   then return nil, b,   nil  -- b fires\n  else             return false, nil, nil -- a fires\nend\n```\n\nSince the port names are inherited and shown in order in the inspector, the user knows `c` is position 3. Returning `nil` at a position means that port's wire doesn't fire. That's already close to working in the executor — `nil` in the store means `inputs_satisfied` returns false downstream.\n\nSo the full picture is:\n\n- Remove renaming from the inspector → ports are always what the function says they are\n- Commit to a defined port order (order they appear in returns, as the parser already extracts them)\n- `nil` at a position = that port doesn't fire\n- The `sora.route` library is still useful for *named* routing without caring about position, but it's optional\n\nWant me to start with removing renaming from the inspector, since that's the concrete UI change, and separately tackle the nil-firing in the executor?"
      }],

{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "promptId":"99e1b34c-4ab2-4385-9605-4e3b398905ec",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T01:40:05.303Z",
  "permissionMode":"acceptEdits",
  "slug":"reactive-toasting-squid",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "message":{
    "role":"user",
    "content":"I don't want to do positional ports because, well, they're very fragile. Easy to make mistakes. Is there a reason we can't just, read through the src file, find all the return statements, and use the names that are present there? If the value is a constant, just have the name and the field be constant and unchangable by the user editing the box properties. If the return value is like, a function or something, then just put the entire function call there verbatim. It'll probably be ugly but I don't see how to do it without being informative. This will cause some issues for example in this system:\n\nfunction blahblahblah(a, b, c)\n  if a == 2 then b = 2\n  return (a, b, c)\nend\n\nin this case, if a is 1, b is 1, and c is 1, then the output will be (1, 2, 1)\nbut if a is 2, then the output will be (2, 2, 1) and the user will have no way to predict that. Thoughts?"
  },
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "uuid":"89bb8ebc-66f4-4368-bcd9-2bdca9aba14c",

}

## [1555]

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T01:41:10.735Z",
  "slug":"reactive-toasting-squid",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"The mutation case isn't really a system problem — it's a code readability problem. The port is correctly named `b`; the user just has to read their own function to know `b` might be 2. That's true of any programming tool. The system can't and shouldn't try to track value provenance through mutations.\n\nThe parsing approach is sound. But it still doesn't tell the executor which return value maps to which port at runtime. `return a, b, c` gives the driver three anonymous positional values — the names are lost.\n\nThe way to fix both problems at once: **require functions to return a table with named keys.**\n\n```lua\nfunction blahblahblah(a, b, c)\n  if a == 2 then b = 2 end\n  return { a = a, b = b, c = c }\nend\n\nfunction classify(text)\n  if score > 0.5 then return { positive = text }\n  else                return { negative = text }\n  end\nend\n```\n\nThe parser reads table keys from return statements — that's already closer to what it does. The driver detects that the return value is a table (not an array) and uses it as a named map. The executor fires only the ports whose keys appear in the returned table. No positional mapping, no library wrapper, no fragility.\n\nThe mutation case looks like `{ b = b }` — the key is the port name, the value is whatever b is at that moment. That's honest and accurate.\n\nConstants come out naturally too: `return { version = \"1.0\" }` — the inspector sees `\"1.0\"` and marks the port as constant. Complex expressions: `return { result = foo(x) }` — shows `foo(x)` verbatim, which is ugly but accurate.\n\nThe one cost: functions need to always return a table. That's a convention the user has to follow, but it's a small one and it buys complete decoupling from positional ordering.\n\nWorth adopting?"
      }],

    "content":"  The parsing approach is sound. But it still doesn't tell the executor which return\n   value maps to which port at runtime. return a, b, c gives the driver three\n  anonymous positional values — the names are lost.\n\n\nwell... why couldn't it? I'm assuming something like this:\n\nfunction thing(a, b, c)\n  if a == 2 then return (a, b, c)\n  else return (c, b, a)\nend\n\nright? where the return value is not consistent. I think in that case we'd have two separate port sections, one for each return value. The first would have three wire outputs, for a, b, c and hte second port section would have three wire outputs, one for c, b, and a. Does that fix the problem?\n\n  The way to fix both problems at once: require functions to return a table with\n  named keys.\n\nI want to try and avoid forcing idioms on the user..."

## [1562]

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T01:44:59.844Z",
  "slug":"reactive-toasting-squid",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"The multi-section display idea is genuinely good for the inspector — each return statement becomes its own port group, and you can wire from whichever group you expect to fire. That's a clean UI.\n\nThe runtime problem is still there though. The driver just sees raw positional values — by the time they cross the function boundary, the names are gone. It gets back `[1, 2, 1]` and has no way to know whether that came from `return a, b, c` or `return c, b, a`. Both produce the same array.\n\nThe one case where disambiguation works automatically: when different return paths produce **different numbers of values**. If path 1 returns 3 values and path 2 returns 1, the driver can check the count and know which path fired. That covers a lot of practical cases:\n\n```lua\nfunction thing(a, b, c)\n  if a == 2 then return a, b, c   -- 3 values → path 1\n  else return c                   -- 1 value  → path 2\nend\n```\n\nBut your example — two paths both returning 3 values — is unresolvable without some form of tagging. The driver genuinely cannot tell them apart.\n\nSo the honest picture is:\n\n- Different value counts → works, no idiom needed, just count-based disambiguation\n- Same value counts, different variable order → unsolvable at runtime without tagging\n\nFor that second case, you're stuck choosing between: source instrumentation (fragile, complex), a tagging convention, or accepting that port names are approximate/informational when paths have equal lengths.\n\nMaybe the pragmatic answer is: implement count-based disambiguation, show the multi-section display in the inspector, and document that \"same-length ambiguous paths\" are a known limitation. In practice most routing functions return different amounts from different paths anyway."
      }],
    "id":"msg_01KHAu1hCrWz1rgxL1AoBiE6",

{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "promptId":"3e607e0d-9c69-451c-8695-804c367fcf15",

  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "message":{
    "role":"user",
    "content":"Okay... Maybe we can update the driver to be able to handle that? Lemme think about it...\n\nokay. here's how I think it needs to be. We have one output wire, that all return values are routed through. There should be a button near it that says \"compare\" or \">=<\" or similar that adds two wires, one above and one below. Then there should be a text-entry field that lets the user type a number. There should also be a drop-down panel on the text-entry field that lets a user select one of the input wire values instead. Then, the result will be sent to one of the three wires - the middle wire is if the value is exactly the same as the defined comparison value. The upper wire is if it's less than, the lower value is greater than. If the returning value matches one of the ports that doesn't have a wire connection, it is silently dropped.\n\nI think this'll solve the issue. What do you think?"
  },

## [1569]

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T02:04:36.861Z",
  "slug":"reactive-toasting-squid",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"That's a clean separation of concerns — computation stays in the function box, routing logic moves to a dedicated node downstream. It's how proper dataflow systems work.\n\nA few thoughts:\n\nThe \"button on the wire\" is a nice idea but it's basically just a box — a comparator box with one data input, one comparand input (literal or wired), and three outputs: `lt`, `eq`, `gt`. The \"insert on wire\" interaction is a UX shortcut to spawning it, which can be a separate thing.\n\nThe comparand-as-wire is the genuinely new feature the branch box doesn't have. Right now branch predicates are always literals. Being able to wire `value_b` as the thing you're comparing against is powerful — compare outputs from two different upstream boxes against each other.\n\nThe silent-drop behavior is already how the executor works — if a port has no downstream wire, nothing happens. You get that for free.\n\nThe thing this solves that the branch box doesn't: the branch box is first-match (fires one port, stops). The comparator fires all matching outputs simultaneously — if the value equals the comparand, `eq` fires, but `lt` and `gt` don't. All three are evaluated independently rather than in order.\n\nOne edge case worth deciding: what's the comparand type? If it's always numeric, lt/eq/gt are straightforward. If it's a string, eq makes sense but lt/gt are lexicographic which might be surprising. Might be worth a type indicator or just restricting to numbers for now.\n\nThis is a genuinely better architecture than tracking return paths. Want me to implement it as a new box kind — or as an inline wire node?"
      }],

## [1574]

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T02:07:37.547Z",
  "slug":"reactive-toasting-squid",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"Throwing on non-number is the right call — keeps the comparator's behavior unambiguous.\n\nLet me make sure I understand the full implication of \"the only way we handle return values, on all boxes\":\n\nRight now, boxes have **named output ports** — you browse a file, pick a function, and the port names come from the return variable names. Those named ports wire to named input ports on downstream boxes. The `branch` and `llm-route` box kinds exist specifically because named ports can't do routing.\n\nWhat you're describing replaces all of that with **positional output slots** — one slot per return value, no names, just position 1, 2, 3. Each slot starts as a single wire. You can optionally attach a comparator to any slot, which splits it into three wires (lt, eq, gt) with a typed comparand. If a branch has no wire, that result is silently dropped. The `branch` and `llm-route` kinds go away entirely — any box can route by attaching a comparator to its output.\n\nThat's a significant schema change. The connection record currently uses `from_output` (a port name). It would need to become `from_slot` (an index) and `from_branch` (null, `\"lt\"`, `\"eq\"`, or `\"gt\"`). The `outputs` array on the box becomes just display labels from the parser — not part of the connection model.\n\nFor LLM routing: instead of `llm-route`, you'd have an ollama box that returns a number (1, 2, 3), then compare that number. The classify logic lives in the Lua function, the routing lives in the comparator.\n\nThat's the right architecture. Is my understanding correct, or am I missing something? And how do you want to handle the wired-comparand case for now — skip it and just support typed constants?"
      }],

        "text":"Got it — I overcomplicated it. Every box has one output wire. That wire carries whatever the function returned. Click compare on that wire and it becomes three wires (lt, middle, gt) with a typed comparand. Only one of the three fires.\n\nTwo things I want to make sure I understand:\n\n**Multiple return values** — if a function returns `a, b, c`, what goes on the one wire? The first value? A wrapped array? Or is the expectation that functions in this system return one thing, and if you need to pass multiple values you structure them into a table?\n\n**Input side** — inputs are still named (the function's parameter names), and you wire values into them from upstream boxes' output wires. That part doesn't change. Only the output side gets simplified to one wire + optional comparator.\n\nIf I have those two right, the model is:\n\n- Box input: named ports, wired from upstream\n- Box runs the function\n- Box output: one wire carrying the result\n- Optional comparator on that wire → three wires, one fires based on numeric comparison\n\nAnd the old `branch`, `llm-route`, and named output ports all disappear. Any box can route just by having a comparator on its wire."
      }],

  "version":"2.1.121",
  "message":{
    "role":"user",
    "content":"  Multiple return values — if a function returns a, b, c, what goes on the one wire?\n   The first value? A wrapped array? Or is the expectation that functions in this\n  system return one thing, and if you need to pass multiple values you structure\n  them into a table?\n\n\nthe whole thing. Just, whatever the return statement outputs, that's what goes down the wire. If the user clicks compare and it returns a tuple or something besides a strict valid number, then it errors.\n\n  Input side — inputs are still named (the function's parameter names), and you wire\n   values into them from upstream boxes' output wires. That part doesn't change.\n  Only the output side gets simplified to one wire + optional comparator.\n\n\nyes this part does change. We're removing the renaming functionality and replacing it with parsing the argument names from the source file."
  },
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",

## [1588]

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T02:11:30.087Z",
  "slug":"reactive-toasting-squid",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"Okay, now I have the complete picture:\n\n**Output:** one wire per box, carries the raw return value — scalar, tuple, table, whatever the function actually returned. Comparator is optional; if attached and the value isn't a strict number, error.\n\n**Input:** named ports parsed from the function's argument list, read-only. The literal value field we just built still makes sense here — supply a constant without wiring.\n\n**Connection model simplifies to:** `{from_box, from_branch (null/\"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\"), to_box, to_input}`. No `from_output` or `from_port` — there's only ever one output per box.\n\n**What disappears:** `outputs` array on the box, named output ports entirely, `branch` box kind, `llm-route` box kind, port renaming in the inspector.\n\nThis is a significant refactor across basically every layer — schema, executor, canvas rendering, inspector, wires, file browser. The old `branch` behavior comes for free on any box that returns a number and has a comparator attached.\n\nBefore I start writing code: should I create issue files for the refactor pieces and plan the order of changes, or do you want to start somewhere specific? The connection schema change is probably the load-bearing piece — everything else follows from it."
      }],

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "promptId":"39f9a489-82ac-4453-94ae-8f9f21bd301e",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T02:13:16.504Z",
  "sourceToolAssistantUUID":"c776354c-4e72-40f9-aadb-9ea24944f3c4",
  "slug":"reactive-toasting-squid",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "message":{
    "role":"user",
    "content":[{
        "type":"tool_result",
        "content":"1\t# 208 — Port literal values\n2\t\n3\t## Status\n4\t\n5\topen\n6\t\n7\t## Current behavior\n8\t\n9\tInput ports on a box can only receive values from wired connections. If no wire\n10\tis connected to an input port, the box never becomes \"ready\" and the runner\n11\tskips it silently. There is no way to supply a constant value to an input from\n12\tthe editor.\n13\t\n14\t## Intended behavior\n15\t\n16\tEach input port has an optional literal value editable directly in the inspector\n17\tpanel. If the value field is non-empty and no wire is connected to that port,\n18\tthe literal value is used at runtime. If a wire IS connected, the wire's value\n19\toverwrites the literal at runtime — wires always win.\n20\t\n21\tThe value field accepts JSON notation (numbers, strings with quotes, arrays,\n22\tobjects) or bare strings for convenience. The executor tries JSON.decode first;\n23\tif that fails, the raw string is used.\n24\t\n25\tThis lets a box be fully configured from the inspector without needing a\n26\tdedicated \"data\" box wired to it for every constant.\n27\t\n28\t## Suggested implementation steps\n29\t\n30\t1. **Data model** — port objects in `box.inputs` gain an optional `value`\n31\t   string field. No schema change needed (extra fields are already tolerated).\n32\t\n33\t2. **Inspector (`004-inspector.js`)** — `mk_port_display()` gains a\n34\t   `show_value` boolean parameter. When true, each port row shows a second\n35\t   text input for the value alongside the name input.       "content":"# 208 — Port literal values\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nInput ports on a box can only receive values from wired connections. If no wire\nis connected to an input port, the box never becomes \"ready\" and the runner\nskips it silently. There is no way to supply a constant value to an input from\nthe editor.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nEach input port has an optional literal value editable directly in the inspector\npanel. If the value field is non-empty and no wire is connected to that port,\nthe literal value is used at runtime. If a wire IS connected, the wire's value\noverwrites the literal at runtime — wires always win.\n\nThe value field accepts JSON notation (numbers, strings with quotes, arrays,\nobjects) or bare strings for convenience. The executor tries JSON.decode first;\nif that fails, the raw string is used.\n\nThis lets a box be fully configured from the inspector without needing a\ndedicated \"data\" box wired to it for every constant.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. **Data model** — port objects in `box.inputs` gain an optional `value`\n   string field. No schema change needed (extra fields are already tolerated).\n\n2. **Inspector (`004-inspector.js`)** — `mk_port_display()` gains a\n   `show_value` boolean parameter. When true, each port row shows a second\n   text input for the value alongside the name input. On change, updates\n   `ports[i].value` and calls `save()`.\n\n3. **Executor (`004-executor.lua`)** — add a pre-seeding pass before the main\n   execution loop: for every box, for every input port that has a non-empty\n   `value`, write `store[box_id..\".\"..port.name]` with the parsed value.\n   Existing `inputs_satisfied` and `collect_inputs` logic requires no changes\n   because they only read from the store.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — mk_port_display, show\n- src/004-executor.lua — execute, inputs_satisfied\n- docs/001-architecture.md — store model, box.inputs schema\n",

        "content":"// Source file browser and function signature parser.\n// Renders into the inspector panel: file list → function list → auto-populate box ports.\n\nconst FileBrowser = (() => {\n\n  // {{{ lua_fn_end\n  // Returns the index of the closing 'end'/'until' that matches the function body\n  // starting at body_start. Tracks nesting depth by counting block openers and closers.\n  // Does not attempt to skip string literals — good enough for well-formatted source.\n  function lua_fn_end(content, body_start) {\n    const tok = /\\b(function|if|while|for|repeat|do|end|until)\\b/g;\n    tok.lastIndex = body_start;\n    let depth = 1;\n    let m;\n    while ((m = tok.exec(content)) !== null) {\n      const kw = m[1];\n      if (kw === 'end' || kw === 'until') {\n        depth--;\n        if (depth === 0) return m.index;\n      } else {\n        depth++;\n      }\n    }\n    return content.length;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ parse_lua_returns\n  // Scans a function body for return statements; returns an array of output names.\n  function parse_lua_returns(body) {\n    const re    = /\\breturn\\b\\s*([^\\n]+)/g;\n    const names = new Set();\n    let m;\n    while ((m = re.exec(body)) !== null) {\n      const expr = m[1].replace(/--.*$/, '').trim();\n      if (!expr) continue;\n      // string literals or concat operator mean the whole expression is complex\n      if (/[\"']|\\.\\./.test(expr)) { names.add('result'); continue; }\n      const parts = expr.split(',');\n      parts.forEach(part => {\n        part = part.trim();\n        // bare identifier → use as port name\n        if (/^[a-zA-Z_]\\w*$/.test(part) &&\n            !['nil','true','false','not','and','or','end'].includes(part)) {\n          names.add(part);\n        } else if (parts.length === 1 && part) {\n          // single complex expression → call it \"result\"\n          names.add('result');\n        }\n        // multi-value complex expression with no bare names: skip\n      });\n    }\n    return [...names];\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ parse_lua\n  function parse_lua(content) {\n    const fns    = [];\n    const fn_re  = /^function\\s+M\\.(\\w+)\\s*\\(([^)]*)\\)/mg;\n    let m;\n    while ((m = fn_re.exec(content)) !== null) {\n      const body_start = m.index + m[0].length;\n      const body_end   = lua_fn_end(content, body_start);\n      const body       = content.slice(body_start, body_end);\n      const inputs     = m[2].trim()\n        ? m[2].split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)\n        : [];\n      const outputs    = parse_lua_returns(body);\n      fns.push({ name: m[1], inputs, outputs });\n    }\n    return fns;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ parse_bash_inputs\n  function parse_bash_inputs(body) {\n    const params = {};\n    // local var=\"${N}\" or local var=\"$N\"\n    const local_re = /local\\s+(\\w+)\\s*=\\s*[\"']?\\$\\{?(\\d+)\\}?[\"']?/g;\n    let m;\n    while ((m = local_re.exec(body)) !== null) {\n      params[parseInt(m[2])] = m[1];\n    }\n    if (Object.keys(params).length > 0) {\n      const max = Math.max(...Object.keys(params).map(Number));\n      return Array.from({ length: max }, (_, i) => params[i + 1] || `arg${i + 1}`);\n    }\n    // fall back: scan for raw $N references\n    const seen = new Set();\n    const pos_re = /\\$\\{?(\\d+)\\}?/g;\n    while ((m = pos_re.exec(body)) !== null) {\n      const n = parseInt(m[1]);\n      if (n > 0) seen.add(n);\n    }\n    if (seen.size > 0) {\n      const max = Math.max(...seen);\n      return Array.from({ length: max }, (_, i) => `arg${i + 1}`);\n    }\n    return [];\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ parse_bash\n  function parse_bash(content) {\n    const fns   = [];\n    const re    = /^(\\w+)\\s*\\(\\s*\\)\\s*\\{/mg;\n    const skip  = new Set(['if','while','for','case','do','done','fi','then','else']);\n    let m;\n    while ((m = re.exec(content)) !== null) {\n      const name = m[1];\n      if (skip.has(name)) continue;\n      const body_start = m.index + m[0].length;\n      const close      = content.indexOf('\\n}', body_start);\n      const body       = content.slice(body_start, close > -1 ? close : body_start + 800);\n      const inputs     = parse_bash_inputs(body);\n      fns.push({ name, inputs, outputs: ['output'] });\n    }\n    return fns;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ parse_functions\n  // Returns [{name, inputs:[string], outputs:[string]}] for a given file.\n  function parse_functions(content, filename) {\n    const ext = filename.split('.').pop();\n    if (ext === 'lua') return parse_lua(content);\n    if (ext === 'sh')  return parse_bash(content);\n    return null;  // null = no parser for this extension\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ render_fn_list\n  // Shows parsed functions for one file; calls on_select(filename, fn) on click.\n  function render_fn_list(container, filename, fns, on_select, on_back) {\n    container.innerHTML = '';\n\n    const back_btn = document.createElement('button');\n    back_btn.className   = 'fb-back';\n    back_btn.textContent = '← ' + filename;\n    back_btn.onclick     = on_back;\n    container.appendChild(back_btn);\n\n    if (fns === null) {\n      const note = document.createElement('div');\n      note.className   = 'fb-note';\n      note.textContent = 'no parser for .' + filename.split('.').pop() + ' files';\n      container.appendChild(note);\n      return;\n    }\n\n    if (fns.length === 0) {\n      const note = document.createElement('div');\n      note.className   = 'fb-note';\n      note.textContent = 'no public functions found (expected: function M.name(...))';\n      container.appendChild(note);\n      return;\n    }\n\n    fns.forEach(fn => {\n      const row = document.createElement('div');\n      row.className = 'fb-fn-row';\n\n      const name_el = document.createElement('div');\n      name_el.className   = 'fb-fn-name';\n      name_el.textContent = fn.name + '(' + fn.inputs.join(', ') + ')';\n      row.appendChild(name_el);\n\n      const in_el = document.createElement('div');\n      in_el.className   = 'fb-fn-ports';\n      in_el.textContent = 'in:  ' + (fn.inputs.length ? fn.inputs.join(', ') : '(none)');\n      row.appendChild(in_el);\n\n      const out_el = document.createElement('div');\n      out_el.className   = 'fb-fn-ports';\n      out_el.textContent = 'out: ' + (fn.outputs.length ? fn.outputs.join(', ') : '(none)');\n      row.appendChild(out_el);\n\n      row.onclick = () => on_select(filename, fn);\n      container.appendChild(row);\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ render\n  // Renders the full file browser into container.\n  // on_select(filename, fn_obj) called when the user picks a function.\n  // Groups: [{label, files:[string], fetch_file: async fn(filename)->text}]\n  async function render(container, on_select) {\n    container.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note\">loading…</div>';\n\n    // collapsed state: set of group labels\n    const collapsed = new Set();\n\n    // load src/ and extra dirs in parallel\n    let src_files = [], extra_dirs = [];\n    try {\n      [src_files, extra_dirs] = await Promise.all([\n        API.list_src_files().catch(() => []),\n        API.list_extra_src().catch(() => []),\n      ]);\n    } catch (e) {\n      container.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note error\">load error: ' + e.message + '</div>';\n      return;\n    }\n\n    // build unified group list\n    const groups = [];\n    if (src_files.length > 0) {\n      groups.push({\n        label: 'src/',\n        files: src_files,\n        fetch_file: f => API.get_src_file(f),\n      });\n    }\n    (extra_dirs || []).forEach(d => {\n      if (d.files && d.files.length > 0) {\n        groups.push({\n          label: d.label + '/',\n          files: d.files,\n          fetch_file: f => API.get_extra_src_file(d.index, f),\n        });\n      }\n    });\n\n    const show_file_list = () => {\n      container.innerHTML = '';\n\n      // add-library-dir button\n      const add_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      add_btn.textContent = '+ library dir';\n      add_btn.className   = 'fb-add-dir-btn';\n      add_btn.onclick     = async () => {\n        const path = prompt('Absolute path to directory:');\n        if (!path || !path.trim()) return;\n        try {\n          const meta = await API.get_meta();\n          const dirs = meta.extra_src_dirs || [];\n          if (!dirs.includes(path.trim())) {\n            dirs.push(path.trim());\n            await API.put_meta({ ...meta, extra_src_dirs: dirs });\n          }\n          render(container, on_select);\n        } catch (e) {\n          const note = document.createElement('div');\n          note.className = 'fb-note error';\n          note.textContent = 'could not save dir: ' + e.message;\n          container.insertBefore(note, container.firstChild);\n        }\n      };\n      container.appendChild(add_btn);\n\n      if (groups.length === 0) {\n        const note = document.createElement('div');\n        note.className   = 'fb-note';\n        note.textContent = 'src/ is empty — add source files or a library dir';\n        container.appendChild(note);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      groups.forEach(group => {\n        const is_collapsed = collapsed.has(group.label);\n\n        // group header row with toggle\n        const hdr = document.createElement('div');\n        hdr.className = 'fb-group-hdr';\n\n        const toggle = document.createElement('span');\n        toggle.className   = 'fb-group-toggle';\n        toggle.textContent = is_collapsed ? '▶' : '▼';\n        hdr.appendChild(toggle);\n\n        const lbl = document.createElement('span');\n        lbl.className   = 'fb-header';\n        lbl.textContent = group.label;\n        hdr.appendChild(lbl);\n\n        hdr.onclick = () => {\n          if (collapsed.has(group.label)) collapsed.delete(group.label);\n          else collapsed.add(group.label);\n          show_file_list();\n        };\n        container.appendChild(hdr);\n\n        if (is_collapsed) return;\n\n        group.files.forEach(filename => {\n          const row = document.createElement('div');\n          row.className   = 'fb-file-row';\n          row.textContent = filename;\n          row.onclick     = async () => {\n            row.textContent = filename + ' …';\n            let content;\n            try {\n              content = await group.fetch_file(filename);\n            } catch (e) {\n              container.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note error\">could not read ' + filename + ': ' + e.message + '</div>';\n              show_file_list();\n              return;\n            }\n            const fns = parse_functions(content, filename);\n            render_fn_list(container, group.label + filename, fns,\n              (f, fn) => on_select(f, fn),\n              show_file_list\n            );\n          };\n          container.appendChild(row);\n        });\n      });\n    };\n\n    show_file_list();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { parse_functions, render };\n})();\n",
        "startLine":1,
        "totalLines":318,
