        "content":"// Thin fetch wrapper for the soramech-server REST API.\n// All functions are async and throw on non-2xx responses.\n\nconst API = (() => {\n  let base_url = '';\n  let map_name = '';\n\n  // {{{ init\n  function init(url, name) { base_url = url.replace(/\\/$/, ''); map_name = name; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ request\n  async function request(method, path, body) {\n    const opts = { method, headers: {} };\n    if (body !== undefined) {\n      opts.headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json';\n      opts.body = JSON.stringify(body);\n    }\n    const res = await fetch(base_url + path, opts);\n    const text = await res.text();\n    let data;\n    try { data = JSON.parse(text); } catch { data = { error: text }; }\n    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(data.error || `HTTP ${res.status}`);\n    return data;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_maps\n  async function list_maps() { return request('GET', '/maps'); }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_boxes\n  async function list_boxes() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_box\n  async function get_box(id) {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ put_box\n  async function put_box(id, data) {\n    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`, data);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ delete_box\n  async function delete_box(id) {\n    return request('DELETE', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_meta\n  async function get_meta() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/meta`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ put_meta\n  async function put_meta(data) {\n    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/meta`, data);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_src_files\n  async function list_src_files() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/src`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_src_file\n  // Returns raw text, not JSON — the request() helper would mis-parse source code.\n  async function get_src_file(filename) {\n    const res = await fetch(base_url + `/maps/${map_name}/src/${encodeURIComponent(filename)}`);\n    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);\n    return res.text();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_extra_src\n  async function list_extra_src() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/extrasrc`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_extra_src_file\n  async function get_extra_src_file(dir_index, filename) {\n    const res = await fetch(base_url + `/maps/${map_name}/extrasrc/${dir_index}/${encodeURIComponent(filename)}`);\n    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);\n    return res.text();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_data\n  async function get_data(filename) {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/data/${filename}`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ put_data\n  async function put_data(filename, data) {\n    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/data/${filename}`, data);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { init, list_maps, list_boxes, get_box, put_box, delete_box,\n           get_meta, put_meta, get_data, put_data,\n           list_src_files, get_src_file,\n           list_extra_src, get_extra_src_file };\n})();\n",

        "content":"-- Synchronous FSM executor for the SoraMech runner.\n-- Walks the graph from the entry box, invokes language drivers for each\n-- box in dependency order, and threads output values through wires.\n-- Each box call is isolated in run_task() — the future thread pool swap point.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal M    = {}\n\n-- {{{ eval_predicate\nlocal function eval_predicate(pred, value)\n    -- structured predicates only; no arbitrary lua eval\n    local op  = pred.op\n    local lit = pred.value\n\n    if op == \"eq\"       then return value == lit\n    elseif op == \"lt\"   then return value <  lit\n    elseif op == \"gt\"   then return value >  lit\n    elseif op == \"lte\"  then return value <= lit\n    elseif op == \"gte\"  then return value >= lit\n    elseif op == \"contains\" then\n        return type(value) == \"string\" and value:find(lit, 1, true) ~= nil\n    elseif op == \"matches\" then\n        return type(value) == \"string\" and value:match(lit) ~= nil\n    end\n    return false\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ shell_quote\nlocal function shell_quote(s)\n    -- wrap a string in single quotes, escaping any embedded single quotes\n    return \"'\" .. tostring(s):gsub(\"'\", \"'\\\\''\") .. \"'\"\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ driver_path_for\nlocal function driver_path_for(ref, drivers)\n    -- binary callers (no extension mapping needed — they are executable directly)\n    -- source callers: look up extension in driver table\n    local ext = ref:match(\"%.([^./]+)$\")\n    if not ext then return ref end  -- no extension: treat as binary\n    local driver = drivers[\".\" .. ext]\n    return driver\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ llm_route_call\n-- Calls ollama to choose which output port name best matches the input text.\n-- Returns: matched_port (string or nil), text (string), err (string or nil).\nlocal function llm_route_call(box, inputs)\n    local ok, ollama_lib = pcall(require, \"ollama\")\n    if not ok then\n        return nil, \"\", \"llm-route: could not load ollama lib: \" .. tostring(ollama_lib)\n    end\n\n    local text_key = (box.inputs and box.inputs[1]) and box.inputs[1].name or \"text\"\n    local text   = tostring(inputs[text_key] or \"\")\n    local prompt = tostring(inputs[\"prompt\"] or \"\")\n    local model  = inputs[\"model\"]\n    local host   = inputs[\"host\"]\n\n    local port_names = {}\n    for _, port in ipairs(box.outputs or {}) do\n        if port.name and port.name ~= \"\" then\n            port_names[#port_names + 1] = port.name\n        end\n    end\n\n    if #port_names == 0 then\n        return nil, text, \"llm-route box '\" .. box.id .. \"' has no output ports defined\"\n    end\n\n    local routing_prompt = \"\"\n    if prompt ~= \"\" then routing_prompt = prompt .. \"\\n\\n\" end\n    routing_prompt = routing_prompt ..\n        \"Text:\\n\" .. text .. \"\\n\\n\" ..\n        \"Reply with ONLY one of these exact words (no punctuation, no explanation): \" ..\n        table.concat(port_names, \", \")\n\n    local reply = ollama_lib.query(routing_prompt, model, host)\n    if not reply then\n        return nil, text, \"llm-route box '\" .. box.id .. \"': ollama returned nil\"\n    end\n\n    -- normalize: trim whitespace and trailing punctuation, lowercase\n    local clean = reply:gsub(\"^%s+\", \"\"):gsub(\"%s+$\", \"\"):gsub(\"[%.!,;:]+$\", \"\"):lower()\n\n    for _, pname in ipairs(port_names) do\n        if pname:lower() == clean then return pname, text, nil end\n    end\n\n    -- no exact match: return nil port (fire_connections will try \"else\")\n    io.stderr:write(\"llm-route box '\" .. box.id .. \"': unmatched reply '\" .. reply .. \"'\\n\")\n    return nil, text, nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ run_task\n-- The task boundary. In v1: synchronous. Future: hand this signature to\n-- the thread pool. Returns outputs table and ok/err.\nlocal function run_task(box, inputs, drivers, map_dir)\n    local ref = box.ref\n    local fn  = box.fn\n\n    -- locate the driver for this ref\n    local driver = driver_path_for(ref, drivers)\n    if not driver then\n        return nil, \"no driver found for ref '\" .. ref .. \"'\"\n    end\n\n    -- resolve ref relative to map_dir\n    local abs_ref = map_dir .. \"/\" .. ref\n\n    -- build argument list: file fn arg_count [args...]\n    local args = {}\n    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n        local val = inputs[port.name]\n        if val == nil then\n            -- nil input becomes JSON null\n            args[#args + 1] = shell_quote(json.encode(nil))\n        else\n            args[#args + 1] = shell_quote(json.encode(val))\n        end\n    end\n\n    local cmd\n    if fn then\n        -- source caller: driver file fn arg_count [args...]\n        cmd = driver .. \" \" .. shell_quote(abs_ref) .. \" \" ..\n              shell_quote(fn) .. \" \" .. #args\n        for _, a in ipairs(args) do cmd = cmd .. \" \" .. a end\n    else\n        -- binary caller: run ref directly with args\n        cmd = abs_ref .. \" \" .. #args\n        for _, a in ipairs(args) do cmd = cmd .. \" \" .. a end\n    end\n\n    -- invoke driver; capture stdout; errors go to stderr (visible in terminal)\n    -- io.popen doesn't support stderr separation; redirect stderr to a tmp file\n    local tmpfile = map_dir .. \"/tmp/driver-stderr-\" .. box.id .. \".txt\"\n    local full_cmd = \"sh -c \" .. shell_quote(cmd .. \" 2>\" .. tmpfile)\n    local ph = io.popen(full_cmd, \"r\")\n    local stdout = ph:read(\"*a\")\n    local ok_close = ph:close()\n\n    -- read stderr if any\n    local sf = io.open(tmpfile, \"r\")\n    local stderr_text = sf and sf:read(\"*a\") or \"\"\n    if sf then sf:close() end\n    os.remove(tmpfile)\n\n    if not ok_close then\n        local err_msg = \"driver failed for box '\" .. box.id .. \"'\"\n        if stderr_text and #stderr_text > 0 then\n            err_msg = err_msg .. \": \" .. stderr_text:gsub(\"%s+$\", \"\")\n        end\n        return nil, err_msg\n    end\n\n    -- parse output JSON array from stdout\n    local result_arr, _, jerr = json.decode(stdout)\n    if not result_arr then\n        return nil, \"box '\" .. box.id .. \"': driver stdout is not valid JSON: \" ..\n            tostring(jerr) .. \" (got: \" .. tostring(stdout):sub(1, 80) .. \")\"\n    end\n    if type(result_arr) ~= \"table\" then\n        return nil, \"box '\" .. box.id .. \"': driver output must be a JSON array\"\n    end\n\n    -- map positional results to named output ports\n    local outputs = {}\n    for i, port in ipairs(box.outputs or {}) do\n        local raw = result_arr[i]\n        if raw ~= nil then\n            -- each element in the outer array is itself a JSON-encoded value\n            local val, _, aerr = json.decode(raw)\n            outputs[port.name] = aerr and raw or val\n        end\n    end\n\n    return outputs, nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ inputs_satisfied\nlocal function inputs_satisfied(box, store)\n    -- a box is ready when all its declared input ports have a value in the store\n    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n        if store[box.id .. \".\" .. port.name] == nil then\n            return false\n        end\n    end\n    return true\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ collect_inputs\nlocal function collect_inputs(box, store)\n    local inputs = {}\n    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n        inputs[port.name] = store[box.id .. \".\" .. port.name]\n    end\n    return inputs\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ fire_connections\nlocal function fire_connections(box, outputs, store, queue, boxes, retry_counts)\n    -- for branch boxes: evaluate predicates and fire the first matching port\n    -- for call boxes: push all wired output values directly\n    if box.kind == \"branch\" then\n        local input_val = outputs[\"_branch_input\"]\n        local fired = false\n        for _, port in ipairs(box.ports or {}) do\n            if port.name == \"else\" then goto next_port end\n            if port.predicate and eval_predicate(port.predicate, input_val) then\n                -- find and fire connections from this port\n                for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n                    if c.from_box == box.id and c.from_port == port.name then\n                        store[c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input] = input_val\n                        queue[#queue + 1] = c.to_box\n                    end\n                end\n                fired = true\n                break\n            end\n            ::next_port::\n        end\n\n        if not fired then\n            -- fire \"else\" port\n            for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n                if c.from_box == box.id and c.from_port == \"else\" then\n                    store[c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input] = input_val\n                    queue[#queue + 1] = c.to_box\n                    fired = true\n                end\n            end\n\n            if not fired then\n                -- unwired else: return signal to re-queue the upstream box\n                return \"retry\"\n            end\n        end\n\n    elseif box.kind == \"llm-route\" then\n        -- fire the matched output port; pass original text through\n        local routed = outputs._routed_port\n        local text   = outputs._text\n        local fired  = false\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box ~= box.id then goto lroute_next end\n            local port_field = c.from_port or c.from_output\n            if port_field == routed then\n                store[c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input] = text\n                local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n                if target and inputs_satisfied(target, store) then\n                    queue[#queue + 1] = c.to_box\n                end\n                fired = true\n            end\n            ::lroute_next::\n        end\n        if not fired then\n            -- fall through to \"else\" port if no match\n            for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n                if c.from_box ~= box.id then goto lroute_else_next end\n                local port_field = c.from_port or c.from_output\n                if port_field == \"else\" then\n                    store[c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input] = text\n                    local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n                    if target and inputs_satisfied(target, store) then\n                        queue[#queue + 1] = c.to_box\n                    end\n                end\n                ::lroute_else_next::\n            end\n        end\n    else\n        -- call box: push each output value to connected input ports\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box ~= box.id then goto next_conn end\n            local val = outputs[c.from_output]\n            store[c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input] = val\n            -- enqueue target if all its inputs are now satisfied\n            local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n            if target and inputs_satisfied(target, store) then\n                queue[#queue + 1] = c.to_box\n            end\n            ::next_conn::\n        end\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ write_last_run\nlocal function write_last_run(map_dir, run_state)\n    local tmp_dir = map_dir .. \"/tmp\"\n    local path    = tmp_dir .. \"/last-run.json\"\n    local f, ferr = io.open(path, \"w\")\n    if not f then\n        io.stderr:write(\"executor: cannot write last-run.json: \" .. tostring(ferr) .. \"\\n\")\n        return\n    end\n    f:write(json.encode(run_state, { indent = true }))\n    f:close()\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ execute\nfunction M.execute(graph, map_dir)\n    local boxes    = graph.boxes\n    local drivers  = graph.drivers\n    local entry_id = graph.entry\n\n    -- store: keyed by \"box_id.port_name\" -> value\n    local store = {}\n\n    -- per-box retry counters (for branch box else-retry)\n    local retry_counts = {}\n\n    -- pre-seed store with any literal values set on input ports\n    -- wires that fire at runtime will overwrite these, so wires always win\n    for box_id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n            if port.value ~= nil and port.value ~= \"\" then\n                -- try JSON decode first; fall back to raw string\n                local parsed, _, _ = json.decode(port.value)\n                store[box_id .. \".\" .. port.name] = parsed ~= nil and parsed or port.value\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    local queue   = { entry_id }\n    local visited = {}  -- boxes that have been run (prevent double-execution)\n    local run_log = {}  -- per-box execution records for last-run.json\n    local map_ok  = true\n    local map_err = nil\n\n    while #queue > 0 do\n        -- dequeue\n        local id = table.remove(queue, 1)\n\n        local box = boxes[id]\n        if not box then\n            map_ok  = false\n            map_err = \"unknown box in queue: '\" .. id .. \"'\"\n            break\n        end\n\n        -- skip boxes whose inputs are not yet satisfied (they'll be re-enqueued)\n        if not inputs_satisfied(box, store) then\n            goto next_iter\n        end\n\n        if visited[id] and box.kind ~= \"branch\" then\n            goto next_iter\n        end\n        visited[id] = true\n\n        local inputs = collect_inputs(box, store)\n\n        -- branch and llm-route are handled without a driver call; they route values\n        local outputs, task_err\n        if box.kind == \"branch\" then\n            local branch_val = inputs[(box.inputs or {})[1] and box.inputs[1].name or \"value\"]\n            outputs = { _branch_input = branch_val }\n            task_err = nil\n        elseif box.kind == \"llm-route\" then\n            local routed_port, text, err = llm_route_call(box, inputs)\n            outputs  = { _routed_port = routed_port, _text = text }\n            task_err = err\n        else\n            outputs, task_err = run_task(box, inputs, drivers, map_dir)\n        end\n\n        run_log[id] = {\n            inputs  = inputs,\n            outputs = outputs or {},\n            status  = task_err and \"error\" or \"ok\",\n            error   = task_err,\n        }\n\n        if task_err then\n            map_ok  = false\n            map_err = task_err\n            io.stderr:write(\"executor: \" .. task_err .. \"\\n\")\n            break\n        end\n\n        -- fire connections and enqueue newly-ready boxes\n        local signal = fire_connections(box, outputs, store, queue, boxes, retry_counts)\n        if signal == \"retry\" then\n            local max_retries = box.retry_limit or 3\n            retry_counts[id] = (retry_counts[id] or 0) + 1\n            if retry_counts[id] > max_retries then\n                map_ok  = false\n                map_err = \"branch box '\" .. id .. \"' exceeded retry limit (\" ..\n                    max_retries .. \")\"\n                break\n            end\n            -- find the upstream box(es) that feed this branch box and re-queue them\n            for src_id, src_box in pairs(boxes) do\n                for _, c in ipairs(src_box.connections or {}) do\n                    if c.from_box ~= src_id then goto next_src_conn end\n                    if c.to_box ~= id then goto next_src_conn end\n\n                    visited[src_id] = nil\n\n                    -- clear the branch box's input from the store so it\n                    -- re-fills when the upstream box runs again\n                    for _, p in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n                        store[id .. \".\" .. p.name] = nil\n                    end\n\n                    -- apply retry_vary: randomize specified input fields on the\n                    -- upstream box before re-running it\n                    local vary = src_box.retry_vary\n                    if vary then\n                        for field_name, range in pairs(vary) do\n                            local lo = tonumber(range.min) or 0\n                            local hi = tonumber(range.max) or 1\n                            local val = lo + math.random() * (hi - lo)\n                            store[src_id .. \".\" .. field_name] = val\n                        end\n                    end\n\n                    queue[#queue + 1] = src_id\n                    ::next_src_conn::\n                end\n            end\n        end\n\n        ::next_iter::\n    end\n\n    -- write last-run snapshot to tmp/\n    write_last_run(map_dir, {\n        ok     = map_ok,\n        error  = map_err,\n        boxes  = run_log,\n    })\n\n    return map_ok, map_err\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",

      "content":"# 108 — Branch box and predicate routing\n\n## Status\n\ncomplete\n\n## Implementation notes\n\nSchema fix (2026-05-07): `src/001-schema.lua` `validate_box` previously applied\nkind-specific connection validation to ALL connections in a box file. Since both\nendpoint boxes store the identical 4-field connection record, a call box file\ncan contain a reciprocal record with `from_port` (from a branch box), and a\nbranch box file can contain a reciprocal record with `from_output` (from a call\nbox). Fixed by routing connection validation on `c.from_box == box.id`:\noutgoing records get the strict kind-specific validator; incoming reciprocal\nrecords get a looser validator (`validate_incoming_connection`) that accepts\neither `from_output` or `from_port`.\n\nExecutor retry: branch inputs are cleared from the store on retry so the\nupstream box re-fires cleanly. `retry_vary` fields are pseudo-randomized in\nthe range before the upstream box is re-queued.\n\nVerified with `maps/branch-test/`: n=30 routes to write-low (result=\"30\"),\nn=70 routes to write-high (result=\"70\"). hello and driver-test maps pass\nregression.\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 104 (executor must exist; predicate evaluation is added to it here)\n- 107 (wire UI must exist; branch port wires need visual distinction)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo branch box type exists. All routing is linear (one output, one wire).\nThere is no mechanism to conditionally fire one box vs. another based on\na value.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA box with \"kind\": \"branch\" has named output ports instead of positional\noutputs. Each port (except \"else\") carries a predicate. The executor\nevaluates each predicate against the input value and fires the first port\nwhose predicate is true. If no predicate matches, the \"else\" port fires.\n\nPort predicates:\n  { \"op\": \"eq\"|\"lt\"|\"gt\"|\"lte\"|\"gte\"|\"contains\"|\"matches\", \"value\": <literal> }\n\n\"matches\" uses lua pattern matching against a string input.\n\"contains\" checks whether a string input contains the literal as a substring.\n\nBranch box behavior in two scenarios:\n\n  Numeric/string predicate branch:\n    - \"else\" port must be wired to something, or the runner refuses to start\n    - If no predicate matches and \"else\" fires, the program continues from\n      the \"else\" port's connection\n    - The runner logs which port fired for each branch box in last-run.json\n\n  LLM output classification:\n    - \"else\" port may be left unwired in the box file (omit the connection)\n    - If \"else\" fires on an unwired port, the runner re-queues the box\n      whose output fed this branch box (the immediately upstream box in the\n      path that led here)\n    - The upstream box is re-invoked with any fields marked \"retry_vary\"\n      in its box file pseudo-randomized (e.g., temperature, top_p)\n    - Retry limit: configurable per branch box, default 3. Exceeded retry\n      limit is a hard error, not a silent loop.\n\nThe \"retry_vary\" field on a box:\n  \"retry_vary\": { \"temperature\": { \"min\": 0.5, \"max\": 1.2 } }\n  On retry, any field listed here is replaced with a random value in range.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Add branch box handling to src/004-executor.lua:\n   - When a branch box fires, evaluate each port's predicate in order.\n   - Fire the first matching port's connection.\n   - If no match, fire \"else\". If \"else\" has no connection, trigger retry.\n2. Add retry state to the executor: a per-box retry counter in run state.\n   On retry trigger, decrement counter; if zero, halt with error.\n3. Implement retry_vary: before re-invoking the upstream box, for each\n   field in its retry_vary table, generate a random value in the given\n   range and override the corresponding input before invocation.\n4. Update src/003-loader.lua validation: branch boxes without an \"else\"\n   connection are valid only if at least one upstream box has a retry_vary\n   field. If neither condition is met, the validator rejects the map.\n5. Update assets/js/006-wires.js: branch box ports each get a distinct\n   color from a cycling palette. Port labels (\"rogue\", \"wizard\", \"else\")\n   are drawn alongside the port dot on the canvas.\n6. Update assets/js/004-inspector.js: branch box inspector shows port list\n   with add/remove, predicate editor per port (op dropdown + value input),\n   and retry limit input.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/001-architecture.md — branch box file format\n- issues/104 — executor (predicate evaluation added here)\n- issues/107 — wire UI (port color and label rendering)\n\n## Notes\n\nPort predicate evaluation order matters: ports are evaluated in the order\nthey appear in the \"ports\" array. The first matching predicate fires. This\nis intentional — the user controls priority by ordering ports. Document\nthis in the inspector UI (e.g., \"ports are evaluated top to bottom\").\n\nThe retry mechanism is deliberately minimal: it re-runs one upstream box\nwith varied parameters. It is not a general loop construct. If the user\nneeds complex retry logic (backoff, multiple retries with different\nstrategies), they should model it with explicit boxes wired in a cycle\nthrough a branch box. The built-in retry is for the common case of\n\"ask the LLM again with a different temperature.\"\n",

          "content":"# 210 — Comparator wire branching\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Supersedes\n\nThe original design of this issue described an `llm-route` box kind that used an\nOllama call to route between named output ports. That design has been removed:\nthe `llm-route` box kind, the executor's `llm_route_call` helper, and all\nrelated inspector and wire rendering code should be reverted. The problem it was\nsolving — conditional routing — is handled instead by the comparator mechanism\ndescribed here, which works on any box.\n\nSimilarly, the `branch` box kind (issue 108) is removed in favour of this mechanism.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nEvery box has named output ports. The inspector shows:\n- A toggle button labelled **compare** next to the output section.\n- When active, a text input for the comparand value.\n\nConnection schema changes:\n- Old: `{from_box, from_output|from_port, to_box, to_input}`\n- New: `{from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input}`\n  where `from_branch` is `null` (no comparator, one wire) or `\"lt\"`/`\"eq\"`/`\"gt\"`.\n\nThe canvas renders one output dot per box by default. When a comparator is\nactive, it renders three stacked dots labelled lt / eq / gt.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. **Box schema** — add optional `comparand` string to the box file format.\n   Remove `outputs` array from call box schema. Remove `ports` array and\n   predicate fields.\n\n2. **Connection schema** — replace `from_output`/`from_port` with `from_branch`\n   (`null` or `\"lt\"`/`\"eq\"`/`\"gt\"`). Update `src/001-schema.lua` validation\n   and `src/003-loader.lua` connection loading.\n\n3. **Executor (`src/004-executor.lua`)**:\n   - Remove `branch` and `llm-route` kind handling from the execute loop.\n   - Remove `fire_connections` named-port logic for both kinds.\n   - After a call box runs: if `box.comparand` is set, parse it as number,\n     compare against the output value (`lt`/`eq`/`gt`), and fire only the\n     connection whose `from_branch` matches. If value is not a number, halt\n     with error.           "content":"# 208 — Port literal values\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nInput ports on a box can only receive values from wired connections. If no wire\nis connected to an input port, the box never becomes \"ready\" and the runner\nskips it silently. There is no way to supply a constant value to an input from\nthe editor.\n\nPort names on both input and output ports are editable text fields in the\ninspector. This is fragile — the names must match the actual function signature\nexactly or the box silently misfires at runtime.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n**Input port names are read-only.** They are derived from the function's\nparameter names when the user selects a function via the file browser (issue\n207). The inspector displays them as non-editable labels. Only the literal\nvalue field is editable per input port.\n\n**Literal values:** Each input port has an optional literal value editable\ndirectly in the inspector panel. If the value field is non-empty and no wire is\nconnected to that port, the literal value is used at runtime. If a wire IS\nconnected, the wire's value overwrites the literal at runtime — wires always win.\n\nThe value field accepts JSON notation (numbers, strings with quotes, arrays,\nobjects) or bare strings for convenience. The executor tries JSON.decode first;\nif that fails, the raw string is used.\n\n**Output ports are gone.** Every call box has exactly one output wire carrying\nthe raw return value (see issue 210). The output section of the inspector is\nreplaced by the comparator toggle (see issue 210). `box.outputs` is removed\nfrom the call box schema.\n\nThis lets a box be fully configured from the inspector without needing a\ndedicated \"data\" box wired to it for every constant, and eliminates the class\nof runtime failures caused by mistyped port names.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. **Data model** — `box.inputs` port objects gain an optional `value` string\n   field. `box.outputs` is removed from call box schema (not needed; see\n   issue 210 for the single-wire model).\n\n2. **Inspector (`004-inspector.js`)**:\n   - `mk_port_display()` renders input port names as non-editable labels\n     (remove the name input).     "oldString":"## Implementation notes\n\nServer: added `handle_list_src` (GET /maps/:name/src) and `handle_get_src`\n(GET /maps/:name/src/:file) in src/005-http-server.lua.\n\nAPI: added `list_src_files()` and `get_src_file(filename)` in 003-api.js.\n\nParser (007-filebrowser.js): Lua matches `function M.name(args)` for inputs;\nscans function body for `return` statements and uses bare identifier names as\noutput port names (falls back to \"result\" for single complex expressions).\nBash matches `name() {` and scans for `local var=\"${N}\"` to name positional\ninputs; outputs always [\"output\"].\n\nInspector (004-inspector.js): ref field is now a read-only display plus a\nBrowse button that replaces the inspector with the file browser.     "newString":"## Implementation notes\n\nServer: added `handle_list_src` (GET /maps/:name/src) and `handle_get_src`\n(GET /maps/:name/src/:file) in src/005-http-server.lua.\n\nAPI: added `list_src_files()` and `get_src_file(filename)` in 003-api.js.\n\nParser (007-filebrowser.js): Lua matches `function M.name(args)` for inputs;\nscans function body for `return` statements and uses bare identifier names as\noutput port names (falls back to \"result\" for single complex expressions).\nBash matches `name() {` and scans for `local var=\"${N}\"` to name positional\ninputs; outputs always [\"output\"].\n\nInspector (004-inspector.js): ref field is now a read-only display plus a\nBrowse button that replaces the inspector with the file browser. On function\nclick, ref/fn/inputs/outputs are set on the box and saved. Inputs and outputs\nare shown as read-only port-display lists, not editable fields. Branch box\ninputs remain manually editable (no source function to parse).\n\n## Architecture update (2026-05-07)\n\nThe output port population step (deriving `box.outputs` from return statement\nnames) is removed as part of the single-wire output redesign (see issue 210).\nWhen a function is selected via the file browser, only `box.inputs` is set —\n`box.outputs` is no longer part of the call box schema.\n\nThe file browser's return-statement parser (`parse_lua_returns`) is kept for\nnow but the results are no longer applied to the box.     "originalFile":"# 207 — Source file browser and port auto-population\n\n## Status\n\ncomplete\n\n## Implementation notes\n\nServer: added `handle_list_src` (GET /maps/:name/src) and `handle_get_src`\n(GET /maps/:name/src/:file) in src/005-http-server.lua.\n\nAPI: added `list_src_files()` and `get_src_file(filename)` in 003-api.js.\n\nParser (007-filebrowser.js): Lua matches `function M.name(args)` for inputs;\nscans function body for `return` statements and uses bare identifier names as\noutput port names (falls back to \"result\" for single complex expressions).\nBash matches `name() {` and scans for `local var=\"${N}\"` to name positional\ninputs; outputs always [\"output\"].\n\nInspector (004-inspector.js): ref field is now a read-only display plus a\nBrowse button that replaces the inspector with the file browser. On function\nclick, ref/fn/inputs/outputs are set on the box and saved. Inputs and outputs\nare shown as read-only port-display lists, not editable fields. Branch box\ninputs remain manually editable (no source function to parse).\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 201 (boxes must render for this to be testable)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe inspector shows editable text inputs for ref, fn, inputs, and outputs.\nUsers must type port names by hand with no relationship to the actual function\nbeing called. Mismatches between the box config and the function signature\ncause silent runtime failures.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nFor call boxes:\n- \"ref\" field shows current value plus a Browse button\n- Clicking Browse replaces the inspector panel with a file list from the\n  map's src/ directory\n- Selecting a file shows all public functions parsed from that file, each\n  with its inputs (from the function signature) and outputs (from return\n  statements), displayed as read-only text\n- Clicking a function sets ref and fn on the box, derives inputs and outputs\n  from the parsed signature, saves the box, and returns to the normal\n  inspector view\n- Inputs and outputs in the inspector are read-only — not editable fields\n\nFor branch boxes: no file browser; ports remain manually configured.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Server: add GET /maps/:name/src (list files in src/) and\n   GET /maps/:name/src/:file (return file content as text/plain)\n2. API: add list_src_files() and get_src_file(filename)\n3. New file 007-filebrowser.js: parse_functions(content, filename),\n   render(container, on_select) that shows file list → function list\n4. Inspector: replace ref text input with display + Browse button;\n   remove editable inputs/outputs; show derived ports as read-only list\n5. When function selected: set box.ref, box.fn, box.inputs, box.outputs\n   (with type: \"any\" for all), autosave\n\n## Parser conventions\n\nLua (.lua): match `function M.name(args)` for inputs; scan function body\nfor `return` statements and use variable names as output names. If the\nreturn expression is not a bare identifier, name it \"result\".\n\nBash (.sh): match `name() {`; scan body for `local var=\"${N}\"` to name\npositional inputs; output is always one value named \"output\".\n\nOther extensions: show file in list but display \"no parser\" when selected.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/001-architecture.md — box file format (ref, fn, inputs, outputs)\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — inspector to modify\n- src/005-http-server.lua — server to extend\n",

          "old_string":"## Notes\n\nPort predicate evaluation order matters: ports are evaluated in the order\nthey appear in the \"ports\" array. The first matching predicate fires. This\nis intentional — the user controls priority by ordering ports. Document\nthis in the inspector UI (e.g., \"ports are evaluated top to bottom\").\n\nThe retry mechanism is deliberately minimal: it re-runs one upstream box\nwith varied parameters. It is not a general loop construct. If the user\nneeds complex retry logic (backoff, multiple retries with different\nstrategies), they should model it with explicit boxes wired in a cycle\nthrough a branch box. The built-in retry is for the common case of\n\"ask the LLM again with a different temperature.\"",
          "new_string":"## Notes\n\nPort predicate evaluation order matters: ports are evaluated in the order\nthey appear in the \"ports\" array. The first matching predicate fires. This\nis intentional — the user controls priority by ordering ports. Document\nthis in the inspector UI (e.g., \"ports are evaluated top to bottom\").\n\nThe retry mechanism is deliberately minimal: it re-runs one upstream box\nwith varied parameters. It is not a general loop construct. If the user\nneeds complex retry logic (backoff, multiple retries with different\nstrategies), they should model it with explicit boxes wired in a cycle\nthrough a branch box. The built-in retry is for the common case of\n\"ask the LLM again with a different temperature.\"\n\n## Architecture update (2026-05-07)\n\nThe `branch` box kind is removed as part of the single-wire output redesign.\nConditional routing is now handled by an optional **comparator** on any box\n(see issue 210): when active, the output wire splits into lt / eq / gt paths\ncompared against a literal number. Non-number values are a hard error.\n\nThe named-port model (`box.ports`, `from_port` in connections, predicate\nobjects, retry_vary) is fully removed. The retry mechanism goes away with it —\nthe loop-through-a-branch-box pattern is the recommended alternative if\nretry logic is needed.\n\nAll executor code specific to the branch kind (`fire_connections` branch\nsection, `retry_counts`, `retry_vary` application) should be reverted when\nissue 210 is implemented.",

    "oldString":"## Notes\n\nPort predicate evaluation order matters: ports are evaluated in the order\nthey appear in the \"ports\" array. The first matching predicate fires. Document\nthis in the inspector UI (e.g., \"ports are evaluated top to bottom\").\n\nThe retry mechanism is deliberately minimal: it re-runs one upstream box\nwith varied parameters. If the user\nneeds complex retry logic (backoff, multiple retries with different\nstrategies), they should model it with explicit boxes wired in a cycle\nthrough a branch box.     "userModified":false,
    "newString":"## Notes\n\nPort predicate evaluation order matters: ports are evaluated in the order\nthey appear in the \"ports\" array. The first matching predicate fires. This\nis intentional — the user controls priority by ordering ports. Document\nthis in the inspector UI (e.g., \"ports are evaluated top to bottom\").\n\nThe retry mechanism is deliberately minimal: it re-runs one upstream box\nwith varied parameters. It is not a general loop construct. If the user\nneeds complex retry logic (backoff, multiple retries with different\nstrategies), they should model it with explicit boxes wired in a cycle\nthrough a branch box. The built-in retry is for the common case of\n\"ask the LLM again with a different temperature.\"\n\n## Architecture update (2026-05-07)\n\nThe `branch` box kind is removed as part of the single-wire output redesign.\nConditional routing is now handled by an optional **comparator** on any box\n(see issue 210): when active, the output wire splits into lt / eq / gt paths\ncompared against a literal number. Non-number values are a hard error.\n\nThe named-port model (`box.ports`, `from_port` in connections, predicate\nobjects, retry_vary) is fully removed. The retry mechanism goes away with it —\nthe loop-through-a-branch-box pattern is the recommended alternative if\nretry logic is needed.\n\nAll executor code specific to the branch kind (`fire_connections` branch\nsection, `retry_counts`, `retry_vary` application) should be reverted when\nissue 210 is implemented.",
    "originalFile":"# 108 — Branch box and predicate routing\n\n## Status\n\ncomplete\n\n## Implementation notes\n\nSchema fix (2026-05-07): `src/001-schema.lua` `validate_box` previously applied\nkind-specific connection validation to ALL connections in a box file. Since both\nendpoint boxes store the identical 4-field connection record, a call box file\ncan contain a reciprocal record with `from_port` (from a branch box), and a\nbranch box file can contain a reciprocal record with `from_output` (from a call\nbox). Fixed by routing connection validation on `c.from_box == box.id`:\noutgoing records get the strict kind-specific validator; incoming reciprocal\nrecords get a looser validator (`validate_incoming_connection`) that accepts\neither `from_output` or `from_port`.\n\nExecutor retry: branch inputs are cleared from the store on retry so the\nupstream box re-fires cleanly. `retry_vary` fields are pseudo-randomized in\nthe range before the upstream box is re-queued.\n\nVerified with `maps/branch-test/`: n=30 routes to write-low (result=\"30\"),\nn=70 routes to write-high (result=\"70\"). hello and driver-test maps pass\nregression.\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 104 (executor must exist; predicate evaluation is added to it here)\n- 107 (wire UI must exist; branch port wires need visual distinction)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo branch box type exists. All routing is linear (one output, one wire).\nThere is no mechanism to conditionally fire one box vs. another based on\na value.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA box with \"kind\": \"branch\" has named output ports instead of positional\noutputs. Each port (except \"else\") carries a predicate. The executor\nevaluates each predicate against the input value and fires the first port\nwhose predicate is true. If no predicate matches, the \"else\" port fires.\n\nPort predicates:\n  { \"op\": \"eq\"|\"lt\"|\"gt\"|\"lte\"|\"gte\"|\"contains\"|\"matches\", \"value\": <literal> }\n\n\"matches\" uses lua pattern matching against a string input.\n\"contains\" checks whether a string input contains the literal as a substring.\n\nBranch box behavior in two scenarios:\n\n  Numeric/string predicate branch:\n    - \"else\" port must be wired to something, or the runner refuses to start\n    - If no predicate matches and \"else\" fires, the program continues from\n      the \"else\" port's connection\n    - The runner logs which port fired for each branch box in last-run.json\n\n  LLM output classification:\n    - \"else\" port may be left unwired in the box file (omit the connection)\n    - If \"else\" fires on an unwired port, the runner re-queues the box\n      whose output fed this branch box (the immediately upstream box in the\n      path that led here)\n    - The upstream box is re-invoked with any fields marked \"retry_vary\"\n      in its box file pseudo-randomized (e.g., temperature, top_p)\n    - Retry limit: configurable per branch box, default 3. Exceeded retry\n      limit is a hard error, not a silent loop.\n\nThe \"retry_vary\" field on a box:\n  \"retry_vary\": { \"temperature\": { \"min\": 0.5, \"max\": 1.2 } }\n  On retry, any field listed here is replaced with a random value in range.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Add branch box handling to src/004-executor.lua:\n   - When a branch box fires, evaluate each port's predicate in order.\n   - Fire the first matching port's connection.\n   - If no match, fire \"else\". If \"else\" has no connection, trigger retry.\n2. Add retry state to the executor: a per-box retry counter in run state.\n   On retry trigger, decrement counter; if zero, halt with error.\n3. Implement retry_vary: before re-invoking the upstream box, for each\n   field in its retry_vary table, generate a random value in the given\n   range and override the corresponding input before invocation.\n4. Update src/003-loader.lua validation: branch boxes without an \"else\"\n   connection are valid only if at least one upstream box has a retry_vary\n   field. If neither condition is met, the validator rejects the map.\n5. Update assets/js/006-wires.js: branch box ports each get a distinct\n   color from a cycling palette. Port labels (\"rogue\", \"wizard\", \"else\")\n   are drawn alongside the port dot on the canvas.\n6. Update assets/js/004-inspector.js: branch box inspector shows port list\n   with add/remove, predicate editor per port (op dropdown + value input),\n   and retry limit input.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/001-architecture.md — branch box file format\n- issues/104 — executor (predicate evaluation added here)\n- issues/107 — wire UI (port color and label rendering)\n\n## Notes\n\nPort predicate evaluation order matters: ports are evaluated in the order\nthey appear in the \"ports\" array. The first matching predicate fires. This\nis intentional — the user controls priority by ordering ports. Document\nthis in the inspector UI (e.g., \"ports are evaluated top to bottom\").\n\nThe retry mechanism is deliberately minimal: it re-runs one upstream box\nwith varied parameters. It is not a general loop construct. If the user\nneeds complex retry logic (backoff, multiple retries with different\nstrategies), they should model it with explicit boxes wired in a cycle\nthrough a branch box. The built-in retry is for the common case of\n\"ask the LLM again with a different temperature.\"\n",

      "content":"// Box rendering, layout, and hit testing.\n// Each box knows its world-space position; the camera transform is applied by the canvas.\n\nconst Boxes = (() => {\n  const BOX_W         = 180;\n  const BOX_HEADER    = 36;\n  const PORT_ROW_H    = 22;\n  const PORT_R        = 6;   // port dot radius in world units\n  const MIN_BOX_H     = 80;\n\n  const KIND_COLOR = { call: '#4a9eff', branch: '#ff8c42', data: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  // boxes: { [id]: box_data }\n  let boxes = {};\n\n  // {{{ box_height\n  function box_height(box) {\n    const n = Math.max(\n      (box.inputs || []).length,\n      (box.kind === 'branch' ? (box.ports || []).length : (box.outputs || []).length)\n    );\n    return Math.max(MIN_BOX_H, BOX_HEADER + n * PORT_ROW_H + 8);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ port_positions\n  // Returns world-space {x,y} for each port dot on a box.\n  function port_positions(box) {\n    const bx = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const by = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const h  = box_height(box);\n    const inputs  = box.inputs  || [];\n    const outputs = box.kind === 'branch' ? port_palette[i % port_palette.length] : color;\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = dot_color + '44';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = dot_color;\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      ctx.fillStyle  = '#9ea3c0';\n      ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n      ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n      ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x - PORT_R - 4, p.y);\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_id) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      draw_box(ctx, boxes[id], id === selected_id);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_port\n  // Returns {box_id, port_name, side, x, y} for the port under world point (wx,wy), or null.\n  function hit_test_port(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(boxes[id]);\n      for (const p of [...inputs, ...outputs]) {\n        const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n        if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= (PORT_R + 4) * (PORT_R + 4)) {\n          return { box_id: id, port_name: p.name, side: p.side, x: p.x, y: p.y };\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_box\n  // Returns box id if (wx,wy) is inside a box body, or null.\n  function hit_test_box(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const b = boxes[id];\n      const x = b.ui?.x ??     "type":"text",
    "file":{
      "content":"// Inspector sidebar: shows and edits the selected box's fields.\n// Fires PUT to the server on every field change (autosave).\n// For call boxes, ref/fn are set via the file browser; ports are read-only and derived.\n\nconst Inspector = (() => {\n  const panel  = document.getElementById('inspector');\n  const title  = document.getElementById('inspector-title');\n  const fields = document.getElementById('inspector-fields');\n\n  let current_box  = null;\n  let on_change_cb = null;\n  let on_delete_cb = null;\n\n  // {{{ hide\n  function hide() {\n    panel.classList.add('hidden');\n    current_box  = null;\n    on_delete_cb = null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ save\n  async function save() {\n    if (!current_box) return;\n    try {\n      await API.put_box(current_box.id, current_box);\n      if (on_change_cb) on_change_cb(current_box);\n    } catch(e) {\n      console.error('autosave failed:', e.message);\n      status_msg('save error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_row\n  function mk_row(label_text, input_el) {\n    const row = document.createElement('div');\n    row.className = 'field-row';\n    const lbl = document.createElement('label');\n    lbl.textContent = label_text;\n    row.appendChild(lbl);\n    row.appendChild(input_el);\n    return row;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_text_input\n  function mk_text_input(value, on_input) {\n    const inp = document.createElement('input');\n    inp.type  = 'text';\n    inp.value = value || '';\n    inp.addEventListener('input', () => { on_input(inp.value); save(); });\n    return inp;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_readonly\n  function mk_readonly(value) {\n    const el = document.createElement('div');\n    el.className   = 'field-readonly';\n    el.textContent = value || '—';\n    return el;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_port_display\n  // Port name is editable; type is read-only (derived from source).\n  // show_value: when true (inputs only), adds a literal value field.\n  function mk_port_display(ports, show_value) {\n    const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    wrap.className = 'port-display';\n    if (!ports || ports.length === 0) {\n      const empty = document.createElement('span');\n      empty.className   = 'port-display-empty';\n      empty.textContent = '(none)';\n      wrap.appendChild(empty);\n    } else {\n      ports.forEach((p, i) => {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className = 'port-display-row';\n\n        const name_inp = document.createElement('input');\n        name_inp.type  = 'text';\n        name_inp.value = p.name || '';\n        name_inp.className = 'port-name-inp';\n        name_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { ports[i].name = name_inp.value; save(); });\n        row.appendChild(name_inp);\n\n        if (p.type && p.type !== 'any') {\n          const type_el = document.createElement('span');\n          type_el.className   = 'port-type';\n          type_el.textContent = ':' + p.type;\n          row.appendChild(type_el);\n        }\n\n        if (show_value) {\n          const val_inp = document.createElement('input');\n          val_inp.type        = 'text';\n          val_inp.value       = p.value !== undefined ? String(p.value) : '';\n          val_inp.placeholder = 'value…';\n          val_inp.className   = 'port-val-inp';\n          val_inp.addEventListener('input', () => {\n            // empty string means \"no literal\" — remove the field entirely\n            ports[i].value = val_inp.value === '' ? undefined : val_inp.value;\n            save();\n          });\n          row.appendChild(val_inp);\n        }\n\n        wrap.appendChild(row);\n      });\n    }\n    return wrap;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_simple_port_list\n  // Addable list of named output ports — no predicates. Used by llm-route.\n  function mk_simple_port_list(ports, on_change) {\n    const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    wrap.className = 'port-list';\n    const render_ports = () => {\n      wrap.innerHTML = '';\n      ports.forEach((p, i) => {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className = 'port-row';\n        const name_inp = document.createElement('input');\n        name_inp.type  = 'text';\n        name_inp.value = p.name || '';\n        name_inp.placeholder = 'port name';\n        name_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { ports[i].name = name_inp.value; on_change(); save(); });\n        row.appendChild(name_inp);\n        const del_btn = document.createElement('button');\n        del_btn.textContent = '×';\n        del_btn.className   = 'port-del';\n        del_btn.addEventListener('click', () => { ports.splice(i, 1); render_ports(); on_change(); save(); });\n        row.appendChild(del_btn);\n        wrap.appendChild(row);\n      });\n      const add_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      add_btn.textContent = '+ port';\n      add_btn.className   = 'add-port';\n      add_btn.addEventListener('click', () => { ports.push({ name: '' }); render_ports(); on_change(); save(); });\n      wrap.appendChild(add_btn);\n    };\n    render_ports();\n    return wrap;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_branch_port_list\n  const OPS = ['eq','lt','gt','lte','gte','contains','matches'];\n  function mk_branch_port_list(ports, on_change) {\n    const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    wrap.className = 'port-list';\n\n    const render_ports = () => {\n      wrap.innerHTML = '';\n      ports.forEach((p, i) => {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className = 'port-row branch-port-row';\n\n        const name_inp = document.createElement('input');\n        name_inp.type  = 'text';\n        name_inp.value = p.name || '';\n        name_inp.placeholder = 'port name';\n        name_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { ports[i].name = name_inp.value; on_change(); save(); });\n        row.appendChild(name_inp);\n\n        if (p.name !== 'else') {\n          if (!p.predicate) p.predicate = { op: 'eq', value: '' };\n\n          const op_sel = document.createElement('select');\n          OPS.forEach(op => {\n            const opt = document.createElement('option');\n            opt.value = op; opt.textContent = op;\n            if (op === p.predicate.op) opt.selected = true;\n            op_sel.appendChild(opt);\n          });\n          op_sel.addEventListener('change', () => { ports[i].predicate.op = op_sel.value; save(); });\n\n          const val_inp = document.createElement('input');\n          val_inp.type  = 'text';\n          val_inp.value = p.predicate.value ?? render_ports(); on_change(); save(); });\n          row.appendChild(del_btn);\n        }\n\n        wrap.appendChild(row);\n      });\n\n      const add_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      add_btn.textContent = '+ port';\n      add_btn.className   = 'add-port';\n      add_btn.addEventListener('click', () => {\n        const else_i = ports.findIndex(p => p.name === 'else');\n        const new_port = { name: '', predicate: { op: 'eq', value: '' } };\n        if (else_i >= 0) ports.splice(else_i, 0, new_port);\n        else ports.push(new_port);\n        render_ports(); on_change(); save();\n      });\n      wrap.appendChild(add_btn);\n    };\n\n    render_ports();\n    return wrap;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ open_browser\n  // Replaces inspector content with the file browser.\n  // On function select: populates ref/fn/inputs/outputs and returns to normal view.\n  function open_browser() {\n    title.textContent = 'browse src/';\n    fields.innerHTML  = '';\n    FileBrowser.render(fields, (filename, fn) => {\n      current_box.ref     = filename;\n      current_box.fn      = fn.name;\n      current_box.inputs  = fn.inputs.map(n  => ({ name: n, type: 'any' }));\n      current_box.outputs = fn.outputs.map(n => ({ name: n, type: 'any' }));\n      save().then(() => show(current_box, on_change_cb));\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ show\n  function show(box, on_changed, on_delete) {\n    current_box  = box;\n    on_change_cb = on_changed;\n    on_delete_cb = on_delete || null;\n    panel.classList.remove('hidden');\n    title.textContent = box.id;\n    fields.innerHTML  = '';\n\n    // delete button — always visible at the top of the inspector\n    if (on_delete_cb) {\n      const del_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      del_btn.textContent = 'delete box';\n      del_btn.className   = 'delete-box-btn';\n      del_btn.onclick     = () => on_delete_cb();\n      fields.appendChild(del_btn);\n    }\n\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('label',\n      mk_text_input(box.label, v => { current_box.label = v; })));\n\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('kind', (() => {\n      const sel = document.createElement('select');\n      ['call','branch','data','llm-route'].forEach(k => {\n        const opt = document.createElement('option');\n        opt.value = k; opt.textContent = k;\n        if (k === box.kind) opt.selected = true;\n        sel.appendChild(opt);\n      });\n      sel.addEventListener('change', () => {\n        current_box.kind = sel.value;\n        show(current_box, on_change_cb);\n        save();\n      });\n      return sel;\n    })()));\n\n    if (box.kind === 'call' || box.kind === 'data') {\n      // ref: editable text input + browse button to populate via file browser\n      const ref_wrap = document.createElement('div');\n      ref_wrap.style.cssText = 'display:flex;gap:4px;align-items:center;';\n      const ref_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      ref_inp.type  = 'text';\n      ref_inp.value = box.ref || '';\n      ref_inp.style.flex = '1';\n      ref_inp.style.minWidth = '0';\n      ref_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { current_box.ref = ref_inp.value; save(); });\n      const browse_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      browse_btn.className   = 'toolbar-btn';\n      browse_btn.textContent = 'browse';\n      browse_btn.style.whiteSpace = 'nowrap';\n      browse_btn.onclick = open_browser;\n      ref_wrap.appendChild(ref_inp);\n      ref_wrap.appendChild(browse_btn);\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('ref', ref_wrap));\n\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('fn', mk_readonly(box.fn)));\n\n      const in_sec = document.createElement('div');\n      in_sec.className   = 'section-label';\n      in_sec.textContent = 'inputs';\n      fields.appendChild(in_sec);\n      fields.appendChild(mk_port_display(box.inputs, true));\n\n      const out_sec = document.createElement('div');\n      out_sec.className   = 'section-label';\n      out_sec.textContent = 'outputs';\n      fields.appendChild(out_sec);\n      fields.appendChild(mk_port_display(box.outputs, false));\n    }\n\n    if (box.kind === 'branch') {\n      if (!current_box.ports) current_box.ports = [{ name: 'else' }];\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('retry limit',\n        mk_text_input(String(box.retry_limit ?? 3),\n          v => { current_box.retry_limit = parseInt(v) || 3; })));\n\n      // branch inputs are manually configured (no source file to parse)\n      const in_sec = document.createElement('div');\n      in_sec.className   = 'section-label';\n      in_sec.textContent = 'inputs';\n      fields.appendChild(in_sec);\n      if (!current_box.inputs) current_box.inputs = [];\n      const in_list = document.createElement('div');\n      in_list.className = 'port-list';\n      (current_box.inputs || []).forEach((p, i) => {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className = 'port-row';\n        const ni = document.createElement('input');\n        ni.type = 'text'; ni.value = p.name || ''; ni.placeholder = 'name';\n        ni.addEventListener('input', () => { current_box.inputs[i].name = ni.value; save(); });\n        const ti = document.createElement('input');\n        ti.type = 'text';     for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                -- outgoing connections (this box is the source) require from_port;\n                -- incoming reciprocal records from call boxes use Used by both the runner and the server\n-- before any file is written to disk.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ valid_kinds\nlocal valid_kinds = { call = true, data = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ valid_branches\n-- null/nil means no comparator (single wire); the three strings are comparator outputs.\nlocal valid_branches = { lt = true, eq = true, gt = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ err\nlocal function err(errors, msg)\n    errors[#errors + 1] = msg\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_connection\nlocal function validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- from_branch is nil (no comparator) or one of \"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\"\n    if c.from_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.from_branch ~= nil and not valid_branches[c.from_branch] then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] 'from_branch' must be nil, 'lt', 'eq', or 'gt'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_box\nfunction M.validate_box(box)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(box) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"box must be a table\" }\n    end\n\n    if box.id == nil or type(box.id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'id'\")\n    end\n    if box.label == nil or type(box.label) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'label'\")\n    end\n    if box.kind == nil or not valid_kinds[box.kind] then\n        err(errors, \"missing or invalid 'kind' (must be 'call' or 'data')\")\n    end\n\n    if box.kind == \"call\" or box.kind == \"data\" then\n        if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"box missing 'ref'\")\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        -- comparand: optional; if present it must be a string parseable as number at runtime\n        if box.comparand ~= nil and type(box.comparand) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'comparand' must be a string\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a table\")\n        elseif box.ui.x == nil or box.ui.y == nil then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must have 'x' and 'y' fields\")\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or type(meta.name) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'name'\")\n    end\n    if meta.entry_box_id == nil or type(meta.entry_box_id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'entry_box_id'\")\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_drivers\nfunction M.validate_drivers(drivers)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(drivers) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"drivers.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    for ext, path in pairs(drivers) do\n        if type(ext) ~= \"string\" or ext:sub(1, 1) ~= \".\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver key '\" .. tostring(ext) .. \"' must be a dot-prefixed extension\")\n        end\n        if type(path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver value for '\" .. ext .. \"' must be a string path\")\n        end\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/001-schema.lua"
        }

The graph is the runner's\n-- internal representation of the map.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal json   = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal schema = require(\"001-schema\")\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ read_json_file\nlocal function read_json_file(path)\n    local f, ferr = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then return nil, \"cannot open \" .. path .. \": \" .. ferr end\n    local raw = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    local obj, _, jerr = json.decode(raw)\n    if not obj then return nil, \"JSON error in \" .. path .. \": \" .. tostring(jerr) end\n    return obj\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ load_drivers\nlocal function load_drivers(map_dir)\n    -- map-local drivers take priority; fall back to global drivers alongside the runner\n    local local_path  = map_dir .. \"/drivers.json\"\n    local global_path = DIR .. \"/drivers.json\"\n\n    local drivers = {}\n\n    -- load global first so local can override\n    local gd, _ = read_json_file(global_path)\n    if gd then\n        for ext, path in pairs(gd) do drivers[ext] = path end\n    end\n\n    local ld, _ = read_json_file(local_path)\n    if ld then\n        for ext, path in pairs(ld) do drivers[ext] = path end\n    end\n\n    return drivers\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ list_box_files\nlocal function list_box_files(boxes_dir)\n    local files = {}\n    local handle = io.popen(\"ls \" .. boxes_dir .. \"/*.json 2>/dev/null\")\n    if not handle then return files end\n    local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n    handle:close()\n    for path in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n        files[#files + 1] = path\n    end\n    return files\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ extension_of\nlocal function extension_of(path)\n    return path:match(\"%.([^./]+)$\") and (\".\" .. path:match(\"%.([^./]+)$\")) or \"\"\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ detect_cycles\n-- depth-first search from start_id; all cycles are errors\nlocal function detect_cycles(boxes, start_id)\n    local visited  = {}\n    local in_stack = {}\n    local errors   = {}\n\n    local function dfs(id)\n        if in_stack[id] then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = \"cycle detected at box '\" .. id .. \"'\"\n            return\n        end\n        if visited[id] then return end\n        visited[id]  = true\n        in_stack[id] = true\n\n        local box = boxes[id]\n        if not box then\n            in_stack[id] = false\n            return\n        end\n\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box == id then\n                dfs(c.to_box)\n            end\n        end\n\n        in_stack[id] = false\n    end\n\n    dfs(start_id)\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ load_map\nfunction M.load_map(map_dir)\n    local errors = {}\n\n    -- meta.json\n    local meta, merr = read_json_file(map_dir .. \"/meta.json\")\n    if not meta then\n        return nil, { merr }\n    end\n    local meta_errs = schema.validate_meta(meta)\n    for _, e in ipairs(meta_errs) do errors[#errors + 1] = \"meta.json: \" .. e end\n\n    -- drivers\n    local drivers = load_drivers(map_dir)\n\n    -- boxes\n    local boxes = {}\n    local box_files = list_box_files(map_dir .. \"/boxes\")\n    for _, path in ipairs(box_files) do\n        local box, berr = read_json_file(path)\n        if not box then\n            errors[#errors + 1] = berr\n        else\n            local box_errs = schema.validate_box(box)\n            if #box_errs > 0 then\n                for _, e in ipairs(box_errs) do\n                    errors[#errors + 1] = path .. \": \" .. e\n                end\n            else\n                boxes[box.id] = box\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if #errors > 0 then return nil, errors end\n\n    local graph = {\n        meta    = meta,\n        boxes   = boxes,\n        entry   = meta.entry_box_id,\n        drivers = drivers,\n        map_dir = map_dir,\n    }\n\n    return graph, {}\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_graph\nfunction M.validate_graph(graph)\n    local errors = {}\n    local boxes  = graph.boxes\n    local drivers = graph.drivers\n\n    -- entry box must exist\n    if not boxes[graph.entry] then\n        errors[#errors + 1] = \"entry_box_id '\" .. tostring(graph.entry) ..\n            \"' does not match any box\"\n    end\n\n    for id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        -- connection integrity: reciprocal check (outgoing connections only)\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box ~= id then goto next_conn end\n\n            local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n            if target == nil then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id ..\n                    \"': connection to unknown box '\" .. tostring(c.to_box) .. \"'\"\n                goto next_conn\n            end\n\n            local found = false\n            for _, tc in ipairs(target.connections or {}) do\n                if tc.from_box    == c.from_box    and\n                   tc.from_branch == c.from_branch and\n                   tc.to_box      == c.to_box      and\n                   tc.to_input    == c.to_input    then\n                    found = true\n                    break\n                end\n            end\n            if not found then\n                local branch_str = c.from_branch and (\".\" .. c.from_branch) or \"\"\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id .. \"': connection \" ..\n                    c.from_box .. branch_str ..\n                    \" -> \" .. c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input ..\n                    \" not reciprocated in target\"\n            end\n\n            ::next_conn::\n        end\n\n        -- driver must exist for call/data boxes with a ref\n        if (box.kind == \"call\" or box.kind == \"data\") and box.ref then\n            local ext = extension_of(box.ref)\n            -- binary callers (no fn) don't need a driver — they are the driver\n            if box.fn and ext ~= \"\" and not drivers[ext] then\n                errors[#errors + 1] = \"box '\" .. id ..\n                    \"': no driver defined for extension '\" .. ext .. \"'\"\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- cycle detection from entry box\n    if boxes[graph.entry] then\n        local cycle_errors = detect_cycles(boxes, graph.entry)\n        for _, e in ipairs(cycle_errors) do\n            errors[#errors + 1] = e\n        end\n    end\n\n    return #errors == 0, errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",

    "content":"-- Synchronous FSM executor for the SoraMech runner.\n-- Walks the graph from the entry box, invokes language drivers for each\n-- box in dependency order, and threads output values through wires.\n-- Each box call is isolated in run_task() — the future thread pool swap point.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal M    = {}\n\n-- {{{ shell_quote\nlocal function shell_quote(s)\n    -- wrap a string in single quotes, escaping any embedded single quotes\n    return \"'\" .. tostring(s):gsub(\"'\", \"'\\\\''\") .. \"'\"\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ driver_path_for\nlocal function driver_path_for(ref, drivers)\n    -- binary callers (no extension mapping needed — they are executable directly)\n    -- source callers: look up extension in driver table\n    local ext = ref:match(\"%.([^./]+)$\")\n    if not ext then return ref end  -- no extension: treat as binary\n    local driver = drivers[\".\" .. ext]\n    return driver\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ run_task\n-- The task boundary. In v1: synchronous. Future: hand this signature to\n-- the thread pool. Returns a single output value and ok/err.\nlocal function run_task(box, inputs, drivers, map_dir)\n    local ref = box.ref\n    local fn  = box.fn\n\n    -- locate the driver for this ref\n    local driver = driver_path_for(ref, drivers)\n    if not driver then\n        return nil, \"no driver found for ref '\" .. ref .. \"'\"\n    end\n\n    -- resolve ref relative to map_dir\n    local abs_ref = map_dir .. \"/\" .. ref\n\n    -- build argument list: each input port's value as a JSON-encoded shell arg\n    local args = {}\n    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n        local val = inputs[port.name]\n        if val == nil then\n            -- nil input becomes JSON null\n            args[#args + 1] = shell_quote(json.encode(nil))\n        else\n            args[#args + 1] = shell_quote(json.encode(val))\n        end\n    end\n\n    local cmd\n    if fn then\n        -- source caller: driver file fn arg_count [args...]\n        cmd = driver .. \" \" .. shell_quote(abs_ref) .. \" \" ..\n              shell_quote(fn) .. \" \" .. #args\n        for _, a in ipairs(args) do cmd = cmd .. \" \" .. a end\n    else\n        -- binary caller: run ref directly with args\n        cmd = abs_ref .. \" \" .. #args\n        for _, a in ipairs(args) do cmd = cmd .. \" \" .. a end\n    end\n\n    -- invoke driver; capture stdout; errors go to stderr (visible in terminal)\n    local tmpfile = map_dir .. \"/tmp/driver-stderr-\" .. box.id .. \".txt\"\n    local full_cmd = \"sh -c \" .. shell_quote(cmd .. \" 2>\" .. tmpfile)\n    local ph = io.popen(full_cmd, \"r\")\n    local stdout = ph:read(\"*a\")\n    local ok_close = ph:close()\n\n    -- read stderr if any\n    local sf = io.open(tmpfile, \"r\")\n    local stderr_text = sf and sf:read(\"*a\") or \"\"\n    if sf then sf:close() end\n    os.remove(tmpfile)\n\n    if not ok_close then\n        local err_msg = \"driver failed for box '\" .. box.id .. \"'\"\n        if stderr_text and #stderr_text > 0 then\n            err_msg = err_msg .. \": \" .. stderr_text:gsub(\"%s+$\", \"\")\n        end\n        return nil, err_msg\n    end\n\n    -- parse output JSON array from stdout\n    local result_arr, _, jerr = json.decode(stdout)\n    if not result_arr then\n        return nil, \"box '\" .. box.id .. \"': driver stdout is not valid JSON: \" ..\n            tostring(jerr) .. \" (got: \" .. tostring(stdout):sub(1, 80) .. \")\"\n    end\n    if type(result_arr) ~= \"table\" then\n        return nil, \"box '\" .. box.id .. \"': driver output must be a JSON array\"\n    end\n\n    -- take the first element of the array as the single output value\n    local raw = result_arr[1]\n    local output_val\n    if raw ~= nil then\n        local val, _, aerr = json.decode(raw)\n        output_val = aerr and raw or val\n    end\n\n    return output_val, nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ inputs_satisfied\nlocal function inputs_satisfied(box, store)\n    -- a box is ready when all its declared input ports have a value in the store\n    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n        if store[box.id .. \".\" .. port.name] == nil then\n            return false\n        end\n    end\n    return true\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ collect_inputs\nlocal function collect_inputs(box, store)\n    local inputs = {}\n    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n        inputs[port.name] = store[box.id .. \".\" .. port.name]\n    end\n    return inputs\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ fire_connections\n-- Routes the single output value through wired connections.\n-- If box.comparand is set: compare output against it (must be a number or error).\n-- Otherwise: fire all connections whose from_branch is nil.\n-- Returns nil on success, or an error string.\nlocal function fire_connections(box, output_val, store, queue, boxes)\n    if box.comparand and box.comparand ~= \"\" then\n        -- comparator mode: output must be a number\n        local comparand = tonumber(box.comparand)\n        if not comparand then\n            return \"box '\" .. box.id .. \"': comparand '\" ..\n                tostring(box.comparand) .. \"' is not a valid number\"\n        end\n        local num_val = tonumber(output_val)\n        if not num_val then\n            return \"box '\" .. box.id .. \"': output value '\" ..\n                tostring(output_val) .. \"' is not a number, but comparator is configured\"\n        end\n\n        -- determine which branch to fire\n        local branch\n        if num_val < comparand then\n            branch = \"lt\"\n        elseif num_val == comparand then\n            branch = \"eq\"\n        else\n            branch = \"gt\"\n        end\n\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box ~= box.id then goto next_cmp_conn end\n            if c.from_branch == branch then\n                store[c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input] = output_val\n                local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n                if target and inputs_satisfied(target, store) then\n                    queue[#queue + 1] = c.to_box\n                end\n            end\n            ::next_cmp_conn::\n        end\n    else\n        -- single-wire mode: fire connections where from_branch is nil\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box ~= box.id then goto next_conn end\n            if c.from_branch == nil then\n                store[c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input] = output_val\n                local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n                if target and inputs_satisfied(target, store) then\n                    queue[#queue + 1] = c.to_box\n                end\n            end\n            ::next_conn::\n        end\n    end\n    return nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ write_last_run\nlocal function write_last_run(map_dir, run_state)\n    local tmp_dir = map_dir .. \"/tmp\"\n    local path    = tmp_dir .. \"/last-run.json\"\n    local f, ferr = io.open(path, \"w\")\n    if not f then\n        io.stderr:write(\"executor: cannot write last-run.json: \" .. tostring(ferr) .. \"\\n\")\n        return\n    end\n    f:write(json.encode(run_state, { indent = true }))\n    f:close()\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ execute\nfunction M.execute(graph, map_dir)\n    local boxes    = graph.boxes\n    local drivers  = graph.drivers\n    local entry_id = graph.entry\n\n    -- store: keyed by \"box_id.port_name\" -> value\n    local store = {}\n\n    -- pre-seed store with any literal values set on input ports;\n    -- wires that fire at runtime will overwrite these, so wires always win\n    for box_id, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n            if port.value ~= nil and port.value ~= \"\" then\n                -- try JSON decode first; fall back to raw string\n                local parsed, _, _ = json.decode(port.value)\n                store[box_id .. \".\" .. port.name] = parsed ~= nil and parsed or port.value\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    local queue   = { entry_id }\n    local visited = {}  -- boxes that have been run (prevent double-execution)\n    local run_log = {}  -- per-box execution records for last-run.json\n    local map_ok  = true\n    local map_err = nil\n\n    while #queue > 0 do\n        -- dequeue\n        local id = table.remove(queue, 1)\n\n        local box = boxes[id]\n        if not box then\n            map_ok  = false\n            map_err = \"unknown box in queue: '\" .. id .. \"'\"\n            break\n        end\n\n        -- skip boxes whose inputs are not yet satisfied\n        if not inputs_satisfied(box, store) then\n            goto next_iter\n        end\n\n        if visited[id] then\n            goto next_iter\n        end\n        visited[id] = true\n\n        local inputs = collect_inputs(box, store)\n\n        local output_val, task_err = run_task(box, inputs, drivers, map_dir)\n\n        run_log[id] = {\n            inputs = inputs,\n            output = output_val,\n            status = task_err and \"error\" or \"ok\",\n            error  = task_err,\n        }\n\n        if task_err then\n            map_ok  = false\n            map_err = task_err\n            io.stderr:write(\"executor: \" .. task_err .. \"\\n\")\n            break\n        end\n\n        -- route output through wired connections\n        local conn_err = fire_connections(box, output_val, store, queue, boxes)\n        if conn_err then\n            map_ok  = false\n            map_err = conn_err\n            io.stderr:write(\"executor: \" .. conn_err .. \"\\n\")\n            break\n        end\n\n        ::next_iter::\n    end\n\n    -- write last-run snapshot to tmp/\n    write_last_run(map_dir, {\n        ok    = map_ok,\n        error = map_err,\n        boxes = run_log,\n    })\n\n    return map_ok, map_err\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",
