3 : 1;\n    return Math.max(MIN_BOX_H, BOX_HEADER + Math.max(n_in, n_out) * PORT_ROW_H + 8);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ port_positions\n  // Returns world-space {x,y} for each port dot on a box.\n  // Output side: null-named single dot when no comparand; 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' dots when comparand set.\n  function port_positions(box) {\n    const bx = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const by = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const h  = box_height(box);\n    const inputs = box.inputs || [];\n\n    const in_pts = inputs.map((p, i) => ({\n      name: p.name, side: 'input',\n      x: bx,\n      y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n    }));\n\n    let out_pts;\n    if (box.comparand && box.comparand !== '') {\n      // three comparator dots\n      out_pts = ['lt', 'eq', 'gt'].map((branch, i) => ({\n        name: branch, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n      }));\n    } else {\n      // single output dot, vertically centered in the box\n      out_pts = [{\n        name: null, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + h / 2,\n      }];\n    }\n\n    return { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_box\n  function draw_box(ctx, box, selected) {\n    const x = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const y = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const w = BOX_W;\n    const h = box_height(box);\n    const kind  = box.kind || 'call';\n    const color = KIND_COLOR[kind] || '#888';\n\n    // shadow when selected\n    if (selected) {\n      ctx.shadowColor = color;\n      ctx.shadowBlur  = 12;\n    }\n\n    // body\n    ctx.fillStyle   = '#1e2130';\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? color : '#3a3f55';\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2 : 1;\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, h, 6);\n    ctx.fill();\n    ctx.stroke();\n\n    ctx.shadowBlur = 0;\n\n    // header bar\n    ctx.fillStyle = color + '33';\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, BOX_HEADER, [6, 6, 0, 0]);\n    ctx.fill();\n\n    // label\n    ctx.fillStyle  = '#e8eaf6';\n    ctx.font       = 'bold 12px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n    ctx.fillText(box.label || box.id, x + 10, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // kind badge (top right)\n    ctx.fillStyle  = color;\n    ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n    ctx.fillText(kind.toUpperCase(), x + w - 8, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // port dots and labels\n    const { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts } = port_positions(box);\n\n    ctx.font      = '10px monospace';\n    ctx.fillStyle = '#9ea3c0';\n\n    in_pts.forEach(p => {\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = '#2d3250';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = '#6c72a0';\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      ctx.fillStyle  = '#9ea3c0';\n      ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n      ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n      ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x + PORT_R + 4, p.y);\n    });\n\n    out_pts.forEach(p => {\n      // comparator branches use distinct colors; single output uses kind color\n      const dot_color = p.name ? (BRANCH_COLOR[p.name] || color) : color;\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = dot_color + '44';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = dot_color;\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      // label branch name ('lt'/'eq'/'gt') to the left of the dot; nothing for single wire\n      if (p.name) {\n        ctx.fillStyle  = dot_color;\n        ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n        ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n        ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n        ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x - PORT_R - 4, p.y);\n      }\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_id) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      draw_box(ctx, boxes[id], id === selected_id);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_port\n  // Returns {box_id, port_name, side, x, y} for the port under world point (wx,wy), or null.\n  // For output dots: port_name is null (single wire) or 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' (comparator).\n  function hit_test_port(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(boxes[id]);\n      for (const p of [...inputs, ...outputs]) {\n        const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n        if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= (PORT_R + 4) * (PORT_R + 4)) {\n          return { box_id: id, port_name: p.name, side: p.side, x: p.x, y: p.y };\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_box\n  // Returns box id if (wx,wy) is inside a box body, or null.\n  function hit_test_box(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const b = boxes[id];\n      const x = b.ui?.x ?? 0, y = b.ui?.y ?? 0;\n      if (wx >= x && wx <= x + BOX_W && wy >= y && wy <= y + box_height(b)) return id;\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_port_world_pos\n  function get_port_world_pos(box_id, port_name, side) {\n    const box = boxes[box_id];\n    if (!box) return null;\n    const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(box);\n    const list = side === 'input' ? inputs : outputs;\n    const p = list.find(p => p.name === port_name);\n    return p ? { x: p.x, y: p.y } : null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return {\n    boxes, BOX_W, BOX_HEADER, PORT_R,\n    box_height, port_positions,\n    draw_all, draw_box, hit_test_port, hit_test_box, get_port_world_pos,\n  };\n})();\n",

    "originalFile":"// Box rendering, layout, and hit testing.\n// Each box knows its world-space position; the camera transform is applied by the canvas.\n\nconst Boxes = (() => {\n  const BOX_W         = 180;\n  const BOX_HEADER    = 36;\n  const PORT_ROW_H    = 22;\n  const PORT_R        = 6;   // port dot radius in world units\n  const MIN_BOX_H     = 80;\n\n  const KIND_COLOR = { call: '#4a9eff', branch: '#ff8c42', data: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  // boxes: { [id]: box_data }\n  let boxes = {};\n\n  // {{{ box_height\n  function box_height(box) {\n    const n = Math.max(\n      (box.inputs || []).length,\n      (box.kind === 'branch' ? (box.ports || []).length : (box.outputs || []).length)\n    );\n    return Math.max(MIN_BOX_H, BOX_HEADER + n * PORT_ROW_H + 8);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ port_positions\n  // Returns world-space {x,y} for each port dot on a box.\n  function port_positions(box) {\n    const bx = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const by = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const h  = box_height(box);\n    const inputs  = box.inputs  || [];\n    const outputs = box.kind === 'branch' ? (box.ports || []) : (box.outputs || []);\n\n    const in_pts  = inputs.map((p, i) => ({\n      name: p.name, side: 'input',\n      x: bx,\n      y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n    }));\n    const out_pts = outputs.map((p, i) => ({\n      name: p.name, side: 'output',\n      x: bx + BOX_W,\n      y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n    }));\n    return { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_box\n  function draw_box(ctx, box, selected) {\n    const x = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const y = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const w = BOX_W;\n    const h = box_height(box);\n    const kind  = box.kind || 'call';\n    const color = KIND_COLOR[kind] || '#888';\n\n    // shadow when selected\n    if (selected) {\n      ctx.shadowColor = color;\n      ctx.shadowBlur  = 12;\n    }\n\n    // body\n    ctx.fillStyle   = '#1e2130';\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? color : '#3a3f55';\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2 : 1;\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, h, 6);\n    ctx.fill();\n    ctx.stroke();\n\n    ctx.shadowBlur = 0;\n\n    // header bar\n    ctx.fillStyle = color + '33';\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, BOX_HEADER, [6, 6, 0, 0]);\n    ctx.fill();\n\n    // label\n    ctx.fillStyle  = '#e8eaf6';\n    ctx.font       = 'bold 12px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n    ctx.fillText(box.label || box.id, x + 10, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // kind badge (top right)\n    ctx.fillStyle  = color;\n    ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n    ctx.fillText(kind.toUpperCase(), x + w - 8, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // port dots and labels\n    const { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts } = port_positions(box);\n\n    ctx.font      = '10px monospace';\n    ctx.fillStyle = '#9ea3c0';\n\n    in_pts.forEach((p, i) => {\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = '#2d3250';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = '#6c72a0';\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      ctx.fillStyle  = '#9ea3c0';\n      ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n      ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n      ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x + PORT_R + 4, p.y);\n    });\n\n    // branch ports use palette colors\n    const port_palette = ['#ff8c42','#4a9eff','#4caf7d','#e91e63','#9c27b0','#00bcd4'];\n    out_pts.forEach((p, i) => {\n      const dot_color = (box.kind === 'branch') ? port_palette[i % port_palette.length] : color;\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = dot_color + '44';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = dot_color;\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      ctx.fillStyle  = '#9ea3c0';\n      ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n      ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n      ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x - PORT_R - 4, p.y);\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_id) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      draw_box(ctx, boxes[id], id === selected_id);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_port\n  // Returns {box_id, port_name, side, x, y} for the port under world point (wx,wy), or null.\n  function hit_test_port(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(boxes[id]);\n      for (const p of [...inputs, ...outputs]) {\n        const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n        if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= (PORT_R + 4) * (PORT_R + 4)) {\n          return { box_id: id, port_name: p.name, side: p.side, x: p.x, y: p.y };\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_box\n  // Returns box id if (wx,wy) is inside a box body, or null.\n  function hit_test_box(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const b = boxes[id];\n      const x = b.ui?.x ?? 0, y = b.ui?.y ?? 0;\n      if (wx >= x && wx <= x + BOX_W && wy >= y && wy <= y + box_height(b)) return id;\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_port_world_pos\n  function get_port_world_pos(box_id, port_name, side) {\n    const box = boxes[box_id];\n    if (!box) return null;\n    const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(box);\n    const list = side === 'input' ? inputs : outputs;\n    const p = list.find(p => p.name === port_name);\n    return p ? { x: p.x, y: p.y } : null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return {\n    boxes, BOX_W, BOX_HEADER, PORT_R,\n    box_height, port_positions,\n    draw_all, draw_box, hit_test_port, hit_test_box, get_port_world_pos,\n  };\n})();\n",

          "content":"// Wire rendering, hit testing, and connection management.\n// Wires are derived from box connection data — no separate wire store.\n\nconst Wires = (() => {\n  const BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET = 80;\n  const HIT_SAMPLES        = 20;\n  const HIT_THRESHOLD_PX   = 8;\n\n  // Colors for comparator branch wires; plain wire uses default\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  let _selected_wire = null;  // { from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input }\n\n  // {{{ selected_wire\n  function selected_wire() { return _selected_wire; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ bezier_point\n  function bezier_point(t, x0, y0, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1) {\n    const mt = 1 - t;\n    return {\n      x: mt*mt*mt*x0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cx0 + 3*mt*t*t*cx1 + t*t*t*x1,\n      y: mt*mt*mt*y0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cy0 + 3*mt*t*t*cy1 + t*t*t*y1,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_bezier\n  function draw_bezier(ctx, x0, y0, x1, y1, color, selected) {\n    const cx0 = x0 + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy0 = y0;\n    const cx1 = x1 - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy1 = y1;\n\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.moveTo(x0, y0);\n    ctx.bezierCurveTo(cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1);\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? '#ffffff' : color;\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2.5 : 1.5;\n    ctx.setLineDash([]);\n    ctx.stroke();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_wire\n  // Returns the connection record if cursor (wx,wy) is within HIT_THRESHOLD pixels\n  // of any wire, or null. Operates in world space; threshold is adjusted for zoom.\n  function hit_test_wire(wx, wy, zoom) {\n    const threshold = HIT_THRESHOLD_PX / zoom;\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        const cx0 = src.x + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy0 = src.y;\n        const cx1 = dst.x - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy1 = dst.y;\n\n        for (let i = 0; i <= HIT_SAMPLES; i++) {\n          const t = i / HIT_SAMPLES;\n          const p = bezier_point(t, src.x, src.y, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, dst.x, dst.y);\n          const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n          if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= threshold*threshold) return c;\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_box_id) {\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        // comparator branches get distinct colors; plain wire uses dim default\n        const color = c.from_branch ? (BRANCH_COLOR[c.from_branch] || '#4a6080') : '#4a6080';\n\n        const is_selected = _selected_wire &&\n          _selected_wire.from_box    === c.from_box &&\n          _selected_wire.from_branch === c.from_branch &&\n          _selected_wire.to_box      === c.to_box &&\n          _selected_wire.to_input    === c.to_input;\n\n        draw_bezier(ctx, src.x, src.y, dst.x, dst.y, color, is_selected);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // Handle wire selection via click\n  Canvas.el.addEventListener('click', e => {\n    if (e.button !== 0) return;\n    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);\n\n    // only try wire hit if no box was hit\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_box(w.x, w.y)) { _selected_wire = null; return; }\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_port(w.x, w.y)) return;\n\n    const wire = hit_test_wire(w.x, w.y, Canvas.cam.zoom);\n    if (wire) {\n      _selected_wire = wire;\n    } else {\n      _selected_wire = null;\n    }\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  });\n\n  // {{{ create_connection\n  // from_branch: null (no comparator) or 'lt'/'eq'/'gt'.\n  // Fetch-before-PUT: read both boxes, add the connection record, write both.\n  async function create_connection(from_box_id, from_branch, to_box_id, to_input) {\n    try {\n      const [src_box, dst_box] = await Promise.all([\n        API.get_box(from_box_id),\n        API.get_box(to_box_id),\n      ]);\n\n      const conn = {\n        from_box:    from_box_id,\n        from_branch: from_branch ?? null,\n        to_box:      to_box_id,\n        to_input:    to_input,\n      };\n\n      src_box.connections = src_box.connections || [];\n      dst_box.connections = dst_box.connections || [];\n\n      // avoid duplicates\n      const dup = src_box.connections.some(c =>\n        c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n        (c.from_branch ?? null) === conn.from_branch &&\n        c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n        c.to_input    === conn.to_input\n      );\n      if (dup) return;\n\n      src_box.connections.push(conn);\n      dst_box.connections.push(conn);\n\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(from_box_id, src_box),\n        API.put_box(to_box_id,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n\n      // update local cache\n      Boxes.boxes[from_box_id] = src_box;\n      Boxes.boxes[to_box_id]   = dst_box;\n\n      const branch_str = from_branch ? '.' + from_branch : '';\n      status_msg('connected ' + from_box_id + branch_str + ' → ' + to_box_id + '.' + to_input);\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    } catch(e) {\n      status_msg('connect error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ delete_connection\n  async function delete_connection(conn) {\n    try {\n      const [src_box, dst_box] = await Promise.all([\n        API.get_box(conn.from_box),\n        API.get_box(conn.to_box),\n      ]);\n\n      const match = c =>\n        c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n        (c.from_branch ?? null) === (conn.from_branch ?? null) &&\n        c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n        c.to_input    === conn.to_input;\n\n      src_box.connections = (src_box.connections || []).filter(c => !match(c));\n      dst_box.connections = (dst_box.connections || []).filter(c => !match(c));\n\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(conn.from_box, src_box),\n        API.put_box(conn.to_box,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n\n      Boxes.boxes[conn.from_box] = src_box;\n      Boxes.boxes[conn.to_box]   = dst_box;\n\n      _selected_wire = null;\n      status_msg('deleted connection');\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    } catch(e) {\n      status_msg('delete wire error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { draw_all, draw_bezier, hit_test_wire, create_connection,\n           delete_connection, selected_wire };\n})();\n",

    "content":"// Wire rendering, hit testing, and connection management.\n// Wires are derived from box connection data — no separate wire store.\n\nconst Wires = (() => {\n  const BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET = 80;\n  const HIT_SAMPLES        = 20;\n  const HIT_THRESHOLD_PX   = 8;\n\n  // Colors for comparator branch wires; plain wire uses default\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  let _selected_wire = null;  // { from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input }\n\n  // {{{ selected_wire\n  function selected_wire() { return _selected_wire; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ bezier_point\n  function bezier_point(t, x0, y0, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1) {\n    const mt = 1 - t;\n    return {\n      x: mt*mt*mt*x0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cx0 + 3*mt*t*t*cx1 + t*t*t*x1,\n      y: mt*mt*mt*y0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cy0 + 3*mt*t*t*cy1 + t*t*t*y1,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_bezier\n  function draw_bezier(ctx, x0, y0, x1, y1, color, selected) {\n    const cx0 = x0 + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy0 = y0;\n    const cx1 = x1 - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy1 = y1;\n\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.moveTo(x0, y0);\n    ctx.bezierCurveTo(cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1);\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? '#ffffff' : color;\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2.5 : 1.5;\n    ctx.setLineDash([]);\n    ctx.stroke();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_wire\n  // Returns the connection record if cursor (wx,wy) is within HIT_THRESHOLD pixels\n  // of any wire, or null. Operates in world space; threshold is adjusted for zoom.\n  function hit_test_wire(wx, wy, zoom) {\n    const threshold = HIT_THRESHOLD_PX / zoom;\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        const cx0 = src.x + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy0 = src.y;\n        const cx1 = dst.x - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy1 = dst.y;\n\n        for (let i = 0; i <= HIT_SAMPLES; i++) {\n          const t = i / HIT_SAMPLES;\n          const p = bezier_point(t, src.x, src.y, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, dst.x, dst.y);\n          const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n          if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= threshold*threshold) return c;\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_box_id) {\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        // comparator branches get distinct colors; plain wire uses dim default\n        const color = c.from_branch ? (BRANCH_COLOR[c.from_branch] || '#4a6080') : '#4a6080';\n\n        const is_selected = _selected_wire &&\n          _selected_wire.from_box    === c.from_box &&\n          _selected_wire.from_branch === c.from_branch &&\n          _selected_wire.to_box      === c.to_box &&\n          _selected_wire.to_input    === c.to_input;\n\n        draw_bezier(ctx, src.x, src.y, dst.x, dst.y, color, is_selected);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // Handle wire selection via click\n  Canvas.el.addEventListener('click', e => {\n    if (e.button !== 0) return;\n    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);\n\n    // only try wire hit if no box was hit\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_box(w.x, w.y)) { _selected_wire = null; return; }\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_port(w.x, w.y)) return;\n\n    const wire = hit_test_wire(w.x, w.y, Canvas.cam.zoom);\n    if (wire) {\n      _selected_wire = wire;\n    } else {\n      _selected_wire = null;\n    }\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  });\n\n  // {{{ create_connection\n  // from_branch: null (no comparator) or 'lt'/'eq'/'gt'.\n  // Fetch-before-PUT: read both boxes, add the connection record, write both.\n  async function create_connection(from_box_id, from_branch, to_box_id, to_input) {\n    try {\n      const [src_box, dst_box] = await Promise.all([\n        API.get_box(from_box_id),\n        API.get_box(to_box_id),\n      ]);\n\n      const conn = {\n        from_box:    from_box_id,\n        from_branch: from_branch ?? null,\n        to_box:      to_box_id,\n        to_input:    to_input,\n      };\n\n      src_box.connections = src_box.connections || [];\n      dst_box.connections = dst_box.connections || [];\n\n      // avoid duplicates\n      const dup = src_box.connections.some(c =>\n        c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n        (c.from_branch ?? null) === conn.from_branch &&\n        c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n        c.to_input    === conn.to_input\n      );\n      if (dup) return;\n\n      src_box.connections.push(conn);\n      dst_box.connections.push(conn);\n\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(from_box_id, src_box),\n        API.put_box(to_box_id,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n\n      // update local cache\n      Boxes.boxes[from_box_id] = src_box;\n      Boxes.boxes[to_box_id]   = dst_box;\n\n      const branch_str = from_branch ? '.' + from_branch : '';\n      status_msg('connected ' + from_box_id + branch_str + ' → ' + to_box_id + '.' + to_input);\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    } catch(e) {\n      status_msg('connect error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ delete_connection\n  async function delete_connection(conn) {\n    try {\n      const [src_box, dst_box] = await Promise.all([\n        API.get_box(conn.from_box),\n        API.get_box(conn.to_box),\n      ]);\n\n      const match = c =>\n        c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n        (c.from_branch ?? null) === (conn.from_branch ?? null) &&\n        c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n        c.to_input    === conn.to_input;\n\n      src_box.connections = (src_box.connections || []).filter(c => !match(c));\n      dst_box.connections = (dst_box.connections || []).filter(c => !match(c));\n\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(conn.from_box, src_box),\n        API.put_box(conn.to_box,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n\n      Boxes.boxes[conn.from_box] = src_box;\n      Boxes.boxes[conn.to_box]   = dst_box;\n\n      _selected_wire = null;\n      status_msg('deleted connection');\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    } catch(e) {\n      status_msg('delete wire error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { draw_all, draw_bezier, hit_test_wire, create_connection,\n           delete_connection, selected_wire };\n})();\n",

        "input":{
          "content":"// Inspector sidebar: shows and edits the selected box's fields.\n// Fires PUT to the server on every field change (autosave).\n// For call boxes, ref/fn are set via the file browser; inputs are read-only, derived from parsing.\n\nconst Inspector = (() => {\n  const panel  = document.getElementById('inspector');\n  const title  = document.getElementById('inspector-title');\n  const fields = document.getElementById('inspector-fields');\n\n  let current_box  = null;\n  let on_change_cb = null;\n  let on_delete_cb = null;\n\n  // {{{ hide\n  function hide() {\n    panel.classList.add('hidden');\n    current_box  = null;\n    on_delete_cb = null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ save\n  async function save() {\n    if (!current_box) return;\n    try {\n      await API.put_box(current_box.id, current_box);\n      if (on_change_cb) on_change_cb(current_box);\n    } catch(e) {\n      console.error('autosave failed:', e.message);\n      status_msg('save error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_row\n  function mk_row(label_text, input_el) {\n    const row = document.createElement('div');\n    row.className = 'field-row';\n    const lbl = document.createElement('label');\n    lbl.textContent = label_text;\n    row.appendChild(lbl);\n    row.appendChild(input_el);\n    return row;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_text_input\n  function mk_text_input(value, on_input) {\n    const inp = document.createElement('input');\n    inp.type  = 'text';\n    inp.value = value || '';\n    inp.addEventListener('input', () => { on_input(inp.value); save(); });\n    return inp;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_readonly\n  function mk_readonly(value) {\n    const el = document.createElement('div');\n    el.className   = 'field-readonly';\n    el.textContent = value || '—';\n    return el;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_port_display\n  // Renders input ports as read-only name labels with an optional literal value field.\n  // Names are derived from source parsing and are not editable here.\n  function mk_port_display(ports) {\n    const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    wrap.className = 'port-display';\n    if (!ports || ports.length === 0) {\n      const empty = document.createElement('span');\n      empty.className   = 'port-display-empty';\n      empty.textContent = '(none)';\n      wrap.appendChild(empty);\n    } else {\n      ports.forEach((p, i) => {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className = 'port-display-row';\n\n        // name is read-only — derived from function signature via file browser\n        const name_el = document.createElement('span');\n        name_el.className   = 'port-name-inp';\n        name_el.textContent = p.name || '';\n        name_el.style.color = '#9ea3c0';\n        row.appendChild(name_el);\n\n        if (p.type && p.type !== 'any') {\n          const type_el = document.createElement('span');\n          type_el.className   = 'port-type';\n          type_el.textContent = ':' + p.type;\n          row.appendChild(type_el);\n        }\n\n        // literal value input — empty means \"no literal\" (wire will supply the value)\n        const val_inp = document.createElement('input');\n        val_inp.type        = 'text';\n        val_inp.value       = p.value !== undefined ? String(p.value) : '';\n        val_inp.placeholder = 'value…';\n        val_inp.className   = 'port-val-inp';\n        val_inp.addEventListener('input', () => {\n          ports[i].value = val_inp.value === '' ? undefined : val_inp.value;\n          save();\n        });\n        row.appendChild(val_inp);\n\n        wrap.appendChild(row);\n      });\n    }\n    return wrap;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ open_browser\n  // Replaces inspector content with the file browser.\n  // On function select: sets ref/fn/inputs from parsed signature (no outputs — single wire).\n  function open_browser() {\n    title.textContent = 'browse src/';\n    fields.innerHTML  = '';\n    FileBrowser.render(fields, (filename, fn) => {\n      current_box.ref    = filename;\n      current_box.fn     = fn.name;\n      current_box.inputs = fn.inputs.map(n => ({ name: n, type: 'any' }));\n      // outputs are not set — all boxes have exactly one output wire\n      save().then(() => show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb));\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ show\n  function show(box, on_changed, on_delete) {\n    current_box  = box;\n    on_change_cb = on_changed;\n    on_delete_cb = on_delete || null;\n    panel.classList.remove('hidden');\n    title.textContent = box.id;\n    fields.innerHTML  = '';\n\n    // delete button — always visible at the top of the inspector\n    if (on_delete_cb) {\n      const del_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      del_btn.textContent = 'delete box';\n      del_btn.className   = 'delete-box-btn';\n      del_btn.onclick     = () => on_delete_cb();\n      fields.appendChild(del_btn);\n    }\n\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('label',\n      mk_text_input(box.label, v => { current_box.label = v; })));\n\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('kind', (() => {\n      const sel = document.createElement('select');\n      ['call', 'data'].forEach(k => {\n        const opt = document.createElement('option');\n        opt.value = k; opt.textContent = k;\n        if (k === box.kind) opt.selected = true;\n        sel.appendChild(opt);\n      });\n      sel.addEventListener('change', () => {\n        current_box.kind = sel.value;\n        show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n        save();\n      });\n      return sel;\n    })()));\n\n    // ref: editable text input + browse button to populate via file browser\n    const ref_wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    ref_wrap.style.cssText = 'display:flex;gap:4px;align-items:center;';\n    const ref_inp = document.createElement('input');\n    ref_inp.type  = 'text';\n    ref_inp.value = box.ref || '';\n    ref_inp.style.flex = '1';\n    ref_inp.style.minWidth = '0';\n    ref_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { current_box.ref = ref_inp.value; save(); });\n    const browse_btn = document.createElement('button');\n    browse_btn.className   = 'toolbar-btn';\n    browse_btn.textContent = 'browse';\n    browse_btn.style.whiteSpace = 'nowrap';\n    browse_btn.onclick = open_browser;\n    ref_wrap.appendChild(ref_inp);\n    ref_wrap.appendChild(browse_btn);\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('ref', ref_wrap));\n\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('fn', mk_readonly(box.fn)));\n\n    // inputs: read-only names from parsing, editable literal values\n    const in_sec = document.createElement('div');\n    in_sec.className   = 'section-label';\n    in_sec.textContent = 'inputs';\n    fields.appendChild(in_sec);\n    fields.appendChild(mk_port_display(box.inputs));\n\n    // output: single wire; optional comparator splits into lt/eq/gt\n    const out_sec = document.createElement('div');\n    out_sec.className   = 'section-label';\n    out_sec.textContent = 'output';\n    fields.appendChild(out_sec);\n\n    const cmp_row = document.createElement('div');\n    cmp_row.style.cssText = 'display:flex;gap:6px;align-items:center;margin-bottom:6px;';\n\n    const has_cmp = box.comparand !== undefined && box.comparand !== '';\n    const cmp_btn = document.createElement('button');\n    cmp_btn.className   = 'toolbar-btn';\n    cmp_btn.textContent = has_cmp ? 'comparing ×' : 'compare';\n    cmp_btn.onclick = () => {\n      if (current_box.comparand !== undefined && current_box.comparand !== '') {\n        delete current_box.comparand;\n      } else {\n        current_box.comparand = '0';\n      }\n      save().then(() => show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb));\n    };\n    cmp_row.appendChild(cmp_btn);\n\n    if (has_cmp) {\n      const cmp_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      cmp_inp.type        = 'text';\n      cmp_inp.value       = box.comparand || '';\n      cmp_inp.placeholder = 'number';\n      cmp_inp.style.cssText = 'flex:1;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n      cmp_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { current_box.comparand = cmp_inp.value; save(); });\n      cmp_row.appendChild(cmp_inp);\n    }\n\n    fields.appendChild(cmp_row);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { show, hide };\n})();\n",

Closes after each response (HTTP/1.0 style).\n-- Started with: luajit soramech-server.lua <maps-root> [port]\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\npackage.path  = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\"\n             .. DIR .. \"/libs/luasocket/share/lua/5.1/?.lua;\"\n             .. DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\"\n             .. package.path\npackage.cpath = DIR .. \"/libs/luasocket/lib/lua/5.1/?.so;\"\n             .. package.cpath\n\nlocal socket = require(\"socket\")\nlocal json   = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal schema = require(\"001-schema\")\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ read_file\nlocal function read_file(path)\n    local f, err = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then return nil, err end\n    local data = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    return data\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ write_file_atomic\nlocal function write_file_atomic(path, data)\n    local tmp = path .. \".tmp\"\n    local f, err = io.open(tmp, \"w\")\n    if not f then return false, err end\n    f:write(data)\n    f:close()\n    local ok, rerr = os.rename(tmp, path)\n    if not ok then return false, rerr end\n    return true\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ parse_json_file\nlocal function parse_json_file(path)\n    local raw, err = read_file(path)\n    if not raw then return nil, err end\n    local obj, _, jerr = json.decode(raw)\n    if not obj then return nil, \"JSON error: \" .. tostring(jerr) end\n    return obj\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ list_dir_json\nlocal function list_dir_json(dir)\n    local handle = io.popen(\"ls \" .. dir .. \"/*.json 2>/dev/null\")\n    if not handle then return {} end\n    local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n    handle:close()\n    local files = {}\n    for path in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n        files[#files + 1] = path\n    end\n    return files\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ list_subdirs\nlocal function list_subdirs(dir)\n    local handle = io.popen(\"ls -d \" .. dir .. \"/*/ 2>/dev/null\")\n    if not handle then return {} end\n    local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n    handle:close()\n    local names = {}\n    for path in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n        local name = path:match(\"/([^/]+)/$\")\n        if name then names[#names + 1] = name end\n    end\n    return names\nend",

{

    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"The server calls `schema.validate_box` which now uses the new `from_branch` schema — that's consistent.\n\nEverything is wired up. Here's a summary of what changed:\n\n- **Schema** (`001-schema.lua`): removed `branch` kind, `valid_ops`, all branch/predicate validators. Connections now use `from_branch` (nil or \"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\"). Call boxes have no `outputs`, optional `comparand` string.\n\n- **Loader** (`003-loader.lua`): removed branch-box cycle exemption (all cycles are errors now). Reciprocal check uses `from_branch`. Removed branch-else validation.\n\n- **Executor** (`004-executor.lua`): removed `eval_predicate`, `llm_route_call`, retry machinery. `run_task` returns a single value (first array element). `fire_connections` routes that value either through a comparator (number check → lt/eq/gt) or straight through to all nil-branched connections.\n\n- **Boxes** (`002-boxes.js`): one output dot centered vertically; if `box.comparand` set, three dots (lt/eq/gt) with distinct colors and labels. Removed branch kind color.\n\n- **Inspector** (`004-inspector.js`): removed `branch`/`llm-route` kinds and their entire UI sections. Input port names are read-only labels. Output section shows a \"compare\" toggle; when active, shows a number input for the comparand.\n\n- **Wires** (`006-wires.js`): all connection records use `from_branch`. Wire color comes from branch name. Dup check and deletion match on `from_branch`.\n\n- **App** (`005-app.js`): new boxes no longer get `outputs: []`."
      }],

## [1729]

```json
{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T02:38:02.407Z",
  "slug":"reactive-toasting-squid",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"**Multiple wires to the same input:** the store is a flat key-value table keyed by `\"box_id.port_name\"`. If two upstream boxes both fire connections to the same input (e.g., both write to `C.x`), it's last-write-wins — whichever upstream box runs last in the queue overwrites the entry. The target box only executes once (the `visited` guard), so it receives whichever value happened to arrive last. There's no merging or error — it silently drops one. Wiring two outputs to the same input is probably a mistake and ideally would be caught at load time, but currently isn't.\n\n**Wire deletion** is already implemented — click a wire to select it (it turns white), then press Delete or Backspace. The mechanism works but it's invisible. Let me make it obvious by showing a status hint when a wire is selected:"
      }],
    "id":"msg_01H5XuiiHBcKrrqtFHYRqzWP",

    "originalFile":"// Wire rendering, hit testing, and connection management.\n// Wires are derived from box connection data — no separate wire store.\n\nconst Wires = (() => {\n  const BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET = 80;\n  const HIT_SAMPLES        = 20;\n  const HIT_THRESHOLD_PX   = 8;\n\n  // Colors for comparator branch wires; plain wire uses default\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  let _selected_wire = null;  // { from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input }\n\n  // {{{ selected_wire\n  function selected_wire() { return _selected_wire; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ bezier_point\n  function bezier_point(t, x0, y0, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1) {\n    const mt = 1 - t;\n    return {\n      x: mt*mt*mt*x0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cx0 + 3*mt*t*t*cx1 + t*t*t*x1,\n      y: mt*mt*mt*y0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cy0 + 3*mt*t*t*cy1 + t*t*t*y1,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_bezier\n  function draw_bezier(ctx, x0, y0, x1, y1, color, selected) {\n    const cx0 = x0 + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy0 = y0;\n    const cx1 = x1 - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy1 = y1;\n\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.moveTo(x0, y0);\n    ctx.bezierCurveTo(cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1);\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? '#ffffff' : color;\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2.5 : 1.5;\n    ctx.setLineDash([]);\n    ctx.stroke();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_wire\n  // Returns the connection record if cursor (wx,wy) is within HIT_THRESHOLD pixels\n  // of any wire, or null. Operates in world space; threshold is adjusted for zoom.\n  function hit_test_wire(wx, wy, zoom) {\n    const threshold = HIT_THRESHOLD_PX / zoom;\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        const cx0 = src.x + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy0 = src.y;\n        const cx1 = dst.x - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy1 = dst.y;\n\n        for (let i = 0; i <= HIT_SAMPLES; i++) {\n          const t = i / HIT_SAMPLES;\n          const p = bezier_point(t, src.x, src.y, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, dst.x, dst.y);\n          const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n          if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= threshold*threshold) return c;\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_box_id) {\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        // comparator branches get distinct colors; plain wire uses dim default\n        const color = c.from_branch ? (BRANCH_COLOR[c.from_branch] || '#4a6080') : '#4a6080';\n\n        const is_selected = _selected_wire &&\n          _selected_wire.from_box    === c.from_box &&\n          _selected_wire.from_branch === c.from_branch &&\n          _selected_wire.to_box      === c.to_box &&\n          _selected_wire.to_input    === c.to_input;\n\n        draw_bezier(ctx, src.x, src.y, dst.x, dst.y, color, is_selected);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // Handle wire selection via click\n  Canvas.el.addEventListener('click', e => {\n    if (e.button !== 0) return;\n    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);\n\n    // only try wire hit if no box was hit\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_box(w.x, w.y)) { _selected_wire = null; return; }\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_port(w.x, w.y)) return;\n\n    const wire = hit_test_wire(w.x, w.y, Canvas.cam.zoom);\n    if (wire) {\n      _selected_wire = wire;\n    } else {\n      _selected_wire = null;\n    }\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  });\n\n  // {{{ create_connection\n  // from_branch: null (no comparator) or 'lt'/'eq'/'gt'.\n  // Fetch-before-PUT: read both boxes, add the connection record, write both.\n  async function create_connection(from_box_id, from_branch, to_box_id, to_input) {\n    try {\n      const [src_box, dst_box] = await Promise.all([\n        API.get_box(from_box_id),\n        API.get_box(to_box_id),\n      ]);\n\n      const conn = {\n        from_box:    from_box_id,\n        from_branch: from_branch ?? null,\n        to_box:      to_box_id,\n        to_input:    to_input,\n      };\n\n      src_box.connections = src_box.connections || [];\n      dst_box.connections = dst_box.connections || [];\n\n      // avoid duplicates\n      const dup = src_box.connections.some(c =>\n        c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n        (c.from_branch ?? null) === conn.from_branch &&\n        c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n        c.to_input    === conn.to_input\n      );\n      if (dup) return;\n\n      src_box.connections.push(conn);\n      dst_box.connections.push(conn);\n\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(from_box_id, src_box),\n        API.put_box(to_box_id,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n\n      // update local cache\n      Boxes.boxes[from_box_id] = src_box;\n      Boxes.boxes[to_box_id]   = dst_box;\n\n      const branch_str = from_branch ? '.' + from_branch : '';\n      status_msg('connected ' + from_box_id + branch_str + ' → ' + to_box_id + '.' + to_input);\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    } catch(e) {\n      status_msg('connect error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ delete_connection\n  async function delete_connection(conn) {\n    try {\n      const [src_box, dst_box] = await Promise.all([\n        API.get_box(conn.from_box),\n        API.get_box(conn.to_box),\n      ]);\n\n      const match = c =>\n        c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n        (c.from_branch ?? null) === (conn.from_branch ?? null) &&\n        c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n        c.to_input    === conn.to_input;\n\n      src_box.connections = (src_box.connections || []).filter(c => !match(c));\n      dst_box.connections = (dst_box.connections || []).filter(c => !match(c));\n\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(conn.from_box, src_box),\n        API.put_box(conn.to_box,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n\n      Boxes.boxes[conn.from_box] = src_box;\n      Boxes.boxes[conn.to_box]   = dst_box;\n\n      _selected_wire = null;\n      status_msg('deleted connection');\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    } catch(e) {\n      status_msg('delete wire error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { draw_all, draw_bezier, hit_test_wire, create_connection,\n           delete_connection, selected_wire };\n})();\n",

{
  "isSidechain":false,
  "promptId":"3609d721-e228-491a-b635-b553d01d15d3",

  "slug":"reactive-toasting-squid",
  "gitBranch":"HEAD",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "message":{
    "role":"user",
    "content":"I'm trying to delete a box and it says this: \"delete error: box 'box-mow661fm' is referenced by: greet, write-result\"\n\nwe should be able to delete boxes that have wires going to them. Also, we should not ask for confirmation - we should just do it. It's fine.\n\nCan we add two buttons to the left side, one for adding a new box and one for deleting wires? By selecting those buttons, we should enter a new mode - one for adding a box and one for deleting a wire. When the mouse button is clicked, it drops the new box at the mouse cursor location. This should replace the double-click functionality. When the delete wire tool is selected, while the mouse is held down it should erase any wires that the mouse cursor passes over. Once the mouse button is lifted it should bring us back to the normal mode. Can you create an issue file for that one?\n\nOkay so in the future when we implement the thread-pool system, a box receiving input (and receiving ALL of it's inputs, unless a field is marked optional, so upon receiving all required inputs) the box should create a new task in the thread pool architecture, and consume the inputs that have been written. If a new input value is sent over a wire, it should \"queue\" up and not overwrite the previous one - so there might be a case where input A has like, 10 values waiting for input B, and every time a value is passed to the input B port it creates a new task with the first input A value and the (new) input B value. We'll need to implement the thread pool library for that though. For now, can you write an issue file that designs a system that works similarly, just... synchronously? Maybe even using coroutines? I think lua supports them by default...\n\nAlso, what's the status on the coupling of the LLM box types and the server, editor, executor, etc? The goal was to completely decouple them, and treat all the box types as library functions."
  },
  "sessionId":"2029ad16-5678-4b15-931f-3f52d826597a",
  "uuid":"0ed44e4f-c370-4885-93c2-4ade76ea9622",

 = { x: 0, y: 0 };\n  let drawing_wire  = null;  // { from_box, from_port, cur_x, cur_y }\n  let hover_port    = null;\n  let status_el     = document.getElementById('status');\n\n  // tool_mode: // update canvas cursor and status hint\n    if (mode === 'add-box') {\n      Canvas.el.style.cursor = 'copy';\n      status_msg('click anywhere to place a box');\n    } else if (mode === const all = await Promise.all(fetches);\n      // mutate the existing object so the draw_all closure sees the new boxes\n      Object.keys(Boxes.boxes).forEach(k => delete Boxes.boxes[k]);\n      all.forEach(b => { Boxes.boxes[b.id] = b; });\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n      status_msg('loaded ' + ids.length + ' boxes');\n    } catch(e) {\n      status_msg('load error: ' + e.message, Boxes.draw_all(ctx, selected_id);\n\n      // draw in-progress wire\n      if (drawing_wire) {\n        const src = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(drawing_wire.from_box, drawing_wire.from_port, 'output');\n        if (src) {\n          Wires.draw_bezier(ctx, src.x, src.y, drawing_wire.cur_x, drawing_wire.cur_y,\n            '#6c72a0', false);\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    requestAnimationFrame(render);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // Mouse interaction\n  Canvas.el.addEventListener('mousedown', e => {\n    if (e.button !== 0) return;\n    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);\n\n    if (tool_mode === 'add-box') {\n      new_box_at(w.x, w.y);\n      set_tool_mode('select');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    if (tool_mode ===  const box_id = Boxes.hit_test_box(w.x, w.y);\n    if (box_id) {\n      selected_id = box_id;\n      drag_box_id = box_id;\n      const b = Boxes.boxes[box_id];\n      drag_offset = { x: w.x -    Inspector.hide();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  });\n\n  Canvas.el.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {\n    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);\n\n    if {\n          erase_seen.add(sig);\n          // remove from local cache immediately for instant visual feedback\n          [wire.from_box, wire.to_box].forEach(id => {\n            if (drawing_wire) {\n      drawing_wire.cur_x = w.x;\n      drawing_wire.cur_y = w.y;\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n      return;\n    }\n\n    if (drag_box_id) {\n      const b = Boxes.boxes[drag_box_id];\n      if (b) {\n        b.ui = b.ui || {};\n        b.ui.x = Math.round(w.x - drag_offset.x);\n        b.ui.y = Math.round(w.y - drag_offset.y);\n        Canvas.mark_dirty();\n      }\n    }\n  });\n\n  Canvas.el.addEventListener('mouseup', async e => {\n    if (e.button !== 0) return;\n\n    if (erasing) {\n      erasing    = false;\n      erase_seen       if (box.connections.length !== before) {\n          await API.put_box(bid, box);\n          Boxes.boxes[bid] = box;\n        }\n      }));\n      await API.delete_box(id);\n      delete if (document.activeElement && document.activeElement.tagName === 'INPUT') return;\n\n    const sel_wire = Wires.selected_wire();\n    if (sel_wire) {\n      await Wires.delete_connection(sel_wire);\n         "input":{
          "content":"# 212 — Editor interaction modes\n\n## Status\n\ncomplete\n\n## Current behavior\n\nCreating a box requires a double-click on the canvas. There is no dedicated\nwire-erase tool; wires must be clicked individually to select them and then\ndeleted with the keyboard. Deleting a box that has incoming connections fails\nwith a server 409 error because the server checks for references before allowing\nthe delete.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nTwo tool-mode buttons appear in the top toolbar:\n\n**+ box**: clicking the button enters add-box mode (button highlights). The\nnext click on the canvas places a new box at the cursor position and returns\nto select mode automatically.\n\n**✕ wire**: clicking the button enters erase-wire mode (button highlights).\nWhile the mouse button is held down and the cursor is dragged across the canvas,\nany wire the cursor passes over is immediately erased. Releasing the mouse button\nexits erase-wire mode and returns to select mode.\n\nDouble-click to create a box is removed; the + box tool is the only creation\npath.\n\nBox deletion is unconditional: before calling the server DELETE, the client\nstrips all connection records referencing the box from every other box (PUT each\naffected box), then issues the DELETE. The server's 409 reference guard is no\nlonger triggered. No confirmation dialog is shown.\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n`set_tool_mode(mode)` exposed from the App closure manages the active button\nclass and canvas cursor ('copy' for add-box, 'cell' for erase-wire).\n\nErase-wire tracks a Set of already-queued wire signatures per drag to avoid\ndouble-deletes. Connections are removed from the local Boxes cache immediately\n(for instant visual feedback) and then deleted from the server asynchronously.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `005-app.js` — add `tool_mode`, `set_tool_mode`, `wire_sig` helpers.\n   Update mousedown/mousemove/mouseup handlers for new modes.\n   Rewrite `delete_box` to strip references before deleting.\n   Remove dblclick handler.\n2. `index.html` — add `#tool-add-box` and `#tool-erase-wire` buttons to toolbar.\n   Add `.toolbar-btn.active` CSS.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/005-app.js — App closure, event handlers\n- assets/index.html — toolbar HTML and CSS\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/212-editor-interaction-modes.md"
        }
      }],

    "content":"# 212 — Editor interaction modes\n\n## Status\n\ncomplete\n\n## Current behavior\n\nCreating a box requires a double-click on the canvas. There is no dedicated\nwire-erase tool; wires must be clicked individually to select them and then\ndeleted with the keyboard. Deleting a box that has incoming connections fails\nwith a server 409 error because the server checks for references before allowing\nthe delete.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nTwo tool-mode buttons appear in the top toolbar:\n\n**+ box**: clicking the button enters add-box mode (button highlights). The\nnext click on the canvas places a new box at the cursor position and returns\nto select mode automatically.\n\n**✕ wire**: clicking the button enters erase-wire mode (button highlights).\nWhile the mouse button is held down and the cursor is dragged across the canvas,\nany wire the cursor passes over is immediately erased. Releasing the mouse button\nexits erase-wire mode and returns to select mode.\n\nDouble-click to create a box is removed; the + box tool is the only creation\npath.\n\nBox deletion is unconditional: before calling the server DELETE, the client\nstrips all connection records referencing the box from every other box (PUT each\naffected box), then issues the DELETE. The server's 409 reference guard is no\nlonger triggered. No confirmation dialog is shown.\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n`set_tool_mode(mode)` exposed from the App closure manages the active button\nclass and canvas cursor ('copy' for add-box, 'cell' for erase-wire).\n\nErase-wire tracks a Set of already-queued wire signatures per drag to avoid\ndouble-deletes. Connections are removed from the local Boxes cache immediately\n(for instant visual feedback) and then deleted from the server asynchronously.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `005-app.js` — add `tool_mode`, `set_tool_mode`, `wire_sig` helpers.\n   Update mousedown/mousemove/mouseup handlers for new modes.\n   Rewrite `delete_box` to strip references before deleting.\n   Remove dblclick handler.\n2. `index.html` — add `#tool-add-box` and `#tool-erase-wire` buttons to toolbar.\n   Add `.toolbar-btn.active` CSS.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/005-app.js — App closure, event handlers\n- assets/index.html — toolbar HTML and CSS\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/212-editor-interaction-modes.md",
    "structuredPatch":[]
  }
}

          "content":"# 213 — Queued inputs and synchronous task model\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nEach input port in the executor store holds exactly one value. When an upstream\nbox fires a connection, it overwrites whatever was previously in that slot. A box\nonly runs once (the `visited` guard prevents re-execution). This means:\n\n- A box with two upstream feeders only processes the last-arriving value.\n- Fan-in patterns (many outputs converging on one input) silently drop values.\n- There is no way to process a stream of values through a box.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nEach input port has a **queue** (ordered list) of waiting values instead of a\nsingle slot. A box becomes \"ready\" when all of its required input ports have at\nleast one value in their queue. When a box runs, it pops one value from the\nfront of each required input queue, then runs the task with those values. After\nthe task completes, the box is checked again — if all required queues are still\nnon-empty, it runs again immediately, consuming the next set of inputs.\n\nOptional ports (marked with `\"optional\": true` in the input object) do not gate\nreadiness. If a value is present in an optional port's queue when the task runs,\nit is consumed; otherwise the task receives nil for that port.\n\nThis model enables:\n- Fan-in: A collects 10 values, B collects 1. Each new value to B creates one\n  task that consumes one A-value and the new B-value.\n- Pipelines: output of one box feeds into the next, which re-runs for each\n  arriving value.\n- Broadcast: one box fans out to two boxes, both of which process that one value.\n\nThe executor stays **synchronous** in this phase. Coroutines are not required\nfor the synchronous model — the simple approach is: after each box run, re-check\nall boxes (not just directly connected ones) for readiness and enqueue any that\nare ready. Run until the queue is empty or an error occurs.\n\n## Data model changes\n\n**Store**: `store[\"box_id.port_name\"]` changes from a single value to an array\nof values (a queue). All reads pop from the front; all writes push to the back.\n\n**Inputs satisfied**: `inputs_satisfied(box, store)` — a port is satisfied when\n`#store[key] > 0`. Optional ports are always considered satisfied.\n\n**Collect inputs**: `collect_inputs(box, store)` — shifts (pops front) one value\nfrom each port's queue and returns the map of port-name → value.\n\n**Visited guard**: remove the `visited` flag. Instead, enqueue a box whenever its\ninputs become satisfied (even if it has run before). This is safe because\nsatisfaction requires queue entries, and collect_inputs consumes them.\n\n**Literal values**: pre-seeded literal values are still pushed once into the\nqueue at startup. They are consumed on first run. A wire can push additional\nvalues on top of the literal.\n\n## Optional port convention\n\nIn the box file:\n```json\n{ \"name\": \"temperature\", \"type\": \"any\", \"optional\": true, \"value\": \"0.7\" }\n```\n\n`optional: true` means this port does not block readiness. The literal `value`\n(if present) is still pre-seeded into the queue as a default. Wires can push\nadditional values.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. **`src/004-executor.lua`** — change store values to arrays. Update\n   `inputs_satisfied` (check array length, skip optional ports). Update\n   `collect_inputs` (table.remove from front). Remove `visited` table.\n   After each `fire_connections`, re-scan all boxes for satisfaction and\n   enqueue the newly ready ones.\n\n2. **`src/001-schema.lua`** — add optional `\"optional\"` boolean to port objects.\n\n3. **`src/004-executor.lua`** — pre-seeding: push literal values into arrays\n   (`store[key] = { parsed_val }`) instead of assigning directly.\n\n4. **`assets/js/004-inspector.js`** — add an \"optional\" checkbox per input port\n   row. On change, update `port.optional` and save.\n\n## Future: thread pool\n\nWhen the synchronous model is replaced by a thread pool, the queue-per-port\ndesign maps directly: a worker thread pops one value from each input queue,\nruns the task, and pushes outputs to the connected ports' queues. The\nsatisfaction check becomes a condition variable or semaphore per port. The\nsynchronous executor described here is the reference implementation.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- src/004-executor.lua — execute, inputs_satisfied, collect_inputs, fire_connections\n- src/001-schema.lua — port schema, optional field\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — optional port checkbox\n- docs/001-architecture.md — store model, box.inputs schema\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/213-queued-inputs-and-task-model.md"
        }

  "type":"user",
  "parentUuid":"00a89b16-a6e1-4437-ae05-8874a72ac9fc",

  "toolUseResult":{
    "content":"# 213 — Queued inputs and synchronous task model\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nEach input port in the executor store holds exactly one value. When an upstream\nbox fires a connection, it overwrites whatever was previously in that slot. A box\nonly runs once (the `visited` guard prevents re-execution). This means:\n\n- A box with two upstream feeders only processes the last-arriving value.\n- Fan-in patterns (many outputs converging on one input) silently drop values.\n- There is no way to process a stream of values through a box.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nEach input port has a **queue** (ordered list) of waiting values instead of a\nsingle slot. A box becomes \"ready\" when all of its required input ports have at\nleast one value in their queue. When a box runs, it pops one value from the\nfront of each required input queue, then runs the task with those values. After\nthe task completes, the box is checked again — if all required queues are still\nnon-empty, it runs again immediately, consuming the next set of inputs.\n\nOptional ports (marked with `\"optional\": true` in the input object) do not gate\nreadiness. If a value is present in an optional port's queue when the task runs,\nit is consumed; otherwise the task receives nil for that port.\n\nThis model enables:\n- Fan-in: A collects 10 values, B collects 1. Each new value to B creates one\n  task that consumes one A-value and the new B-value.\n- Pipelines: output of one box feeds into the next, which re-runs for each\n  arriving value.\n- Broadcast: one box fans out to two boxes, both of which process that one value.\n\nThe executor stays **synchronous** in this phase. Coroutines are not required\nfor the synchronous model — the simple approach is: after each box run, re-check\nall boxes (not just directly connected ones) for readiness and enqueue any that\nare ready. Run until the queue is empty or an error occurs.\n\n## Data model changes\n\n**Store**: `store[\"box_id.port_name\"]` changes from a single value to an array\nof values (a queue). All reads pop from the front; all writes push to the back.\n\n**Inputs satisfied**: `inputs_satisfied(box, store)` — a port is satisfied when\n`#store[key] > 0`. Optional ports are always considered satisfied.\n\n**Collect inputs**: `collect_inputs(box, store)` — shifts (pops front) one value\nfrom each port's queue and returns the map of port-name → value.\n\n**Visited guard**: remove the `visited` flag. Instead, enqueue a box whenever its\ninputs become satisfied (even if it has run before). This is safe because\nsatisfaction requires queue entries, and collect_inputs consumes them.\n\n**Literal values**: pre-seeded literal values are still pushed once into the\nqueue at startup. They are consumed on first run. A wire can push additional\nvalues on top of the literal.\n\n## Optional port convention\n\nIn the box file:\n```json\n{ \"name\": \"temperature\", \"type\": \"any\", \"optional\": true, \"value\": \"0.7\" }\n```\n\n`optional: true` means this port does not block readiness. The literal `value`\n(if present) is still pre-seeded into the queue as a default. Wires can push\nadditional values.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. **`src/004-executor.lua`** — change store values to arrays. Update\n   `inputs_satisfied` (check array length, skip optional ports). Update\n   `collect_inputs` (table.remove from front). Remove `visited` table.\n   After each `fire_connections`, re-scan all boxes for satisfaction and\n   enqueue the newly ready ones.\n\n2. **`src/001-schema.lua`** — add optional `\"optional\"` boolean to port objects.\n\n3. **`src/004-executor.lua`** — pre-seeding: push literal values into arrays\n   (`store[key] = { parsed_val }`) instead of assigning directly.\n\n4. **`assets/js/004-inspector.js`** — add an \"optional\" checkbox per input port\n   row. On change, update `port.optional` and save.\n\n## Future: thread pool\n\nWhen the synchronous model is replaced by a thread pool, the queue-per-port\ndesign maps directly: a worker thread pops one value from each input queue,\nruns the task, and pushes outputs to the connected ports' queues. The\nsatisfaction check becomes a condition variable or semaphore per port. The\nsynchronous executor described here is the reference implementation.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- src/004-executor.lua — execute, inputs_satisfied, collect_inputs, fire_connections\n- src/001-schema.lua — port schema, optional field\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — optional port checkbox\n- docs/001-architecture.md — store model, box.inputs schema\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "type":"create",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/213-queued-inputs-and-task-model.md",
    "structuredPatch":[]
  }
}

    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"**On the LLM decoupling question:** it's essentially complete. The executor has zero LLM-specific code — `llm_route_call` and `eval_predicate` are gone. The inspector has no LLM box type. Wires have no LLM awareness. The only remaining artifact is `libs/ollama.lua`, which is just a library — it's no different from any other helper a Lua function might `require`. A box that needs an LLM call writes a Lua function that calls `require(\"ollama\")`, selects it via the file browser, and the executor calls it identically to any other box. The coupling is fully severed at the architecture level.\n\n**Summary of what just changed:**\n- **Delete box**: now strips all incoming connection records from other boxes before calling DELETE — no more 409, no confirmation dialog\n- **+ box tool**: click button → cursor becomes `copy` → next canvas click places a box → back to select mode; double-click removed\n- **✕ wire tool**: click button → cursor becomes `cell` → drag across wires to erase them → mouse up returns to select mode\n- **Issues 212 and 213** created"

handle_put_box\nlocal function handle_put_box(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name = req.parts[2]\n    local box_id   = req.parts[4]\n    local path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"boxes\", box_id .. \".json\")\n    if not path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n\n    local box, _, jerr = json.decode(req.body)\n    if not box then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid JSON: \" .. tostring(jerr))\n    end\n\n    local errs = schema.validate_box(box)\n    if #errs > 0 then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"schema error: \" .. table.concat(errs, \"; \"))\n    end\n\n    local ok, werr = write_file_atomic(path, req.body)\n    if not ok then return json_err(client, \"500 Internal Server Error\", tostring(werr)) end\n    json_ok(client, { ok = true })\nend\n-- }}}\n",

    "originalFile":"// Thin fetch wrapper for the soramech-server REST API.\n// All functions are async and throw on non-2xx responses.\n\nconst API = (() => {\n  let base_url = '';\n  let map_name = '';\n\n  // {{{ init\n  function init(url, name) { base_url = url.replace(/\\/$/, ''); map_name = name; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ request\n  async function request(method, path, body) {\n    const opts   "message":{
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"All clean. `req.path` is now the clean path without query string, which is exactly what the static file serving and the logging need. `req.query` is only used by the new `handle_list_dirs` handler.\n\nHere's what changed:\n\n- **Server**: `parse_request` now splits query strings from the path before building `parts` — previous handlers are unaffected since they only use `parts`. New `GET /fs/dirs?path=...` route lists immediate subdirectories of any absolute path on the server filesystem.\n\n- **API**: `list_dirs(path)` added.\n\n- **File browser**: Clicking \"+ library dir\" now opens an in-panel directory navigator instead of a `prompt()`. It starts at `/home`, shows subdirectories as clickable rows, has a `..` row for going up, and a \"✓ use this directory\" button that saves the selection. The back button cancels and returns to the file list."

    "newString":"  // {{{ show_content\n  // Renders arbitrary content into the inspector panel without a box context.\n  // Used by the map picker and any other non-box inspector views.\n  function show_content(title_text, render_fn) {\n    current_box  = null;\n    on_change_cb = null;\n    on_delete_cb = null;\n    panel.classList.remove('hidden');\n    title.innerHTML   = '';\n    title.textContent = title_text;\n    fields.innerHTML  = '';\n    render_fn(fields);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ show\n  function show(box, on_changed, on_delete) {\n    current_box  = box;\n    on_change_cb = on_changed;\n    on_delete_cb = on_delete || null;\n    panel.classList.remove('hidden');\n\n    // title: editable label input + read-only id subtitle\n    title.innerHTML = '';\n    const lbl_inp = document.createElement('input');\n    lbl_inp.type      = 'text';\n    lbl_inp.value     = box.label || '';\n    lbl_inp.className = 'inspector-title-inp';\n    lbl_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { current_box.label = lbl_inp.value; save(); });\n    title.appendChild(lbl_inp);\n    const id_sub = document.createElement('div');\n    id_sub.className   = 'inspector-id-sub';\n    id_sub.textContent = box.id;\n    title.appendChild(id_sub);\n\n    fields.innerHTML = '';\n\n    // delete button — always visible at the top of the inspector\n    if (on_delete_cb) {\n      const del_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      del_btn.textContent = 'delete box';\n      del_btn.className   = 'delete-box-btn';\n      del_btn.onclick     = () => on_delete_cb();\n      fields.appendChild(del_btn);\n    }\n\n    // label is now the editable title — no separate field needed\n\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('kind', (() => {",
    "originalFile":"// Inspector sidebar: shows and edits the selected box's fields.\n// Fires PUT to the server on every field change (autosave).\n// For call boxes, ref/fn are set via the file browser; inputs are read-only, derived from parsing.\n\nconst Inspector = (() => {\n  const panel  = document.getElementById('inspector');\n  const title  = document.getElementById('inspector-title');\n  const fields = document.getElementById('inspector-fields');\n\n  let current_box  = null;\n  let on_change_cb = null;\n  let on_delete_cb = null;\n\n  // {{{ hide\n  function hide() {\n    panel.classList.add('hidden');\n    current_box  = null;\n    on_delete_cb = null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ save\n  async function save() {\n    if (!current_box) return;\n    try {\n      await API.put_box(current_box.id, current_box);\n      if (on_change_cb) on_change_cb(current_box);\n    } catch(e) {\n      console.error('autosave failed:', e.message);\n      status_msg('save error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_row\n  function mk_row(label_text, input_el) {\n    const row = document.createElement('div');\n    row.className = 'field-row';\n    const lbl = document.createElement('label');\n    lbl.textContent = label_text;\n    row.appendChild(lbl);\n    row.appendChild(input_el);\n    return row;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_text_input\n  function mk_text_input(value, on_input) {\n    const inp = document.createElement('input');\n    inp.type  = 'text';\n    inp.value = value || '';\n    inp.addEventListener('input', () => { on_input(inp.value); save(); });\n    return inp;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_readonly\n  function mk_readonly(value) {\n    const el = document.createElement('div');\n    el.className   = 'field-readonly';\n    el.textContent = value || '—';\n    return el;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_port_display\n  // Renders input ports as read-only name labels with an optional literal value field.\n  // Names are derived from source parsing and are not editable here.\n  function mk_port_display(ports) {\n    const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    wrap.className = 'port-display';\n    if (!ports || ports.length === 0) {\n      const empty = document.createElement('span');\n      empty.className   = 'port-display-empty';\n      empty.textContent = '(none)';\n      wrap.appendChild(empty);\n    } else {\n      ports.forEach((p, i) => {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className = 'port-display-row';\n\n        // name is read-only — derived from function signature via file browser\n        const name_el = document.createElement('span');\n        name_el.className   = 'port-name-inp';\n        name_el.textContent = p.name || '';\n        name_el.style.color = '#9ea3c0';\n        row.appendChild(name_el);\n\n        if (p.type && p.type !== 'any') {\n          const type_el = document.createElement('span');\n          type_el.className   = 'port-type';\n          type_el.textContent = ':' + p.type;\n          row.appendChild(type_el);\n        }\n\n        // literal value input — empty means \"no literal\" (wire will supply the value)\n        const val_inp = document.createElement('input');\n        val_inp.type        = 'text';\n        val_inp.value       = p.value !== undefined ? String(p.value) : '';\n        val_inp.placeholder = 'value…';\n        val_inp.className   = 'port-val-inp';\n        val_inp.addEventListener('input', () => {\n          ports[i].value = val_inp.value === '' ? undefined : val_inp.value;\n          save();\n        });\n        row.appendChild(val_inp);\n\n        wrap.appendChild(row);\n      });\n    }\n    return wrap;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ open_browser\n  // Replaces inspector content with the file browser.\n  // On function select: sets ref/fn/inputs from parsed signature (no outputs — single wire).\n  function open_browser() {\n    title.textContent = 'browse src/';\n    fields.innerHTML  = '';\n    FileBrowser.render(fields, (filename, fn) => {\n      current_box.ref    = filename;\n      current_box.fn     = fn.name;\n      current_box.inputs = fn.inputs.map(n => ({ name: n, type: 'any' }));\n      // outputs are not set — all boxes have exactly one output wire\n      save().then(() => show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb));\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ show\n  function show(box, on_changed, on_delete) {\n    current_box  = box;\n    on_change_cb = on_changed;\n    on_delete_cb = on_delete || null;\n    panel.classList.remove('hidden');\n    title.textContent = box.id;\n    fields.innerHTML  = '';\n\n    // delete button — always visible at the top of the inspector\n    if (on_delete_cb) {\n      const del_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      del_btn.textContent = 'delete box';\n      del_btn.className   = 'delete-box-btn';\n      del_btn.onclick     = () => on_delete_cb();\n      fields.appendChild(del_btn);\n    }\n\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('label',\n      mk_text_input(box.label, v => { current_box.label = v; })));\n\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('kind', (() => {\n      const sel = document.createElement('select');\n      ['call', 'data'].forEach(k => {\n        const opt = document.createElement('option');\n        opt.value = k; opt.textContent = k;\n        if (k === box.kind) opt.selected = true;\n        sel.appendChild(opt);\n      });\n      sel.addEventListener('change', () => {\n        current_box.kind = sel.value;\n        show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n        save();\n      });\n      return sel;\n    })()));\n\n    // ref: editable text input + browse button to populate via file browser\n    const ref_wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    ref_wrap.style.cssText = 'display:flex;gap:4px;align-items:center;';\n    const ref_inp = document.createElement('input');\n    ref_inp.type  = 'text';\n    ref_inp.value = box.ref || '';\n    ref_inp.style.flex = '1';\n    ref_inp.style.minWidth = '0';\n    ref_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { current_box.ref = ref_inp.value; save(); });\n    const browse_btn = document.createElement('button');\n    browse_btn.className   = 'toolbar-btn';\n    browse_btn.textContent = 'browse';\n    browse_btn.style.whiteSpace = 'nowrap';\n    browse_btn.onclick = open_browser;\n    ref_wrap.appendChild(ref_inp);\n    ref_wrap.appendChild(browse_btn);\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('ref', ref_wrap));\n\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('fn', mk_readonly(box.fn)));\n\n    // inputs: read-only names from parsing, editable literal values\n    const in_sec = document.createElement('div');\n    in_sec.className   = 'section-label';\n    in_sec.textContent = 'inputs';\n    fields.appendChild(in_sec);\n    fields.appendChild(mk_port_display(box.inputs));\n\n    // output: single wire; optional comparator splits into lt/eq/gt\n    const out_sec = document.createElement('div');\n    out_sec.className   = 'section-label';\n    out_sec.textContent = 'output';\n    fields.appendChild(out_sec);\n\n    const cmp_row = document.createElement('div');\n    cmp_row.style.cssText = 'display:flex;gap:6px;align-items:center;margin-bottom:6px;';\n\n    const has_cmp = box.comparand !== undefined && box.comparand !== '';\n    const cmp_btn = document.createElement('button');\n    cmp_btn.className   = 'toolbar-btn';\n    cmp_btn.textContent = has_cmp ? 'comparing ×' : 'compare';\n    cmp_btn.onclick = () => {\n      if (current_box.comparand !== undefined && current_box.comparand !== '') {\n        delete current_box.comparand;\n      } else {\n        current_box.comparand = '0';\n      }\n      save().then(() => show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb));\n    };\n    cmp_row.appendChild(cmp_btn);\n\n    if (has_cmp) {\n      const cmp_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      cmp_inp.type        = 'text';\n      cmp_inp.value       = box.comparand || '';\n      cmp_inp.placeholder = 'number';\n      cmp_inp.style.cssText = 'flex:1;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n      cmp_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { current_box.comparand = cmp_inp.value; save(); });\n      cmp_row.appendChild(cmp_inp);\n    }\n\n    fields.appendChild(cmp_row);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { show, hide };\n})();\n",
